# Mendari vision audit: full evidence

Companion to [`vision-audit.md`](vision-audit.md). Audited commit `e55ed48c304ad26f110ad9f101be827358c674f0`. Every audited element in full, under the same IDs as the report: what the plan says, the current state, every evidence entry, and the recommendation. Then every plan defect and every opportunity the auditors recorded. Paths are relative to the repository root at the audited commit; `$ command -> output` lines were run in the audit worktree or a scratch directory outside it.

## Vision principles and the open/proprietary split

### P1.1: Partial (verified); severity high; stage 3; effort L (1-2 weeks)

**Plan says.** Every pack is scored in four configurations: Mendari alone, + Jev, + LLM, + Jev + LLM (p.2; method in A9, p.17)

**Current state.** A free-form provider leaderboard exists (one row per configuration per dataset) and all five packs ship evals/leaderboard.json: 166 rows in total. Re-classified by walking each row's variant tree in the pack manifest: 22 offline, 30 with Jev, 114 with an LLM, 0 with both. Every dataset of every pack has the first three arms; no pack has the fourth. No variant in any pack combines Jev and an LLM (variants are rules, jev, llm, rules_and_jev, rules_and_llm, plus one naive_bayes-then-jev cascade). ai-guard, clinical-trial-prescreener and prior-auth-preflight have one remote slot, so they cannot express the fourth arm at all. patient-inbox-router and referral-router have two remote slots, so a mixed run (for example safety_screen=rules_and_jev with router=llm) could be typed by hand today, but none was run and nothing treats it as an arm. The code has no concept of an arm: `mendari leaderboard --run slot=variant` evaluates exactly the configurations the caller lists and merges them into the existing file; nothing searches variants within an arm or reports a best one. evals/benchmark.json is the offline arm only, and scripts/build-reference-pack.sh regenerates only that. Remote rows were measured on 100-case heads of the 300-600 case sets and on 24-38 case hand-written sets (largest critical-label count in any leaderboard dataset: 28; the inbox `test` head has 2 urgent cases). Four of five leaderboards hold rows from older pack versions: trial and prior-auth are entirely 0.1.0 (packs are 0.1.2), ai-guard mixes 0.1.1 and 0.1.2, referral mixes 0.1.0 and 0.1.1; only inbox is all current (0.3.0). Ranking differs by surface: the Decision Card and the Hub sort by accuracy, the dashboard by lowest critical-label detection rate, then accuracy, then cost; none matches A9's order.

**Evidence.**

- $ python (each leaderboard row classified by the remote provider types in its variant tree, composite members included) -> ai-guard 34 rows {offline 4, jev 6, llm 24}; trial 34 {4, 6, 24}; inbox 28 {6, 4, 18}; prior-auth 34 {4, 6, 24}; referral 36 {4, 8, 24}; total 166 {offline 22, jev 30, llm 114}; rows with both jev and llm: 0; every dataset has all three arms
- $ python (packs/*/pack.yaml provider variants) -> remote slots: ai-guard [screen], trial [notes], prior-auth [notes], inbox [safety_screen, router], referral [specialty_reader, triage_screen]; variants combining jev and llm: none in any pack
- src/mendari/evals/leaderboard.py:42-75 - a row is built from one report; no arm field, no grouping by arm
- src/mendari/evals/leaderboard.py:85-92 - build() merges new rows into existing rows keyed by (config, dataset); rows from earlier pack versions are kept
- src/mendari/evals/leaderboard.py:153 - `ranked = sorted(rows, key=lambda item: -(item["accuracy"] or 0.0))` (card table ranks by accuracy)
- src/mendari/dashboard/leaderboard.js:14-16 - safetyScore is the minimum detected/n over critical labels; safetyFirst sorts by it, then accuracy, then cost; :32 says so on screen
- hub/app/packs/[namespace]/[name]/page.tsx:100-102 - 'ranked by accuracy'; rows sorted by accuracy
- src/mendari/cli.py:271-299 - cmd_leaderboard evaluates only the --run configurations given and merges into the existing file
- src/mendari/server/app.py:259, 876 - `REMOTE_EVAL_LIMIT = 200` caps a hosted evaluation at 200 cases
- $ python (leaderboard pack_version per row against manifest version) -> ai-guard {0.1.2: 16, 0.1.1: 18}, manifest 0.1.2; trial {0.1.0: 34}, manifest 0.1.2; prior-auth {0.1.0: 34}, manifest 0.1.2; referral {0.1.0: 19, 0.1.1: 17}, manifest 0.1.1; inbox {0.3.0: 28}, manifest 0.3.0
- $ python (largest critical-label n per leaderboard dataset) -> inbox red_flags 28, red_flags_holdout 20, test 2; prior-auth 2-7; trial 4-12; referral 12-22; ai-guard 9-26; every remote row has n of 24-38 or 100
- scripts/build-reference-pack.sh:11, 17, 24, 30, 36 - only `mendari eval --dataset test` with the default (offline) providers is regenerated; the leaderboard never is
- tests/test_leaderboard.py::test_rows_merge_by_configuration_and_dataset, ::test_cli_runs_configurations_and_merges - pass ($ pytest tests/test_leaderboard.py tests/test_share.py tests/test_public_tree.py -> 12 passed, 1 skipped)

**Recommendation.** Make the arm a first-class concept before A9's statistics: derive the arm of every configuration from the manifest (the set of remote provider types in its variant trees), add a combined variant to each remote slot (for example any_of[rules, jev, llm]) or a deployment-level composition so every pack can express arm 4, and add a `mendari scoreboard` runner that executes all four arms on the same cases and stores per-case predictions. Drop or grey every row that was not measured on the current pack digest. Use one ranking function for the card, the dashboard and the Hub.

### P1.2: Contradicts the plan (verified); severity medium; stage 3; effort S (<1 day)

**Plan says.** Mendari has no preferred model provider (p.2)

**Current state.** Neutral in most of the design, with one vendor default written into product code. Neutral: every pack defaults to offline variants (rules, naive_bayes, criteria, dosing); no pack pins a model; automation_requires in three packs names rules_and_jev and rules_and_llm side by side; default daily limits are equal (500 and 500); the llm provider speaks one wire protocol (OpenAI-compatible chat completions with a strict JSON schema), so a local server works through LLM_BASE_URL. Not neutral: an `llm` variant with nothing configured calls `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` through the Vercel AI Gateway (both constants in code; a test pins the model; on a Vercel deployment the credential is automatic, so this path runs with no configuration), whereas Jev refuses to run without JEV_MODEL and JEV_API_URL. The package hard-depends on one hosting vendor's credential library (vercel-oidc). Jev, one company's product (TypeSafe), is the only vendor with its own provider type, its own health block, its own `/api/providers/jev/models` route and a built-in list price (the published price of jev-1.13.0, used as the default for whichever Jev model answers; a pack variant may override it). The dashboard prettifies only `claude-*` and `jev-*` model names. The inbox pack ships a Jev-only cascade with no LLM equivalent. The provider registry is a fixed dict of ten classes, so another vendor cannot add an adapter without a change to core. Models named in the committed comparisons: jev-1.13.0, two Anthropic models and one open-weight model.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/providers/llm.py:49-50 - `GATEWAY_URL = "https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1"`, `DEFAULT_MODEL = "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5"`
- src/mendari/providers/llm.py:114 - `model = self.settings.model or os.environ.get(MODEL_ENV, "").strip() or DEFAULT_MODEL`; :381 - deployment_info reports the same default
- $ python (in-process app, no provider variables set) GET /api/health -> llm: {endpoint: ai-gateway.vercel.sh, credentials: vercel-oidc, default_model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5}; jev: {credentials: None, endpoint_configured: False, model: None}
- src/mendari/providers/jev.py:113-119 - no model or no endpoint -> ProviderError('not_configured') (no vendor default on the Jev side)
- src/mendari/providers/jev.py:49-51, 69 - `PRICE_PER_1K_INPUT_TOKENS_USD = 0.000042` ('Published price of jev-1.13.0 ... A variant can override it') is the default of `cost_per_1k_input_tokens_usd`
- pyproject.toml:25 - `"vercel-oidc>=0.9"` in the core dependencies; src/mendari/providers/credentials.py:30-48 - keys come from an environment variable or a Vercel Connect connector
- src/mendari/providers/__init__.py:19-33 - PROVIDER_TYPES is a fixed dict of ten classes; no plugin entry point
- src/mendari/server/app.py:619-625 - health reports a `jev` block; :646-653 - `/api/providers/jev/models`; no equivalent route per LLM vendor
- src/mendari/dashboard/pack.js:121-127 - modelText special-cases `claude-...` and `jev-...`
- packs/patient-inbox-router/pack.yaml:141 - comment 'LLM_MODEL; default Claude Sonnet 5'; the router's only composite is `cascade` (naive_bayes then jev)
- tests/test_llm.py::test_request_is_structured_minimal_and_default_model (line 117 asserts body['model'] == 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-5'), ::test_local_openai_compatible_servers, ::test_deployment_info_reads_the_fixed_variables - pass (8 selected tests passed)
- src/mendari/settings.py:13-14 - DEFAULT_JEV_DAILY_LIMIT = 500, DEFAULT_LLM_DAILY_LIMIT = 500
- packs/ai-guard/policy.yaml:18-19, packs/prior-auth-preflight/policy.yaml:23-24, packs/referral-router/policy.yaml:22-23 - automation_requires lists [rules_and_jev, rules_and_llm]
- $ python (models named in leaderboard rows) -> jev-1.13.0, anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5, anthropic/claude-sonnet-5, openai/gpt-oss-120b
- In flight, not audited: `git log --oneline HEAD..claude/inbox-automation-gate` -> '899cd468 Inbox automation gate, and Mendari + Jev wherever Jev is set up', 'ef15e750 Review fixes: Jev defaults fill only unchosen slots, fall back when Jev cannot answer' (by title, this would make Jev a default where it is configured)

**Recommendation.** Remove DEFAULT_MODEL: an llm variant without LLM_MODEL should fail `not_configured`, as Jev does, and the test at tests/test_llm.py:117 should assert that. Keep the gateway as a documented option, not the silent default endpoint, and move vercel-oidc to an optional extra. Make the dashboard's model naming generic. Decide with the owner whether the in-flight 'Mendari + Jev wherever Jev is set up' default is compatible with this principle before it merges. Add the A9 disclosure field for the TypeSafe relationship.

### P2.1: Missing (verified); severity blocker; stage 2; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** Synthetic-only sandbox (p.2); A4.3 adds a blocking, audited acknowledgement before Try it (p.10); A7.3 a deterministic PHI detector on uploads (p.16)

**Current state.** Stated on screen, enforced nowhere. The dashboard shell carries a static badge 'sandbox · synthetic data only' and Try it says 'Synthetic records only; decisions here are recorded.' There is no acknowledgement, no PHI detection and no input check beyond the pack's JSON schema anywhere in src, on any entry point (dashboard, REST decide, FHIR, CDS Hooks). A message containing a name, date of birth, MRN, SSN and phone number was accepted, decided (HUMAN_REVIEW) and stored in clear: PHI mode defaults to `off` and all five packs set `audit.store_input: full`. The badge is static HTML, so it also shows on a deployment running PHI mode `encrypt` with real data, where it would be false. The sandbox generator tags every FHIR resource it writes as synthetic, but nothing checks for the tag. The acknowledgement (A4.3) gates stage 2; the PHI detector on uploads (A7.3) is a stage-4 item.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/dashboard/index.html:60 - `<span class="badge tag">sandbox<span class="tag-detail"> · synthetic data only</span></span>` (static)
- src/mendari/dashboard/try.js:36, 120 - 'Synthetic records only; decisions here are recorded.' / 'Synthetic messages only; decisions here are recorded.' (text, no gate; no confirm or acknowledgement in the file)
- $ git grep -n -i -E 'acknowledg|i understand|synthetic.only|is_synthetic|phi.?detect|mrn|ssn|date of birth|de-?identif' -- src/mendari (vendor and FHIR schema data excluded) -> no enforcement code; the only hits for the sandbox tag are in src/mendari/sandbox and one terminology constant
- src/mendari/sandbox/fhir_records.py:22 - SANDBOX_TAG is written on generated resources (:60, :174); no reader checks it on input
- src/mendari/core/phi.py:141 - `mode = os.environ.get("MENDARI_PHI_MODE", "").strip().lower() or "off"`
- packs/ai-guard/pack.yaml:272, packs/clinical-trial-prescreener/pack.yaml:327, packs/patient-inbox-router/pack.yaml:214, packs/prior-auth-preflight/pack.yaml:284, packs/referral-router/pack.yaml:270 - `store_input: full`
- $ python notices.py (in-process app on a scratch SQLite database; inbox example with body 'John Q. Example, DOB ..., MRN 00123456, SSN ..., phone ...') -> 'decide status 200 | outcome: HUMAN_REVIEW | recommendation: medical_assistant'; 'audit read status 200 | stored in clear: True'; health phi_mode: off
- $ python notices.py GET / -> of the notice phrases, only 'synthetic data only' is present

**Recommendation.** Build A4.3 as specified (blocking acknowledgement, chained per user and per notice version). Make the badge follow a deployment data-policy setting instead of static HTML. For a cheap, deterministic check on the hosted sandbox, require the existing sandbox tag (src/mendari/sandbox/fhir_records.py:22) on FHIR and CDS Hooks inputs and refuse untagged resources; add the deterministic PHI detector (A7.3) as a warning on Try it and the REST decide route before it becomes a hard reject on uploads.

### P2.2: Contradicts the plan (verified); severity blocker; stage 4; effort S (<1 day)

**Plan says.** Sites share metrics only (p.2); A11.2: no case content, no identifiers, no free text, and a schema test rejects any extra field; A11.3: suppress any cell under 10 (p.20)

**Current state.** `mendari eval --share SITE` and the registry's report endpoint exist, and both pass the report through `shareable()`. That filter drops `misclassified`, the report id and the dataset's name and hash, and removes subgroup cells and calibration bins under 10. But it copies `decisions` and `policy` whole. `decisions.critical[*].missed_ids` is a list of case ids, so the id of every missed critical case leaves the site and is stored in the registry's database. On the committed benchmarks that is 62 ids for ai-guard and 2 for the trial pack. With a site's own data those ids can be encounter or record numbers. `policy.governance_override` goes out as it is too: the approver's name and a free-text reference. Small cells are not suppressed outside subgroups and calibration bins: critical-label counts (n=6 survives), the confusion matrix and per-label supports are sent as they are. There is no payload schema, so extra fields are not rejected. The registry's public reports endpoint returns only seven summary numbers per site, so the ids are held server-side, not displayed. The existing test checks only ids from `misclassified` on the referral benchmark, which has no missed critical case, so it passes without exercising the leak. A site is a free-text name sent with any publisher token; there is no site key or signature (A11.1 not built). Only the SQLite backend of the registry test ran here; the Postgres variant was skipped.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/evals/share.py:17-28 - `_KEPT` includes "policy" and "decisions"; :32 copies kept keys verbatim; MIN_GROUP (:16) is applied only at :38 (calibration bins) and :45 (subgroup cells)
- src/mendari/evals/harness.py:180-184 - each critical item carries `missed_ids: [r["id"] ...]`
- $ python (shareable() on each committed benchmark) -> ai-guard: 62 case ids shared (unsafe_advice=yes, ids of the form guard-NNNN); clinical-trial-prescreener: 2 ids shared (one of them also listed in misclassified), critical cell with n=6 (note_pancreatitis) shared; inbox, prior-auth, referral: 0 ids; shared question keys include `confusion` and `per_label`
- $ python (shareable() on a report with a governance override) -> governance_override shared verbatim: {approved_by: ..., reference: ..., allow_auto: True}
- src/mendari/core/policy.py:25-37 - GovernanceOverride holds `approved_by` and `reference` (free text); harness.py:209 puts it in the report
- tests/test_share.py:15-21 - test_case_ids_and_dataset_identity_stay_home checks only `BENCHMARK["misclassified"]` ids on the referral-router benchmark
- src/mendari/hub/client.py:163-171 - share_report posts `shareable(report)`; src/mendari/hub/registry.py:302, 316 - the registry applies the same filter and stores the whole result; :321-330 - reports() returns only summary(); src/mendari/evals/share.py:52-65 - the seven summary fields
- src/mendari/hub/registry.py:468-470 - ReportRequest: `site` is a pattern-checked string, `report` is any dict; :609-610 - 'Any publisher token may submit; the site name is the site's choice'
- hub/app/packs/[namespace]/[name]/page.tsx:53 - Hub caption 'metrics only; no cases leave a site'; :69 - invites `mendari eval ... --share "Your site"`
- tests/test_hub_client.py::test_eval_share_sends_the_metrics, tests/test_registry.py::test_sites_share_metrics_and_compare_with_the_benchmark[sqlite] - pass; the Postgres parametrisation was skipped (no MENDARI_TEST_DATABASE_URL)

**Recommendation.** Fix now, ahead of A11's stage: `--share` already ships, and the registry and Hub that receive and invite these reports go live at stage 4. Replace the copy-through with a strict allow-list schema (pydantic, extra=forbid) of counts and rates only, drop missed_ids and the governance override's names and text, apply the minimum cell size to critical counts, confusion matrices and per-label supports, and add a regression test built on a report that has missed critical ids (the ai-guard benchmark has 62). Then add site keys and signatures (A11.1).

### P2.3: Done (verified); severity none; stage n/a; effort S (<1 day)

**Plan says.** Real-world evidence comes from sites running evaluations on their own data (p.2)

**Current state.** A site can evaluate any pack on its own labelled JSONL file, offline and inside its own environment, and compare the result with the pack's published benchmark: `mendari eval <pack> --dataset <file>` accepts a path, writes a report that holds ids but no case text, and reports degradation against the benchmark by subgroup and label. Run here on the shipped local-site example. Nothing leaves the machine unless `--share` is passed (see P2.2 for what that sends).

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/evals/harness.py:93-101 - resolve_dataset takes a pack dataset name or a path to a JSONL file
- src/mendari/cli.py:132-176 - cmd_eval evaluates, compares with the benchmark, and shares only when --share is given
- $ mendari eval mendari/patient-inbox-router --dataset datasets/local-site-example.jsonl --out <scratch>/local.json (run from the scratch directory, no provider variables) -> 'Dataset local-site-example (n=400) ... Destination accuracy 93.2% ... Critical urgency=urgent 18/18 detected, 0 automated ... Performance degradation detected (-6.1 pts overall; tolerance 3.0)'
- tests/test_evals.py::test_local_validation_localises_degradation, tests/test_cli.py::test_eval_fails_on_degradation_when_asked - pass

**Recommendation.** None for the local run itself. The sharing half is P2.2; signed site results and pooling are A11.

### P3.1: Partial (verified); severity high; stage 3; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** Grades are scoped and versioned: each grade names the pack, dataset and model versions it applies to (p.2); A9: record the exact configuration and every model version per run (p.17)

**Current state.** Evaluation reports are well scoped; everything derived from the leaderboard is not. An evaluation report (and each pack's evals/benchmark.json) names pack id, version and digest, dataset name, SHA-256 and n, and each slot's variant, type and model or local fingerprint. All five committed benchmarks carry the current pack digest and dataset hash, and a fresh offline run reproduced each of the five exactly (ignoring id, time and latency). All five committed Decision Cards equal a fresh render. The card names the version, the full digest, and the last benchmark's date, dataset, n and hash prefix. Gaps: (1) leaderboard rows keep only pack_version (no digest), dataset name and n (no hash, and no mark that n=100 is a head of a 300-600 case file); the rendered tables in the card, the dashboard and the Hub show no pack version at all, so the 0.1.2 trial and prior-auth cards present provider comparisons measured on 0.1.0 and nothing in the tables says so. (2) Model versions in reports and leaderboard rows are the requested ids, not the versions that answered. Jev stamps the model that answered on each answer, so a Jev decision record carries it; LLM answers record the requested alias; both providers also put requested and effective model in `ProviderOutput.extra`, which no code reads; the evaluation report takes its model from the configured provider info. (3) Nothing checks that a benchmark or a leaderboard row belongs to the current digest when a card is rendered, and CI leaves benchmark.json and DECISION_CARD.md out of its regeneration diff. (4) The registry's summary shows the benchmark's dataset name, n and accuracy without hash, date or models. (5) The terminal report prints pack, version and digest prefix but no model and no dataset hash. (6) No staleness marker exists.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/evals/harness.py:201-216 - report carries pack id/version/digest, providers variant/type/model (from decision.provider_info), dataset name/sha256/n/limit; :40 - the sha256 is of the whole file even when only a head is used
- $ python det.py (fresh offline run of `test` for each of the five packs) -> for all five: 'digest match: True | dataset sha match: True | fresh == committed (ignoring id, created_at, latency_ms): True'
- $ python (render_card(pack) against the committed DECISION_CARD.md) -> equal for all five packs; 'provider-comparison section mentions a pack version: False' for all five
- src/mendari/core/card.py:75 - card prints `Pack digest`; :263-268 - 'Last validation | <date> on `<dataset>` (n=..., sha256 `<12 hex>...`)'
- src/mendari/evals/leaderboard.py:50-54 - a row keeps dataset name, n, report_id, created_at, pack_version; no digest, no sha256, no limit
- src/mendari/evals/leaderboard.py:149-161 - rendered table columns: Configuration, Accuracy, Macro-F1, ECE, AUTO, False automation, Critical detected, p50 latency, Cost, Errors (no pack version)
- packs/clinical-trial-prescreener/DECISION_CARD.md:3 - version 0.1.2; :238 - 'Provider comparison'; :383 - only the version history says 'measured on 0.1.0'
- src/mendari/providers/jev.py:161 - extra = {requested_model, effective_model}; :171, 180 - `answered_by = replace(provider.info, model=effective)` is stamped on each Jev answer
- src/mendari/providers/llm.py:202-204 - extra = {requested_model, effective_model when the response names one}; answers are made with the configured provider info (base.py make_answer, `provider=self.info`)
- $ git grep -n -w extra -- src/mendari (python) -> ProviderOutput.extra is declared at providers/base.py:56 and written in jev.py and llm.py; read nowhere
- src/mendari/core/card.py:39-54 - read_benchmark validates shape only; no comparison of report['pack']['digest'] with pack.digest
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:79 - `git diff --exit-code -- packs datasets ':!packs/*/evals/benchmark.json' ':!packs/*/DECISION_CARD.md'`
- src/mendari/hub/registry.py:392-399 - registry benchmark summary is dataset name, n, accuracy
- src/mendari/evals/render.py:23-27 - terminal report header: pack id, version, digest prefix, slot=variant, dataset name and n

**Recommendation.** Put the digest, dataset hash, limit and the set of effective model versions on every leaderboard row; have the LLM provider stamp the answering model on its answers as Jev does, and carry the set of answering models into the evaluation report. Have the card, the dashboard and the Hub show only rows for the current digest (older ones under 'earlier versions'), and make `mendari validate` or CI fail when a card would show rows from another digest. Add the 30-day and version-change staleness rule from A9.

### P3.2: Partial (verified); severity high; stage 3; effort S (<1 day)

**Plan says.** A grade is an engineering evaluation, not clinical validation (p.2); A9: each grade carries that scope statement (p.18); Part B stage 3: remove anything in public docs that implies clinical validity (p.12)

**Current state.** No output carries that statement or the words 'engineering evaluation'. The nearest equivalents are on the Decision Card only: the footer ('It is not evidence of performance at your site; run local validation first') and the provider-comparison note ('Synthetic and hand-written data: compare configurations with each other, not with performance at a real site'). Both are about site performance, not about clinical validation. The card works against the principle in its headings: the synthetic benchmark sits under '## Validation' and 'Last validation', in all five committed cards. Evaluation reports, benchmark.json, leaderboard.json, the terminal report, the registry description and the Hub page carry no scope statement at all.

**Evidence.**

- $ git grep -n -i -E 'engineering evaluation|clinical validation' -- . (vendor, lock files, data, notes, tasks excluded) -> no hits
- src/mendari/core/card.py:148 - `## Validation`; :266 - 'Last validation'; :159-161 - comparison caveat; :182-183 - footer
- $ python (each committed DECISION_CARD.md, lower-cased) -> for all five: 'engineering evaluation': False, 'clinical validation': False, 'not a medical device': False, 'research preview': False, 'not evidence of performance at your site': True, '## validation': True, 'last validation': True
- src/mendari/evals/render.py:16-67 - terminal report prints pack, providers, dataset and metrics; no statement
- hub/app/packs/[namespace]/[name]/page.tsx:37 - 'Benchmark accuracy' fact with no scope statement; :73-77 - renders the card's Markdown
- tests/test_evals.py::test_decision_card_renders - asserts the '## Validation' heading and that the digest is in the card (lines 145, 149); no test asserts a scope statement

**Recommendation.** Add a `scope` object to mendari.eval and mendari.leaderboard (pack digest, dataset name and hash, model versions, date, the sentence 'engineering evaluation, not clinical validation') and render it at the top of the card, the dashboard leaderboard, the terminal report and the Hub page. Rename the card's 'Validation' section to 'Engineering evaluation' and 'Last validation' to 'Last evaluation'. Test for the sentence on each surface.

### P4: Partial (verified); severity blocker; stage 2; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** Research preview, not a medical device, until a regulatory review says otherwise (p.2); A4.2: persistent notice on every dashboard page including 'Not for emergencies: patients should call 911' (p.10)

**Current state.** In product code the statement appears in two places only: the developer landing page at /docs (a warning callout and the footer) and the OpenAPI description. The dashboard application itself says only 'sandbox · synthetic data only'. Decision Cards, CDS Hooks cards (source label is 'Mendari · <pack> <version>'), CDS discovery, the FHIR capability statement, the API pack endpoints, CLI output, the Hub site (tag 'synthetic data only') and the mendari.co page ('Healthcare decisions you can test, trust and share. ... Coming soon') do not say it. There is no 911 or emergency notice on any surface; the only mention of 911 in served content is an out-of-scope line in the inbox pack's own card ('Portals must keep telling patients to call 911'), which is a statement about portals, not a notice. No test asserts any of these notices. README, docs/index.md and SECURITY.md say it, but those are documents.

**Evidence.**

### P5.2: Partial (verified); severity medium; stage 3; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** Every build uses real deterministic computation and real statistics, seeded where random (p.2, shared header p.6)

**Current state.** The metrics that exist are real and deterministic: accuracy, per-label precision, recall and F1, macro-F1, confusion matrix, ECE over 10 equal-width bins, multi-class Brier, threshold sweep, percentiles, critical-label detection, subgroup rates, and a population stability index for drift monitoring. Two runs on the same inputs differ only in the report id and measured latency. What the plan means by statistics does not exist yet: there is no confidence interval, bootstrap, significance test, multiple-comparison adjustment or agreement statistic anywhere in src, and scipy and statsmodels are not dependencies. Reports are not byte-reproducible (random uuid, wall-clock timestamp, measured latency), which is why CI leaves benchmark.json and the card out of its byte-identical check. ECE binning is equal-width where A9 specifies equal-mass.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/evals/metrics.py:14, 49-77, 80, 90, 106 - classification, calibration ('equal-width confidence bins'), brier, percentiles, threshold_sweep
- src/mendari/evals/monitoring.py:8-12, 52 - PSI drift against the benchmark's confidence bins
- $ git grep -n -i -E 'clopper|pearson|bootstrap|mcnemar|holm|kappa|wilson|confidence interval|binom|chi-square|resampl|p-value' -- src python, scripts -> no hits
- $ grep -n -i -E 'scipy|statsmodels|numpy|hypothesis|re2|scikit' pyproject.toml -> no hits
- src/mendari/evals/harness.py:199-200 - `"id": str(uuid.uuid4())`, `"created_at": datetime.now(UTC)...`
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:79 - the byte-identical check excludes packs/*/evals/benchmark.json and packs/*/DECISION_CARD.md
- tests/test_evals.py::test_classification_metrics, ::test_expected_calibration_error, ::test_brier_score, ::test_threshold_sweep, ::test_parallel_evaluation_matches_sequential - pass
- $ python det.py -> two runs differ in: id, latency_ms.max, latency_ms.mean, latency_ms.p50, latency_ms.p95

**Recommendation.** Add a pure statistics module (Clopper-Pearson, percentile bootstrap with a fixed seed, exact McNemar, Holm) tested against scipy and statsmodels as dev-only references, and store per-case predictions (ids, labels, probabilities; no text) so every statistic can be recomputed byte-for-byte without calling a paid provider again. Separate the deterministic part of a report (metrics) from the run envelope (id, time, latency) so the first can be hashed and signed, and include it in the CI reproducibility check.

## The licensing decision (Apache-2.0)

**Current state.** One wheel holds the engine, CLI and library. It declares Apache-2.0 as a PEP 639 expression and carries the licence file; the image label and README say the same. This is the declaration only: nothing has been published yet.

- pyproject.toml:69 - /LICENSE is in the sdist include list

- Dockerfile:21 - COPY README.md LICENSE ./ ; Dockerfile:44 - org.opencontainers.image.licenses='Apache-2.0'
- README.md:983-985 - License section: Apache-2.0
- scripts/check_sdist.py:42-45 with .github/workflows/ci.yml:282-283 and .github/workflows/release.yml:29-31 - the built sdist fails the check if a tracked LICENSE is missing from it
- tests/test_packaging.py::test_the_sdist_includes_exactly_the_build_inputs - pins the include list (LICENSE included) to the allow-list

**Recommendation.** Nothing to build. Keep as is.

### A1.4-NOTICE: Missing (verified); severity blocker; stage 3; effort S (<1 day)

**Plan says.** Add NOTICE (A1 step 4, p.7)

**Current state.** No NOTICE file exists at the root and none ever existed on this branch. The only NOTICE in the tree is swagger-ui's own, next to the vendored bundle. The sdist allow-list would reject a root NOTICE today. Legal weight by itself is small (Apache-2.0 does not oblige a licensor to ship one), but it is a named A1 deliverable in the stage 3 gate and the natural place for the LOINC notice and third-party attributions that are also missing.

**Evidence.**

- $ git ls-files | grep -i -E 'notice|trademark|license|copying|authors' -> LICENSE, src/mendari/dashboard/LICENSE-lucide.txt and three files under src/mendari/dashboard/vendor/swagger-ui/5.33.0/ (LICENSE, NOTICE, swagger-ui-bundle.js.LICENSE.txt)
- $ git log --oneline HEAD -- NOTICE NOTICE.md NOTICE.txt -> (empty)
- scripts/check_sdist.py:23 - INCLUDED = {src, packs, datasets, README.md, LICENSE, pyproject.toml}; line 40-41 reports any other top-level entry as 'not part of a source build'
- pyproject.toml:64-71 - sdist include has no /NOTICE
- Dockerfile:21 - copies README.md and LICENSE only
- $ TestClient GET /NOTICE and /LICENSE on a scratch database -> 404 both (the server serves only the vendored notices under /static)

**Recommendation.** Create NOTICE with the project name, a copyright line, and third-party attributions (swagger-ui/SmartBear, Lucide ISC and Feather MIT, HL7 FHIR R4 schema and US Core 6.1.0 as sources, the LOINC notice, CPT and SNOMED CT notices only if that content stays). Add /NOTICE to the pyproject sdist include, to INCLUDED in scripts/check_sdist.py, to the names in tests/test_packaging.py and to the Dockerfile COPY. Hatchling 1.32.4 picks up a root NOTICE as a licence file by default, so check the built wheel's dist-info/licenses rather than assume. The copyright holder depends on the owner's legal-entity choice; an entity-neutral line ('The Mendari Authors') works until then.

### LIC.cpt: Unknown (verified); severity high; stage 3; effort M (1-3 days)

**Current state.** Facts verified, law unknown. No HCPCS, CDT, DRG, MedDRA or commercial criteria (MCG, InterQual) content was found.

**Current state.** The repository has no CLA and plans none. Today the question is moot in fact: every commit on this branch is by the owner (two identities) or Dependabot. What DCO-only allows later is a legal question. General reading, for counsel to confirm: contributions arrive under Apache-2.0 by the licence's own section 5 and by CONTRIBUTING.md; that licence is permissive and sublicensable, so the owner can run a proprietary hosted service, ship closed derivative works and license later versions of the combined work on other terms, provided the Apache conditions (notices, attribution) are still met for contributors' code. What the owner cannot do without a CLA or assignment is drop those conditions, relicense contributors' code under terms the Apache licence does not allow, or withdraw the Apache grant on anything already published. A CLA mainly adds explicit ownership and patent representations made to the entity.

**Evidence.**

- CONTRIBUTING.md:92-93 - inbound = outbound, no agreement
- LICENSE:131-137 (section 5) - a contribution submitted for inclusion is under this licence unless stated otherwise; LICENSE:124-129 (section 4, last paragraph) - derivative works may carry additional or different terms if the licence's conditions are otherwise met; LICENSE:67-72 (section 2) - the copyright grant includes the right to sublicense
- $ git log --format='%an' HEAD | sort | uniq -c -> 120 Marc J Saint-jour, 63 Junebugg1214, 4 dependabot[bot] (187 commits)

**Recommendation.** Owner with counsel, before the first outside pull request is merged (the choice cannot be applied retroactively): confirm DCO-only is enough for the business model on p.1, or adopt a CLA for engine code while keeping DCO for community packs. Record the decision in an ADR and CONTRIBUTING.md.

### LIC.patent: Unknown (unknown); severity blocker; stage 2; effort owner; owner only

**Plan says.** Patent decision made with counsel before any public disclosure (Stage 1 gate, p.4; Part B, p.11 and p.12), alongside an Apache-2.0 release (p.1)

**Current state.** Not determinable from the repository. The licensing fact that bears on the decision: Apache-2.0 section 3 gives everyone who receives the code a royalty-free licence to the owner's patent claims that the owner's own contribution necessarily practises, so a patent on a method implemented in the open engine cannot be asserted against users or forks of that code. It stays assertable against independent implementations. A counsel memo recording the decision settles the item.

**Evidence.**

- LICENSE:74-88 - section 3, Grant of Patent License, with the termination-on-litigation clause
- $ git grep -n -i patent -- . ':!uv.lock' ':!LICENSE' ':!src/mendari/dashboard/vendor' ':!hub/package-lock.json' -> one hit inside the generated FHIR schema file (a resource description); no project statement about patents

**Recommendation.** Owner with a patent attorney. Tell the attorney the code will be Apache-2.0, which methods will be in the open release and which only in the closed trust layer (grading method, hidden-set rotation), so the filing question is asked about the right things.

**Unit notes.** Scope and method: skeptic pass over the licensing unit at commit e55ed48c304ad26f110ad9f101be827358c674f0, read-only, in the worktree only. Every Done, Contradicts, blocker and high item and every measurement was re-checked against the code; the rest were spot-checked. Commands that could write ran with their working directory, database and temp paths under the scratchpad (tmp/licensing/skeptic): a targeted pytest run of tests/test_vendor.py, tests/test_packaging.py and tests/test_public_tree.py (18 passed), `mendari validate` on three scratch copies of a fixture pack with altered licence values, a TestClient probe of the static notice files against a scratch SQLite database, and read-only Python tallies (importlib.metadata, uv.lock, hub/package-lock.json, the prior-auth data files). `git status --short` in the worktree printed nothing at the end; nothing was created or changed there. An ignored var/mendari.db (08:56, before this session) was already present and was not touched. What held up: the auditor's measurements reproduced exactly (LICENSE digest; 80 installed distributions and the 34/+2/+45/+25 lock closure; the npm tally of 476 packages; 275 first-party code files with no header; 1,256 rows, 12 codes and 1,916 CPT occurrences; the code-system URL counts; 187 commits, 4 sign-offs, 228 AI co-author trailers; `mendari validate` accepting any licence string; the static notice files served with the stated sizes). Headline after correction: the Apache-2.0 declaration itself is in good order (canonical LICENSE, correct package metadata, vendored swagger-ui and Lucide notices present and served, swagger-ui tested). Missing from A1 step 4 are NOTICE and the whole DCO mechanism (text, check, acceptance). The larger findings sit outside the plan's wording: AMA CPT codes inside a reference pack declared Apache-2.0; an LGPL-3.0-only required runtime dependency with no licence gate or SBOM; no trademark policy and no way to tell a Mendari grade from a publisher's own; no takedown path in the registry; and an open/proprietary boundary the plan never defines while the registry, Hub, leaderboard and site-report code already sit inside the Apache-2.0 wheel. Legal questions for counsel, which the repository cannot answer (all Unknown and owner_only): dependency-licence sign-off, DCO-only versus CLA, trademark clearance and filing, control of the names, badge rules, legal entity and assignment, employer IP, AI-assisted authorship, whether the Apache-2.0 LICENSE already in the tree governs partner access during the NDA phase, the patent decision in light of the Apache patent grant, the open/closed boundary, and provider terms on publishing benchmarks. The CPT item is Unknown as to law but its facts are verified and it has an engineering fix that removes the question. The licence readings given in LIC.dco-vs-cla, LIC.patent and LIC.private-phase are general readings for counsel to confirm, not legal advice. Limits of verification: 19 packages in uv.lock (18 from the docs group and the runtime-closure package httpx2-jsfetch) are not installed in this environment, so their licences were not read from metadata. No sdist, wheel or image was built (a build needs the network), so wheel and image contents are inferred from pyproject.toml, the Dockerfile and the installed editable metadata. The CC0 status of HL7's R4 schema and US Core, Lucide's current LICENSE text, and the AMA, LOINC, SNOMED and X12 licence positions are from those bodies' published terms as generally known, not fetched here. Whether the PyPI name is free and whether the DCO App is installed could not be checked offline. Stage assignments for Part B items follow the plan's page-11 to page-13 lists and the page-4 gates: the extracted text groups the stage headings, so the dependency-licence and names items are placed at stage 3 (first public distribution) although the plan lists them among Stage 1 preparation. Cross-references: LIC.open-4 (synthetic-example label) is the same requirement as A2 step 6 and the Stage 1 gate; LIC.takedown's mechanism is A10 step 3; count each once. Outside this unit but adjacent: the plan's data agreements for any de-identified real cases in hidden sets (p.12), for which the repository holds nothing to check because no hidden set exists. Regression tests a build session should add (kept from the auditor's list): a licence allow-list test over the locked runtime closure; an npm licence check over hub/package-lock.json; scripts/check_dco.py with scratch-repository tests (signed, unsigned, merge and bot commits); NOTICE in the sdist allow-list, the packaging test and the built wheel's dist-info/licenses; a test that the Lucide notice exists whenever a sprite does; a test that PackManifest and the registry refuse an empty or non-SPDX licence; a tree test that fails if the AMA CPT system URL or a 'CPT <5 digits>' label appears under packs/, datasets/ or src/mendari/sandbox once the codes are replaced; and, if any trust-layer code is kept private, a packaging test that its path never appears in the sdist, wheel or image. In flight, not audited (from `git log --oneline HEAD..<branch>` only): claude/community-packs has 7 commits, including c7f4caeb ('the contributor's guide, templates, ADR-0007 and the owner's steps (B7)') and c0c72bd8 ('community-check, the pack-check job and the community scaffold'), which by tasks/todo.md lines 70 and 85 are meant to add the DCO text to CONTRIBUTING and an Apache-2.0 manifest rule for community packs. claude/inbox-automation-gate (3 commits), feat/dashboard-tables (1) and claude/design-c (3) do not appear, by their titles, to touch licensing.

### TC4.owner-only: Unknown (inferred); severity medium; stage 2; effort L (1-2 weeks)

**Plan says.** Hosted platform 'Owner only' (p2)

**Current state.** Who can sign in to the hosted site is deployment configuration, deliberately scrubbed from the tree. The mechanism is verified: with a provider that has no roles (Google), roles come from an email-to-role map in an environment variable, so adding a person means editing the variable and redeploying; a signed-in person with no mapped role gets a 403. That map is a working stopgap for 3 to 5 partners, which is why the gap is rated medium; what it cannot do is put them in separate organizations (TC4.one-org). Evidence that would settle the claim: the hosted /api/health and /api/auth/me output, signed in.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/server/auth.py:402-408 - roles_from: with role claim `email`, a role is given only when email_verified is true
- src/mendari/server/auth.py:810-812 - no role -> AuthError 'your account has no Mendari role; ask an administrator', 403
- docs/deploying-with-phi.md:63-76 - Google example with MENDARI_OIDC_ROLE_CLAIM=email and a per-person map (lead)
- docs/security/review-packet.md:303 - production's settings were not checked while building (lead)

**Recommendation.** Settle with the hosted /api/health and /api/auth/me output signed in. Closing the gap is plan A6 (invitations replacing the env map).

### TC4.one-org: Partial (verified); severity high; stage 2; effort L (1-2 weeks)

**Plan says.** Hosted platform 'one shared organization'; blocks: 'No accounts or organizations' (p2)

**Current state.** Half right. Organization tenancy already exists in code: the organization comes from an OIDC claim (unset, or absent from the token: everyone is in `default`), every record is stamped with it, reads are filtered by it, and cross-organization isolation is tested for REST, FHIR, keys and SMART launches. What does not exist: users, organizations, memberships or invitations as data (no such tables), so an organization can only come from the identity provider's claim, and with a claimless provider such as Google every partner would share `default` with the owner's data. The local test run covers SQLite only; the Postgres variants of these tests are skipped without MENDARI_TEST_DATABASE_URL (they run in CI).

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/server/auth.py:218 - org_claim from MENDARI_OIDC_ORG_CLAIM; :813-815 - org = the claim's value or DEFAULT_ORG
- src/mendari/core/tenancy.py:17 - DEFAULT_ORG = 'default'; :33-41 - acting_for sets the org for the request
- $ scratch serve_check.py, sqlite_master -> tables api_keys, audit_events, capability_versions, decision_inputs, decisions, deployments, eval_reports, feedback, governance_approvals, notes, oauth_clients, oauth_tokens, org_usage, provider_usage, rate_limits, smart_sessions (no users, organizations, memberships or invitations)
- tests/test_auth.py::test_organizations_never_see_each_others_work (tests/test_auth.py:680)
- tests/test_fhir_routes.py::test_another_organization_reads_and_finds_nothing (tests/test_fhir_routes.py:338)
- $ pytest tests/test_auth.py -k 'organization or org or key' -> 22 passed
- $ git grep -n -i -E 'invitation|invite|membership' HEAD -- src -> no match

**Recommendation.** Write A6 as an extension of the existing tenancy (an invitations/memberships table that maps a verified email to organization and role, feeding Principal.org) rather than a new data model; keep the existing cross-organization tests as the base of A6's 'every route as two organizations' acceptance.

### TC5.secret: Done (verified); severity none; stage 4; effort S (<1 day)

**Plan says.** Pack safety 'Unsafe: a pack can choose which server secret is sent and to which URL' (p2)

**Current state.** Outdated: true at 0182417c (the Jev config took `api_key_env` from the pack), fixed by PR #127 after the plan was written. The eight `*_env` keys of jev and llm variants are refused at load (variants and composite members) and again in the provider; the variable names for endpoint, model and key are fixed constants; and the jev and llm config models forbid unknown keys, so a variant that names a URL or headers directly is refused too (re-checked with three scratch packs). The plan's A3 'reported exploit' regression test already exists. Still open under A3.1 (other unit): a pack may pin `model`, and for llm variants the pack's model wins over the deployment's LLM_MODEL (a cost lever, not an exfiltration path); the unknown-key refusal echoes the offending value in its message.

### TC5.regex: Missing (verified); severity blocker; stage 4; effort L (1-2 weeks)

**Plan says.** Pack safety 'Unsafe: ... regex patterns have no time limit' (p2)

**Current state.** Still true. PR #127 compiles every pack pattern at load (length and count caps, clean errors) but patterns still run on Python `re` with no time limit, as the module itself states. Reproduced independently: a pack with `(a+)+$` validates, and a 41-character input holds the process past a 15 s kill (23 characters: 1.3 s; 26 characters: 4.5 s). No linear-time engine, CPU budget, process isolation or fuzz test exists (re2, regex and hypothesis are not installed).

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/core/patterns.py:10-14 - '`re` has no time limit ... a pack's patterns can slow or stall the worker ... packs from others will run in an isolated process ... once uploads or a public registry exist'
- $ mendari validate evil-regex (scratch pack, rules pattern (a+)+$) -> rc=0 ok
- $ mendari decide evil-regex --text 'a'*N+'!' -> N=10 0.8 s, N=22 1.3 s, N=25 4.5 s, N=40 TIMEOUT after 15 s (killed)
- $ python -c importlib.util.find_spec for re2, regex, hypothesis -> None, None, None
- tests/test_patterns.py - 11 test functions (15 collected, all pass) on compile-at-load; none on run time

**Recommendation.** Must land before any untrusted pack runs on a shared deployment (plan stage 4, and before the todo's B9, see TC10.community). Specify the outcome (bounded wall time per decision, the worker survives, health stays green) and allow process isolation with a hard limit; RE2 as written would reject three shipped packs (see plan_defects).

### TC6.plaintext: Partial (verified); severity blocker; stage 2; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** Hosted patient-data handling: 'Inputs stored in plaintext' (p3)

**Current state.** True for the code default, unknown for the hosted site. PHI mode defaults to `off`; all five reference packs set `store_input: full` (also the spec default); in that combination the input is written in clear inside the hash-chained decision record. `hash` and `encrypt` (AES-256-GCM, keyed input hash, chained reads) exist and are tested, and the Kubernetes and on-prem templates set `encrypt`, but nothing makes them the default on the hosted (Vercel) entrypoint, which passes no PHI setting, and startup has no check that refuses `off` when sign-in is on. Reproduced locally: the input text is readable in the decisions table. Blocks hosted partner sign-in (the table's 'stage 2, hosted access'; the figure lists A5 in the gate into stage 3), not self-hosted stage 2.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/core/phi.py:141 - mode = MENDARI_PHI_MODE or 'off'
- src/mendari/core/audit.py:374-376 - keep = store_input == 'full' and mode != 'hash'; in_record = keep and mode == 'off'; record['input'] = inputs
- packs/patient-inbox-router/pack.yaml:214, packs/ai-guard/pack.yaml:272, packs/referral-router/pack.yaml:270, packs/prior-auth-preflight/pack.yaml:284, packs/clinical-trial-prescreener/pack.yaml:327 - store_input: full; src/mendari/core/spec.py:408 - default 'full'
- src/mendari/server/vercel.py:55-61 - create_app called with no PHI setting; src/mendari/server/app.py:325 - phi = phi_policy(), no check against sign-in
- deploy/kubernetes/mendari.yaml:27 and deploy/onprem/.env.example:20 - MENDARI_PHI_MODE encrypt (templates only)
- $ scratch serve_check.py -> health phi_mode: off; 'plaintext input in chained decision record: [True]'; decision_inputs rows: 0
- $ pytest tests/test_phi.py -> 9 passed (hash, encrypt, purge, chained reads)

**Recommendation.** A5.1. Simplest safe form: the server refuses to start with PHI mode `off` when sign-in is on and the public URL is not local, so the hosted site cannot fall back to plaintext by omission. The hosted mode itself needs the signed-in /api/health output to confirm.

### TC6.erase: Partial (verified); severity high; stage 2; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** Hosted patient-data handling: inputs 'can't be erased' (p3)

**Current state.** True in mode `off`: the input is part of the chained record and no command removes it. In `encrypt` mode inputs sit apart and `mendari phi purge` deletes those older than N days with the chain intact, but there is no per-decision erase, no scheduled purge on Vercel (no cron in vercel.json; the Kubernetes CronJob and the on-prem compose job schedule it), and `--days 0` is refused. Notes can be erased one by one in any mode.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/core/audit.py:1016-1029 - purge_inputs deletes only decision_inputs rows (the encrypted store) by age and chains 'input.purged'
- src/mendari/core/audit.py:835 - erase_note; src/mendari/cli.py:897-907 - mendari notes erase
- src/mendari/cli.py:885-887 - days = args.days or MENDARI_RETENTION_DAYS; days < 1 raises 'give --days or set MENDARI_RETENTION_DAYS'
- $ mendari phi purge --db decide.db --days 0 -> rc=1 'error: give --days or set MENDARI_RETENTION_DAYS'
- vercel.json:1-13 - no crons key; deploy/kubernetes/mendari.yaml:89-109 - CronJob running `mendari phi purge`; deploy/onprem/docker-compose.yml:36-49 - daily purge job
- tests/test_phi.py::test_retention_purges_inputs_and_keeps_the_chain

**Recommendation.** A5.2 and A5.5, plus a per-decision input erase mirroring erase_note (the plan does not ask for one, but 'erase' in A5's acceptance implies it).

### TC7.inbox-gap: Missing (verified); severity blocker; stage 2; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** p3: 'the inbox pack is risk level 0 with no automation_requires. A rules-only deployment AUTO-routed 7 of the 20 held-out emergencies it missed.'

**Current state.** Still true at e55ed48c, reproduced. The inbox pack is risk level 0 and has no `automation_requires` (three other packs use it). With the default offline providers (safety_screen=rules, router=naive_bayes), the 20 held-out emergencies split as: 4 flagged stat for nurse review; 9 sent to nurse review at routine priority; 7 AUTO-routed to the nurse queue at routine priority with no review step. So 16 are missed as emergencies and 7 of those are automated. The all-rules configuration (router=rules) automates none. The pack's own risk rationale says such messages 'are never auto-routed'. The same run reports 'false automation rate 0.0% (0 of 7)', because that metric counts only a wrong destination among AUTO decisions; the local-validation comparison does flag 'urgency=urgent cases automated: 7 of 20', but no gate runs on the held-out set. A fix is in flight on claude/inbox-automation-gate (2 commits, not audited).

**Evidence.**

- packs/patient-inbox-router/pack.yaml:13-21 - risk level 0; rationale 'messages that may describe an emergency are never auto-routed'
- $ git grep -n automation_requires HEAD -- packs -> ai-guard/policy.yaml:18, prior-auth-preflight/policy.yaml:23, referral-router/policy.yaml:22; nothing under packs/patient-inbox-router
- $ mendari eval mendari/patient-inbox-router --dataset red_flags_holdout -> 'Critical urgency=urgent 4/20 detected, 7 automated'; 'false automation rate 0.0% (0 of 7)'; 'urgency=urgent cases automated: 7 of 20'
- $ scratch auto7.py (Decision on each held-out emergency, default providers) -> 9 HUMAN_REVIEW nurse routine; 7 AUTO nurse routine; 4 HUMAN_REVIEW nurse stat
- packs/patient-inbox-router/evals/leaderboard.json:513 - 'auto_missed': 7 (safety_screen=rules, router=naive_bayes); packs/patient-inbox-router/DECISION_CARD.md:212 and :215 - '4/20 (7 automated)' and, for router=rules, '4/20 (0 automated)'
- src/mendari/evals/harness.py:143-148 and :226 - false automation = AUTO with a wrong primary label; :179 - auto_missed counts critical cases with outcome AUTO
- src/mendari/evals/gate.py:1-12 - the pull-request gate compares the benchmark dataset with main only
- $ git log --oneline HEAD..claude/inbox-automation-gate -> ef15e750, 899cd468 (in flight, not audited)

**Recommendation.** A4.1 before any design partner self-hosts: the default configuration is the unsafe one. Also correct the risk rationale text, and make the reference-pack CI job fail any shipped default with auto_missed > 0 on a bundled dataset.

## Stage gates and the owner checklist (Part B)

### B01: Partial (verified); severity high; stage 3; effort S (<1 day) build, then owner (counsel)

**Plan says.** Open-source the engine under Apache-2.0 at stage 3; counsel confirms every dependency's licence is compatible (p11)

**Current state.** Apache-2.0 is applied in the tree (LICENSE, pyproject). There is no NOTICE file, no third-party licence inventory and no licence check in CI. Three unconditional runtime dependencies (psycopg, psycopg-binary, psycopg-pool) are LGPL-3.0-only and ship inside the image; certifi is MPL-2.0. Bundled content the plan does not mention needs the same review: CPT codes in the prior-auth pack, SNOMED CT and LOINC codes in the trial and referral packs, HL7-derived schema files, vendored Swagger UI and Lucide. Counsel's confirmation cannot be seen from a repository.

**Evidence.**

- LICENSE:1-4 - Apache License 2.0 text; pyproject.toml:7 - license = "Apache-2.0"
- $ ls NOTICE* -> no matches found (re-run)
- $ importlib.metadata over .venv (80 distributions, re-run) -> psycopg, psycopg-binary, psycopg-pool = LGPL-3.0-only; certifi, pathspec, pytest-base-url = MPL-2.0; text-unidecode = Artistic/GPL (dev only)
- pyproject.toml:23-24 - psycopg[binary] and psycopg-pool are unconditional runtime dependencies
- packs/prior-auth-preflight/pack.yaml:82-84,104 - CPT codes (72148, 29880, 95810, 72100...) in a pack whose licence is Apache-2.0; no AMA notice in the tree
- $ git grep -l -i 'snomed\|loinc' -- packs -> clinical-trial-prescreener and referral-router files
- $ grep -n -i licen .github/workflows/*.yml -> no match (re-run)

**Recommendation.** Build: generate a third-party licence inventory from uv.lock and hub/package-lock.json, add NOTICE, add a CI job that fails on a licence outside an allow-list. Owner: give counsel the inventory plus the bundled-content list (CPT, SNOMED CT, LOINC, HL7 schema, US Core, Swagger UI, Lucide) and the LGPL psycopg question for the container image.

### B40: Partial (inferred); severity medium; stage 6; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** Ask EHR partners which decision-support source attributes they need under ONC's HTI-1 rule, and provide them from the Decision Cards (p13)

**Current state.** Measured against the 31 predictive-DSI source attributes of 45 CFR 170.315(b)(11)(iv)(B), listed from memory with no network access (check against the rule text): a Decision Card can supply 7 today, 6 in part, and 18 not at all. Supplied: output description, intended use, patient population, intended users, cautioned out-of-scope uses, known risks and limitations, validity on same-source test data. In part: developer (name, no contact), output type, intended decision-making role (risk level and automation row), demographic variables used as inputs (readable from the inputs table), fairness on same-source data (subgroup table), validity on data other than the training source (the provider comparison on hand-written hold-out sets, still synthetic). Absent: funding source, training-data inclusion and exclusion, demographic representativeness, relevance of training data, both fairness-process items, all four external-validation items, external fairness, outcome-evaluation references, all four ongoing-maintenance items, both update-schedule items. Packs with no trained model would fall under the shorter evidence-based list in (iv)(A) instead, where the card lacks the bibliographic citation and funding source. The card is Markdown only; the CDS Hooks card gives the EHR a label with no link to it.

**Recommendation.** Extend the spec's card with the missing attribute groups (developer contact, funding, training data, fairness, external validation, maintenance, update schedule), render them, serve them as structured JSON, and put the card's URL in the CDS card's source.url. **Recommendation.** As W2.clin-label and W2.clin-review.

**Unit notes.** Scope and method. Skeptic pass over the auditor's findings for unit partB-gates, audited commit e55ed48c only, read-only. Part B bullets are numbered B01-B42 in plan order (B09 split in three; B19 and B21 now carry their sub-bullets as B19.1-3 and B21.1-5). The text extraction of pages 11-13 put the stage headings at the top of each page, so which stage a bullet sits under is inferred from order and wording; the stage field follows the gate figure first and that inference second. Gate status rule: Done only if every prerequisite is evidenced; all five gates are Partial and none has a single fully evidenced prerequisite (0 of 6, 0 of 8, 0 of 7, 0 of 6, 0 of 6). Most important findings, after re-checking. (1) Stage 2 cannot open: the inbox router's default configuration still automates 7 of 20 held-out emergencies, reproduced by `mendari eval` and by a separate script; its Decision Card says emergencies are 'never auto-routed' on line 18 and shows '4/20 (7 automated)' on line 212. A fix is in flight on claude/inbox-automation-gate (2 commits, not audited). (2) No reference pack carries the synthetic-example label and none records a clinical reviewer; three packs disclose non-review in a bullet, the inbox router does not, and GOVERNANCE.md promises a sign-off none has. (3) Terms, privacy notice and acceptable-use policy do not exist in any form. (4) The only prepared external-review scope leaves the registry and Hub for later, so gate 3->4 is not covered. (5) The repo's own plan (tasks/todo.md, 4 Oct) makes the repository public earlier than the launch plan allows and carries none of its legal prerequisites. (6) SECURITY.md deliberately has no e-mail address, contradicting the plan's security@/conduct@ bullet; this leaves no reporting channel while the repo is private. (7) There is no dedicated kill switch; the only all-pack stop is a decision quota of zero, which needs a redeploy. Limits. 33 of the 64 items are owner matters (owner_only true); the 21 with no repository trace are Unknown and say what would settle them. Blocker counts overlap: each gate item restates prerequisites that also appear as B items, B23 repeats B04 and B05, and B19.1, B19.2, B34 and W2.clin-label are facets of the missing A8 workflow, so count gaps by prerequisite, not by item. The HTI-1 attribute list in B40 is from memory of 45 CFR 170.315(b)(11)(iv)(B) with no network access; which fields the card has is verified. GitHub platform facts (environment protection, rulesets and private vulnerability reporting on a private repository under a Free personal account) rest on the repo's own note at tasks/todo.md:149 and on memory, not on a check of the account. Docker was not run: W3.it and W2.it rely on route-level tests plus the CI job definition. Postgres variants of the targeted tests were skipped (no test database); SQLite variants passed. Hosted settings (daily limits, firewall, Vercel protection, OAuth consent screen) are deliberately absent from the tree (tests/test_public_tree.py), so they are Unknown by design. No secret scanner was run. In flight, not audited (from `git log --oneline HEAD..<branch>` only): claude/inbox-automation-gate (2 commits), claude/community-packs (7), feat/dashboard-tables (1), claude/design-c (3). Isolation. Every command that could create files ran with its working directory and outputs under scratchpad/tmp/partB-gates-skeptic/ (a scaffolded pack, one SQLite file, three small scripts, pytest's base temp). Targeted pytest runs used -p no:cacheprovider, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 and a 58-second subprocess timeout. `git status --short` in the worktree prints nothing at the end and HEAD is still e55ed48c. The git-ignored var/ directory's timestamp moved from 13:47:24 to 13:49:58 EDT during the session while var/mendari.db itself stayed at 08:56:27; none of my commands names that path and other skeptic sessions were running in the same worktree at the time (their scratch folders appeared alongside mine), so I attribute it to a transient file from another session; nothing remains there and nothing tracked changed. No secret value was printed; git remote output was shown with credentials masked and trailer counts with e-mail addresses stripped.

## A1. Pre-public hygiene

### A1.1a: Partial (verified); severity medium; stage 2; effort S (<1 day)

**Plan says.** Step 1 (p7): scan the full git history for secrets with gitleaks.

**Current state.** A CI job `secrets` runs gitleaks v8.30.1 (image pinned by digest) over a full-depth checkout with the default rules plus one narrow allowance. It starts on pull requests and pushes to main only: no schedule, no tag trigger, no manual trigger, and the tracker treats making it a required check as optional. The only test reads strings in the workflow and the shape of the allowlist; nothing proves the scanner detects anything (no planted-key control). gitleaks is not installed here and docker was off-limits, so no run was reproduced; the only statement of a clean result is a tracker line (a lead). My own pattern scan (13 well-known key formats) over all 237 local commits found no key; the single 'PRIVATE KEY' hit is a string comparison in code. That scan is not a substitute for the tool.

**Evidence.**

- .github/workflows/ci.yml:395-408 - job `secrets`: checkout with fetch-depth 0 (line 404), then `docker run ... ghcr.io/gitleaks/gitleaks:v8.30.1@sha256:... git /repo --config /repo/.gitleaks.toml --redact --no-banner --exit-code 1` (lines 407-408)
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:3-6 - triggers are push to main and pull_request only
- .gitleaks.toml:6-17 - useDefault = true; one allowlist: rule generic-api-key, path deploy/onprem/.env.example, condition AND, regex on the empty MENDARI_PHI_KEY line
- tests/test_workflow_safety.py::test_the_history_is_scanned_for_secrets (lines 108-121) - asserts fetch-depth 0, the image name, the config flag, --exit-code 1 and the allowlist shape; it never runs a scan
- $ which gitleaks trufflehog -> gitleaks not found / trufflehog not found
- $ git log --all -E -G<pattern> --format=@%h --name-only, for AWS, GitHub, Slack, sk-, Google, Stripe live, Neon, Vercel ids and tokens, JWT, PyPI token, Neon host, bypass header -> none; for 'BEGIN ... PRIVATE KEY' -> 204ee206 src/openhealth/standards/bulk.py only (the string comparison now at src/mendari/standards/bulk.py:61)
- $ git rev-list --count --all -> 237; $ git rev-list --count HEAD -> 187
- tasks/todo.md:102-103 - 'Optionally make `secrets` a required check' (lead)
- tasks/todo.md:137 - 'gitleaks found none beyond the allowed example file' (lead, not evidence)

**Recommendation.** Run gitleaks once by hand over a mirror clone (all refs) and record tool version, refs scanned and result in the private report. In CI, add a positive-control step (a throwaway repository with a fake key must make the same command exit 1) so a silently broken scan cannot pass, and make the job a required check.

### A1.3c: Contradicts the plan (verified); severity low; stage 3; effort S (<1 day)

**Plan says.** Step 3 (p7): container image publishing must use the same environment.

**Current state.** images.yml publishes from a second environment, `ghcr`, not `pypi`, and a test pins that name. It is a separate workflow with no dependency on release.yml: a tag whose release build fails its tests can still build and push images (subject to the same unverifiable approval), there is no tag-equals-version check, and the engine image is pushed without any smoke test at tag time (only per-pack images run `mendari test`), although the header says each is tested. A second environment with the same reviewer rule gives the same protection and keeps the two write scopes apart, so the deviation is in the letter more than the intent.

### A1.3d: Partial (verified); severity high; stage 3; effort S (<1 day)

**Plan says.** Step 3 (p7): container image publishing must no longer run on any version tag automatically.

**Current state.** Since the plan's commit the image job gained `environment: ghcr` and job-scoped permissions, which is the plan's own gate. The trigger is unchanged: the workflow still starts on every `v*` tag push. Whether publishing then waits for a person depends entirely on a reviewer rule in GitHub settings that the repository cannot show and that its own tracker lists as not yet set (and, per the same note, cannot take effect while the repository is private on the current plan). With no rule, a tag push today builds and pushes six images to GHCR with the workflow token: the workflow fails open. A test requires any job with a write scope to sit in a workflow triggered only by tag pushes, so moving to a manual trigger fails the suite until that test changes.

Change tests/test_workflow_safety.py lines 28-31 and 78-79 in the same PR.

**Current state.** images.yml builds each of the six images with plain docker build on ubuntu-latest and pushes that single-architecture (amd64) image. There is no buildx, QEMU or platforms setting in any workflow, and no test asserts platforms. The workflow has never run (no v* tag exists), so no image of any architecture is on GHCR. The base images are pinned by digest, which does not prevent a multi-arch build.

- $ git tag -l -> (no tags), so images.yml (tags v* only, line 5-7) has never published

**Recommendation.** Switch the image job to buildx with platforms linux/amd64,linux/arm64 (pinned setup-qemu and setup-buildx actions), smoke-test each architecture before the push, and add a pull-request job that builds both platforms without pushing so the workflow is exercised before the first tag. Add a workflow test that asserts both platforms.

### A2.5a: Partial (verified); severity low; stage 3; effort S (<1 day)

**Plan says.** `mendari new`: one-line errors naming file, field and fix instead of raw tracebacks (p.8, item 5)

**Current state.** Two failure modes give a clean one-line error (target not empty, bad --id); a missing --id is an argparse usage error. ### A2.5c: Partial (verified); severity medium; stage 3; effort S (<1 day)

**Plan says.** `mendari test`: one-line errors naming file, field and fix (p.8, item 5)

**Current state.** No traceback in the first auditor's 33 broken-input runs or in the skeptic's 144 validate and test runs; test shares validate's loader, so the same message gaps apply. Silent passes matter more than wording. A misspelt expectation key is ignored, so the test passes while checking nothing; a case with no expect at all passes; an empty cases file reports '0 passed, 0 failed' with exit 0; an unknown key in a case (for example providers:) is ignored. A --provider override naming a slot the pack does not have is silently dropped, so the run uses default providers and reports PASS. test also runs a case whose input violates the pack's schema and reports an expectation failure, where validate names the schema problem.

- $ mendari test case-no-expect -> PASS x / 1 passed, 0 failed

- $ mendari test good --provider nope=rules -> 3 passed, 0 failed (the override is ignored)
- src/mendari/settings.py:167-170 - an unscoped setting for a slot the pack lacks is neither chosen nor listed as skipped; src/mendari/cli.py:31-37 - the comment says a typed setting that cannot apply is an error here

- $ mendari validate t-input-invalid -> '- tests/cases.yaml case 1 (x): input 3 is not of type 'object''; $ mendari test t-input-invalid -> FAIL x / recommendation: expected 'refill', got None
- tests/test_pack_content.py::test_a_behaviour_test_of_the_wrong_shape_is_named_never_a_500

**Recommendation.** Reject unknown expect keys, unknown case keys and cases with no expectation, naming the case and the nearest valid key; make zero cases a failure or a loud warning. On the command line, make an override for an unknown slot an error, and print the running variants at the top of mendari test as eval does.

## A3. Packs from outside authors safe to run (pack security)

### A3.1a: Partial (verified); severity high; stage 4; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** A pack may name only a provider type and variant (p.9, step 1)

**Current state.** A pack can no longer name a secret or a destination URL, but a remote variant still carries configuration that decides what the call does, what it costs and, on the default LLM endpoint, which model vendor receives the input. `llm`: the pack's pinned `model` beats the deployment's LLM_MODEL (a test asserts it), and the default endpoint is a gateway that routes by model id, so the pack picks the vendor that processes the decision input on the deployment's credential; the pack also sets max_tokens (up to 32,000), timeout (up to 120 s), reasoning effort and temperature. `jev`: the deployment's JEV_MODEL wins, but the pack sets its own price (0 is accepted) and timeout. The pack chooses which input fields leave (`state_fields`; omitted means the whole input: the probe sent the message and the patient fields) and its own default variant (`use:`). The only spend limit is a daily call count (default 500 per provider type), not a cost or token cap. `mendari validate` says ok for such a pack.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/core/spec.py:296-301 - ProviderVariant is `extra="allow"`: provider-specific keys ride in the manifest
- src/mendari/providers/llm.py:78-91 - LlmConfig fields a pack may set: model, timeout_ms<=120000, state_fields, max_tokens<=32000, temperature, reasoning_effort, calibration, batch
- src/mendari/providers/llm.py:114 - `self.settings.model or os.environ.get(MODEL_ENV, ...)`: the pack's model wins over the deployment's
- src/mendari/providers/llm.py:49,147-149 - the default endpoint is the Vercel AI Gateway, called with AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY or the deployment's OIDC token
- src/mendari/providers/jev.py:62-71,104,160 - JevConfig: model (JEV_MODEL wins), timeout_ms, state_fields, cost_per_1k_input_tokens_usd (ge=0, used for cost_usd), batch
- src/mendari/providers/base.py:170-177 - batch_state returns the whole input when a variant omits state_fields
- src/mendari/settings.py:13-14,111-126 - the jev and llm daily limits default to 500 calls; they count calls, not cost
- tests/test_llm.py::test_model_precedence_and_options - line 146 asserts 'the pack's pin wins' over LLM_MODEL
- $ python skeptic/wire.py (scratch pack through load_pack and build_provider, httpx.MockTransport, LLM_MODEL set to a deployment-approved model) -> mendari validate rc 0; llm request: url https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/chat/completions, deployment key attached, model 'somevendor/most-expensive-model', max_tokens 32000, reasoning high, timeout_ms 120000, input fields sent ['message','patient'] with age_band and preferred_language; jev request: url and key the deployment's, model 'deployment-jev', pack_price 0.0

**Recommendation.** Define a closed, per-type list of pack-settable fields and enforce it at load. For remote providers the deployment owns model and spend: for any pack that is not the deployment owner's, LLM_MODEL (or an allowed-models list) wins over a pack pin, the deployment caps max_tokens, timeout and effort, and the Jev price comes from deployment configuration. Keep `state_fields` (data minimisation) and require it on remote variants of outside packs. The in-flight community-packs work (tasks/todo.md:60-63, a lead, not audited) says a community pack's pinned model and max_tokens give way; make that the rule for every outside pack.

### A3.1b: Done (verified); severity none; stage 4; effort S (<1 day)

**Plan says.** Bind each provider type to its secret and its destination in server configuration (p.9, step 1)

**Current state.** Since PR #127 the names of the variables that supply endpoint, model and key are constants in code, read from the deployment's environment. No pack value reaches an environment lookup, a request URL or an Authorization header: every `os.environ` read in core/ and providers/ uses a literal, a module constant, or a name its caller passes as a constant (`resolve_key`, `phi._key`). Jev: JEV_API_URL with JEV_API_KEY or JEV_CONNECTOR. LLM: LLM_BASE_URL (default the Vercel AI Gateway) with AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY or OIDC, or LLM_API_KEY for another base. CQL: MENDARI_CQL_URL, called through the FHIR allow-list. Which variant runs per slot is the deployment's MENDARI_PROVIDERS, else the pack's default. One caveat, carried under A3.1a: the default LLM destination is a gateway, so the URL is bound but the vendor behind it follows the pack's `model`.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/providers/jev.py:56-59,115,148 - API_KEY_ENV, CONNECTOR_ENV, ENDPOINT_ENV, MODEL_ENV constants; endpoint from os.environ[ENDPOINT_ENV]; resolve_key(key_env=API_KEY_ENV, connector_env=CONNECTOR_ENV)
- src/mendari/providers/llm.py:57-60,147-155,190-197,385-386 - fixed variable names; the token is chosen by the deployment's base URL only; POST to f"{self.base_url}/chat/completions"
- src/mendari/providers/cql.py:56,98-102,191 - MENDARI_CQL_URL, called through GuardedHttp()
- src/mendari/providers/credentials.py:119-126 - resolve_key reads only the names its caller passes
