### A6.chain: Partial (verified); severity high; stage 3; effort L (1-2 weeks)

**Plan says.** Audit question for A6 (p15 items 2-3 and acceptance 1): does the audit chain separate organizations?

**Current state.** No: one global chain with an organization filter on reads, not one chain per organization. audit_events has no organization column; each append links to the newest event of the whole deployment, under one deployment-wide lock. Reads are filtered by joining each event to its decision's organization. Consequences: (1) an organization's export cannot be verified on its own, since its events' prev_hash values point at other organizations' events; (2) verify answers every admin with the global count and head and moves when another organization acts; (3) key, client, governance and deployment events belong to no decision, so no route returns them to anyone; (4) the organization a decision belongs to is not covered by any hash: moving a row to another organization leaves verify ok and hands the decision to the other organization.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/core/audit.py:93-101 - audit_events: seq, decision_id, event, payload, created_at, prev_hash, hash (no org)
- src/mendari/core/audit.py:733-734 - _append_many reads the last hash of the whole table
- src/mendari/core/audit.py:1911-1914 - _JOINED: audit_events JOIN decisions (non-decision events never match)
- src/mendari/core/audit.py:401-405 - decision.created payload: record_sha256 (+ requested_by); the org is only a column (:397)
- src/mendari/core/db.py:188 - every exclusive Postgres session takes one pg_advisory_xact_lock
- $ .venv/bin/python -B $SK/p1.py -> CHAIN audit_events columns: created_at, decision_id, event, hash, payload, prev_hash, seq; VERIFY as org a and org b: 15 events each, same head; b's count after a decides again: 15 -> 16; b's first event's prev_hash is the hash of org a's decision.created
- $ .venv/bin/python -B $SK/p1.py -> non-decision chain rows: 10 of 17; EXPORT (org a admin) event codes: decision.created, feedback.recorded, review.resolved only
- $ .venv/bin/python -B $SK/p1.py -> MOVE (UPDATE decisions SET org) a's decision to b: b reads it 200, a reads it 404, verify ok True; decision.created payload keys: record_sha256, requested_by

**Recommendation.** Bind the organization into every new chained event's payload and add a nullable org column to audit_events (NULL = default or deployment). Then choose: per-organization chains (own head, own lock, own verify and a self-verifying export) with the existing chain kept as the default organization's, or one global chain plus per-organization proofs. Either way scope verify, give administrative events an organization-scoped reader, and cut over with a chained marker event because old and new instances overlap during a deploy.

### A6.owner-data: Unknown (inferred); severity high; stage 3; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** Audit question for A6 (p15 item 2): what would break for the owner's existing data when accounts and organizations land?

**Current state.** The repository cannot show what production holds; the distinct org values, the count of NULL-org rows, the live keys and the sign-in settings would settle it, and only the owner can read them. From the code, the risks are: (1) the owner's access is the e-mail mapping itself, so removing it without a bootstrap locks the owner out, on a platform with no shell; (2) existing rows are 'default' or NULL, so any change to how the owner's organization is derived (an organization claim, a generated id) strands them: the owner would sign in to another organization and see an empty dashboard; (3) rewriting org values is outside the store's additive-only migration rule; (4) existing keys, approvals, quota counters and EHR registrations name 'default' as text; (5) switching the chain to per-organization linking breaks verify for the existing chain unless verify changes in the same release and mixed-version instances are handled; (6) live sessions carry org and claims and must not keep granting by stale claims after the switch; (7) exact-match test oracles (public route set, role permissions, route scopes) fail until updated.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/core/audit.py:233-240 - _ADDED_COLUMNS: 'Additive only: nullable, no default, never renamed or dropped'; decisions.org 'NULL is the default organization'
- src/mendari/core/audit.py:2072 - COALESCE(d.org, 'default') = org
- src/mendari/server/auth.py:813-815 - the owner's organization is 'default' when no claim is set or sent
- src/mendari/core/audit.py:1828-1839 - verify() walks all rows by seq with one running prev
- src/mendari/server/auth.py:536-545 - sessions made before a change keep roles from stored claims for up to 8 hours
- src/mendari/server/vercel.py:25-28 - hosted sign-in is configured only through MENDARI_OIDC_* variables
- tests/test_auth.py:358-411,416-452 - exact oracles for public routes, role permissions and route scopes

**Recommendation.** Before building, the owner reads from production the distinct org values and NULL counts per table, the live keys and the sign-in variables. Build with: 'default' kept as the owner's organization id; an idempotent bootstrap of the owner's membership from one environment value; additive tables and columns only; a rehearsal that loads a copy-shaped database (synthetic rows in the old layout) and asserts the owner sees the same counts before and after and verify stays ok.

**Unit notes.** Scope: audited commit e55ed48c only, as the skeptic for unit A6. $SK = <the audit's scratch folder>/tmp/A6-skeptic (p1.py: routes, two-organization sweep, keys, scopes, chain; p2.py: sign-in organization fallback, no-role page, quotas, a 24-hour rate; p3.py: aggregates, PAS, evaluation spend; run.py, run_tests.py, run_snippets.py: runners with a 60 s subprocess timeout; their scratch SQLite files). Everything ran with python -B, its working directory, databases, TMPDIR and HOME under $SK, sign-in on with sessions made as tests/conftest.py makes them, and no network beyond a 127.0.0.1 server started by scripts/check_doc_snippets.py. I wrote my own probes instead of re-running the auditor's; the auditor's files in tmp/A6 were read only. Verdict on the auditor's findings: they hold. Every Done, Contradicts, blocker and high item was re-checked in the code and reproduced by command; no status was refuted except A6.5 (Missing -> Partial). The headline stands: tenancy for decision data is real (41 organization-data routes, no leak found in three 51-call sweeps plus writes), so the plan's 'no organizations' is imprecise. What A6 lacks is the identity layer (users, memberships, invitations, an organization record), the Keys screen and rotation, a real no-access page, a dedicated per-user daily cap, the scope fixes and the generated isolation test. The two findings the plan does not name remain the ones that decide whether hosted partner access is safe: a sign-in without an organization claim lands in 'default' with the owner's data (A6.2b), and the audit chain is one global chain whose events carry no organization, are partly unreadable, and do not make a decision's organization tamper-evident (A6.chain). Stage: every item is marked 3 because the gate out of stage 2 is the one that lists A6. In practice A6.1a, A6.2a, A6.2b and A6.acc-1 must be finished before any design partner is given hosted access during stage 2 (the plan's gates do not say so: see the plan defect). Partners can self-host meanwhile, as plan p14 says. Severity: A6 as a whole is an explicit gate prerequisite; blocker is kept for the two items without which a partner cannot safely be on the hosted site at all (A6.1a, A6.2b). Not determinable from the repository: what the production database and environment hold (distinct org values, NULL-org rows, live keys, the sign-in variables). That the hosted deployment signs in with Google by e-mail map comes from the owner's notes, not from the code; the code evidence is the fallback at src/mendari/server/auth.py:813-815. Tests a build session should add (the auditor's list, kept): a generated two-organization sweep built from app.routes with a reviewed allow-list of deployment-wide routes; a static test that every AuditStore reader calls _scope() or is on a short operator-only list (verify, purge, erase); sign-in tests that a missing, list-valued, numeric or literal-'default' claim never yields the default organization in memberships mode; one check_doc_snippets pass per key preset in a non-default organization, plus a CDS Hooks example; chain tests (an organization's export verifies alone, verify does not move when another organization acts, changing a decision's organization breaks verification, administrative events readable only by their organization); browser tests for the invitation flow, the Keys screen and the no-access page; limit tests (per-principal daily cap answers 429 with Retry-After and records nothing, two keys of one organization share the organization bucket, evaluation calls counted per organization); a migration rehearsal on a database in today's layout. Tests run: 30 targeted tests passed on SQLite (all of test_api_keys, 7 of test_auth, 1 of test_fhir_routes, 5 of test_limits, test_doc_snippets), and a selection of test_backend_services exited 0; Postgres variants skipped (no test database here; CI runs them). ## A7. Pack store

### A7.1: Missing (verified); severity blocker; stage 4; effort L (1-2 weeks)

**Plan says.** A versioned pack store per organization in the database, keyed by each pack's content digest, alongside the built-in packs; drafts and published versions immutable once saved (p.16, item 1).

**Current state.** Confirmed by re-reading the code and probing a scratch server. No pack store exists in the hosted server. Packs are read from the file system once at start-up (MENDARI_PACKS_PATH, the hub pull cache, the bundled packs) into one process-wide dict keyed by pack id, newest version only, and every organization is served the same dict. The audit database has 16 tables and none holds packs, versions or drafts; there is no draft or published state anywhere in src. This is a missing feature, not a present exposure: nothing can be uploaded to the platform today. Building blocks that exist: (a) the Hub registry, a separate FastAPI app that is not mounted in the platform server, with its own tables storing immutable signed versions keyed by (namespace, name, version) and archives keyed by archive SHA-256; it is scoped by namespace and by admin or namespace tokens, not by organization, and the content digest is only a field in the metadata JSON; (b) Pack.digest content addressing, with later reads checked against the hashes taken at load; (c) organization scoping through the tenancy context variable, already used by governance_approvals, eval_reports and api_keys; (d) the shared SQLite/Postgres layer in core/db.py that both stores use; (e) the deployments table, which already records pack id, version and digest per environment.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/server/app.py:355-364 - packs come from discover(packs_paths) at start-up; `installed` keeps only the newest version per pack id; `packs` is one dict for the whole process
- src/mendari/server/app.py:656-663 - list_packs returns every served pack to any caller; no organization filter
- src/mendari/core/audit.py:70-231 - `_TABLES`: 16 tables (decisions, audit_events, eval_reports, provider_usage, feedback, decision_inputs, governance_approvals, deployments, api_keys, capability_versions, smart_sessions, oauth_clients, oauth_tokens, rate_limits, org_usage, notes); none holds packs, versions or drafts
- src/mendari/hub/registry.py:80-92 - hub_versions PRIMARY KEY (namespace, name, version); hub_archives keyed by archive_sha256; no org column
- src/mendari/hub/registry.py:234-241 - publishing an existing version answers 409 'versions are immutable'
- tests/test_registry.py::test_a_signed_pack_is_published_once_and_read_back - passes ($ pytest tests/test_governance.py tests/test_gate.py tests/test_feedback.py tests/test_registry.py tests/test_archive.py -> 91 passed, 35 skipped, re-run by the verifier)
- src/mendari/core/pack.py:260-282 - `_digest`: sha256 over every behaviour-defining file; :29-30 evals/ and DECISION_CARD.md are left out of the digest
- src/mendari/core/registry.py:27-37 - search_paths: environment variable, hub cache, bundled packs; nothing from a database
- src/mendari/core/audit.py:151-160 - deployments table: environment, release, pack_id, pack_version, pack_digest
- $ git grep -n -i -E 'draft|promot|pack_store|pack store|pack-author|pack_author|pack_versions|UploadFile|multipart|upload' -- src/mendari (JSON and vendored files excluded) -> 2 unrelated comment hits ('pack-authored')
- $ git grep -n 'hub.registry' -- src/mendari/server -> no hits; the registry app is started only by `mendari registry serve` (src/mendari/cli.py:767)
- $ in-process TestClient on a scratch database (re-run): POST /api/packs -> 405; PUT /api/packs/mendari/patient-inbox-router -> 405; POST .../versions, .../promote, .../copy and /api/packs/drafts -> 404

**Recommendation.** Add `pack_versions` (org, pack_id, version, digest, state draft|published, archive_sha256, created_by, created_at; primary key org+digest) and an archive blob table to the audit store, written with RegistryStore's insert-if-absent pattern and chained (`pack.draft.saved`, `pack.published`). Resolve packs per request as built-ins plus the caller's organization's rows. Reuse hub/archive.verify and extract unchanged. Drop the uploader's evals/ and DECISION_CARD.md on save (they are outside the digest) and compute Mendari's own. Refuse uploads into built-in namespaces such as `mendari/`. Decide first whether this is a new table or the Hub registry's schema with org and state columns (see the opportunity 'One store, not two').

### A7.2: Missing (verified); severity blocker; stage 4; effort L (1-2 weeks)

**Plan says.** A pack-author role. Authors upload a signed archive or copy a built-in pack, then validate and test it as a draft. Drafts run under the A3 safeguards plus a per-organization CPU and provider budget (p.16, item 2).

**Current state.** Confirmed. There is no author role, no permission for pack writes, no upload or copy route and no CLI copy command. Validation and behaviour tests exist only as CLI commands; the validation logic sits in cli.py rather than in a reusable function. Signed-archive build, verify and extract are implemented and tested (size, expansion, path, link and name-collision checks) and can be reused as they are. The safeguards the item names are not in place at this commit: (1) `(a+)+$` passes pack validation and runs on Python `re` with no time limit (re-measured: the match time quadruples for every two extra characters), no test covers catastrophic patterns, and the module's own docstring says isolation waits until uploads exist; (2) no CPU budget of any kind exists in src; (3) per-organization quotas exist for decisions, Jev calls and LLM calls, but evaluations are exempt by design and by test, so a draft's test runs would be limited only by the deployment-wide daily provider budget and a 6-per-hour rate limit per principal; (4) there are no users, memberships or invitations; the organization comes from an OIDC claim.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/server/auth.py:91-109 - ROLES = viewer, reviewer, service, governance, admin; PERMISSIONS holds no pack-write permission
- src/mendari/hub/archive.py:171-217 - verify: caps, file hashes and Ed25519 signature checked in memory before anything is written; :220-244 extract: the pack must load with the signed id, version and digest
- $ pytest tests/test_governance.py tests/test_gate.py tests/test_feedback.py tests/test_registry.py tests/test_archive.py -> 91 passed, 35 skipped (Postgres variants); re-run by the verifier
- src/mendari/cli.py:60-95 - cmd_validate and _test_input_problems: builds every provider variant, parses the FHIR mapping, checks test inputs against the schema; CLI-only ($ git grep '_test_input_problems' -- src -> cli.py only)
- src/mendari/core/patterns.py:10-14 - '`re` has no time limit ... packs from others will run in an isolated process with memory and time limits once uploads or a public registry exist'; :39 re.compile
- $ python (re-run): patterns.problem('(a+)+$', RULES_FLAGS) -> None; re.search on 'a'*n+'!' takes 0.018 s (n=18), 0.071 s (n=20), 0.29 s (n=22)
- $ grep -n -i 'backtrack|a+|time limit|slow' tests/test_patterns.py -> no hits: no test exercises a catastrophic pattern
- $ git grep -n -i -E 'cpu|process_time|setrlimit|RLIMIT|multiprocessing|re2' -- 'src/mendari/**/*.py' pyproject.toml -> no budget, isolation or linear-time engine
- src/mendari/core/decision.py:162-165 - for_evaluation() returns a budget without the organization limits
- tests/test_limits.py::test_each_organization_has_its_own_quota_and_evaluations_spend_none - passes (re-run)
- src/mendari/settings.py:129 - ORG_METRICS = decisions, jev, llm (no CPU or evaluation metric); src/mendari/server/limits.py:100 - evaluate: Rate(6, 3600, 6), keyed per principal (:265)
- $ mendari copy mendari/patient-inbox-router x -> 'invalid choice: copy' (re-run)
- $ git grep -n -i -E 'invitation|membership|invite' -- 'src/mendari/**/*.py' -> no hits; no users, organizations, memberships or invitations table in src
- src/mendari/server/auth.py:17, 814 - the organization comes from MENDARI_OIDC_ORG_CLAIM

**Recommendation.** Do not open any upload path until A3 item 2 lands (RE2 or an isolated worker with time and memory limits) and A6's membership model exists. Then add an `author` role with a `packs.write` permission (people only, like `keys`); `POST /api/packs/drafts` taking an .ohpack verified against keys registered to the organization; `POST /api/packs/{id}/copy` that rewrites the namespace to the organization's; a library function validate_pack() shared by the CLI, the Hub publish path and the store; and an `eval` organization metric plus a wall-clock or CPU budget per draft run charged through CallBudget. Charging evaluations to an organization reverses a tested rule (evaluations spend no organization quota), so change that test deliberately and say so in the PR.

### A7.3: Missing (verified); severity blocker; stage 4; effort L (1-2 weeks)

**Plan says.** Test-data upload with checks: schema validation per case; label set equal to the pack's declared answers; minimum 50 cases per label to run an evaluation; duplicate detection; a hash check that rejects any case matching a hidden evaluation set (A8); reject any upload over the PHI-detection threshold (names, dates of birth, MRNs, phone numbers, addresses) with a deterministic detector that reports what was found (p.16, item 3).

**Current state.** Confirmed; every measurement was reproduced on a scratch copy of the inbox pack. There is no dataset upload. The server evaluates only a pack's own datasets or JSONL files an operator placed in one server-side directory shared by all organizations. load_dataset checks only that each line is JSON with an `input` object. None of the six checks exists: a label outside the declared answers is a KeyError traceback from `mendari eval` and an HTTP 500 from the eval route; a case that fails the input schema is scored as a BLOCK rather than rejected; 20 cases repeated three times are scored as n=60; a 3-case file reports 100% accuracy with no size warning; a case holding a name, date of birth, MRN, phone number and street address is accepted and evaluated, locally and through the route. No hidden sets exist (A8 absent), datasets have only a whole-file SHA-256, and no PHI detector exists anywhere in src or scripts. One reusable piece: PhiPolicy.input_hash, a keyed HMAC over the canonical input, could give per-case hashes. The shipped reference data would itself fail the plan's rules (labels under 50 cases in every pack; heavy duplication in ai-guard).

**Evidence.**

- $ mendari eval inbox --dataset ds/dups.jsonl -> exit 0, 'Dataset dups (n=60)' for 20 distinct cases (re-run)
- $ mendari eval inbox --dataset ds/phi.jsonl (one case with a name, DOB, MRN, phone, street address) -> exit 0, n=5, report produced; the eval route answers 200 for the same file (re-run)
- $ mendari eval inbox --dataset ds/tiny.jsonl -> exit 0, n=3, accuracy 100.0%, no warning (re-run)
- src/mendari/server/app.py:429-444 - datasets are the pack's own or `datasets_dir.glob('*.jsonl')`; $ POST .../datasets -> 405 (re-run)
- $ git grep -n -i -E 'phi_detect|detect_phi|mrn|dob|deidentif|presidio|scrub|redact|hidden.set|hidden_set|dedup|duplicate' -- 'src/mendari/**/*.py' scripts -> no detector, no hidden-set code, no duplicate check

**Recommendation.** Write the checks as pure functions in a new src/mendari/evals/dataset_checks.py and ship them first as a local command (`mendari data check PACK FILE`) run in CI on every shipped dataset; the hosted upload then calls the same code. Include: per-case validation with core/input_schema.validator; labels within the declared answers; per-label counts; within-file duplicates and overlap with the pack's own train and calibration data by canonical-input HMAC; lookup against A8's hash index without revealing which set matched; and a PHI detector whose report names kind, case id, field path and count, never the text. Fix the KeyError now so a bad label is a MendariError naming the case id and a 422 from the route (S, independent of the store).

### A7.4: Partial (verified); severity high; stage 4; effort L (1-2 weeks); M (1-3 days) if A9's statistics module has landed first, as the plan's run order intends

**Plan says.** Authors run the existing evaluation on their own data and compare a draft with the current version on the same cases: accuracy, macro-F1, calibration, false automation, critical-label recall, each with confidence intervals (methods in A9), plus a paired comparison of the two versions (p.16, item 4).

**Current state.** Confirmed, with one correction. The evaluation exists and is tested, as point estimates only: accuracy; per-label precision, recall, F1; macro-F1 (mean over labels with support); ECE over 10 equal-width bins; multi-class Brier; false-automation rate (wrong AUTO over AUTO with ground truth) and share (over all cases); per-critical-label detection rate and automated count; threshold sweep; latency p50/p95; cost; subgroups. There is no confidence interval and no paired test anywhere in src, tests or scripts, and scipy and statsmodels are not installed. compare() is a threshold check of one report against a baseline report, built for site-versus-benchmark validation: accuracy delta against the pack's tolerance, per-label recall drop over twice the tolerance (support 10 or more), subgroup drop over twice the tolerance (n 15 or more), false-automation rise over the tolerance, ECE rise over 0.05, and any automated critical case; it does not check that both reports are on the same dataset. gate() applies the same tolerance in a CI script. `compare` and `gate` are not CLI commands. Locally a draft can be set against the current version with `mendari eval DRAFT --dataset X --baseline current.json`. Reproduced: a draft (thresholds lowered to 0.60) that introduced 3 false automations on the 600 test cases (0 of 567 became 3 of 574) is reported as 'No degradation beyond tolerance (3.0 pts)', exits 0 even with --fail-on-degradation, and passes scripts/pack_gate.py, which is the gate the packs workflow runs on pull requests today. Correction to the first audit: reports keep the first 50 misclassified cases of the primary question and, per critical label, every missed case id (uncapped); they still hold no per-case result vector, so a paired comparison cannot be computed from two saved reports. On the hosted server an evaluation needs the admin-only `evaluate` permission, runs only the one served version on pack or server-side datasets, and is one synchronous request capped at 200 cases for remote providers.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/evals/metrics.py:14-46 - accuracy and macro-F1 (:39 only labels with support); :49-77 ECE, docstring 'equal-width confidence bins', bins=10; :80-87 Brier; no interval returned
- src/mendari/evals/harness.py:223-228 - automation n, accuracy, false_automation_rate (over AUTO), false_automation_share (over all cases); :160-186 critical: n, detected, detection_rate, auto_missed, missed_ids (all of them); :255-265 misclassified ids capped at 50
- src/mendari/evals/compare.py:53-170 - threshold rules at lines 74, 98, 112, 126, 139; no check that the two datasets' sha256 match
- src/mendari/evals/gate.py:22-75 - tolerance thresholds on accuracy (:41) and false automation (:52); critical detection must not fall (:71) and automated critical count must not rise (:73)
- $ git grep -n -i -E 'clopper|bootstrap|mcnemar|wilson|kappa|resampl|holm|paired|confidence.interval|binom|scipy|statsmodels' -- src tests scripts pyproject.toml (vendored and JSON files excluded) -> no hits; $ python -c 'import scipy' -> ModuleNotFoundError
- $ mendari eval draft --dataset test --baseline out/current.json -> 'false automation rate 0.5% (3 of 574)' ... 'No degradation beyond tolerance (3.0 pts)'; with --fail-on-degradation exit 0 (re-run; draft digest sha256:d0f732be8114...)
- $ python scripts/pack_gate.py draft --report out/draft.json --main out/current.json -> 'false automation rate | 0.0% | 0.5%' ... 'No regression in the critical metrics', exit 0 (re-run)
- .github/workflows/packs.yml - the pull-request job for changed packs ends with scripts/pack_gate.py; this is the only version-to-version gate in use
- $ mendari eval draft --dataset calibration --baseline out/current.json -> compared 'Local performance (calibration, n=300)' with 'Public benchmark (test, n=600)' without objecting to the different dataset (re-run)
- $ mendari compare inbox inbox -> 'invalid choice: compare'; $ mendari gate inbox -> 'invalid choice: gate' (re-run)
- tests/test_evals.py::test_classification_metrics, ::test_expected_calibration_error, ::test_brier_score, ::test_local_validation_localises_degradation, ::test_comparison_with_itself_is_clean; tests/test_gate.py (5 tests) - pass (re-run)
- src/mendari/server/auth.py:164 - POST .../evals needs `evaluate`; :92-109 only admin holds it; src/mendari/server/app.py:259, 875-876 - REMOTE_EVAL_LIMIT = 200
- verifier's own stdlib calculation, not product code (matches the first audit): exact 95% intervals 23/23 -> [85.2%, 100%]; 3/574 -> [0.11%, 1.52%]; 0/567 -> [0%, 0.65%]; exact McNemar for 0 against 3 discordant cases -> p = 0.25

**Recommendation.** The plan runs A9 before A7, so build src/mendari/evals/stats.py there (exact Clopper-Pearson by bisection on the binomial CDF, seeded percentile bootstrap, exact McNemar; stdlib only) and reuse it here. For A7 add src/mendari/evals/paired.py that takes two per-case result vectors and refuses to run unless the dataset sha256 match, and keep per-case rows (id, correct, auto, auto_wrong, critical hit; ids only) in an internal result artifact. Expose it as `mendari compare CURRENT DRAFT --dataset X` and as the store's comparison. Report new false automations and newly automated critical cases by case id as hard findings, whatever the tolerance or p-value says. Independent of the store, tighten gate.py now: a rise in the count of false automations on the benchmark fails unless waived in the pull request.

### A7.5: Missing (verified); severity blocker; stage 4; effort M (1-3 days), after A7.1

**Plan says.** Promote a draft only through the existing governance approval, bound to its digest (p.16, item 5).

**Current state.** Confirmed. Promotion does not exist: the served version is whichever is newest on disk at start-up. The governance approval that exists is an approval to automate, not to promote. It is per organization, bound to pack id and exact digest, has an expiry and a revocation, is hash-chained, needs the `approve` permission, records the signed-in person as approver, and is looked up by digest for each decision. It accepts risk levels 2 and 3 only: re-measured, approving the risk-0 inbox pack answers 409 'a risk level 0 pack needs no approval'. So it cannot be recorded for three of the five reference packs (risk 0, 1, 1) or for the `mendari new` template (risk 1), and at levels 2 and 3 reusing it for promotion would also lift the AUTO cap, because an active approval is passed into every decision as the runtime override.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/core/audit.py:1297-1330 - approve_automation stores org, pack_id, pack_digest, approver, reference, expires_at and chains governance.approved; :1307 `if risk_level not in (2, 3)` refuses
- src/mendari/core/audit.py:1360-1370 - active_approval matches org, pack_id and exact pack_digest, not revoked, not expired
- src/mendari/server/app.py:422-427 - approved_override passes the approval for pack.digest into each decision as GovernanceOverride; :822-838 the approve route; :827 the approver is the signed-in principal (acting_as)
- tests/test_governance.py::test_an_approval_is_for_exactly_one_pack_and_expires, ::test_levels_that_need_no_approval_or_can_never_have_one_are_refused, ::test_approvals_and_revocations_are_in_the_hash_chain - pass (re-run)
- $ TestClient POST /api/governance {pack_id: mendari/patient-inbox-router, reference, approver} -> 409 'a risk level 0 pack needs no approval' (re-run)
- $ risk levels read through load_pack (re-run): inbox 0, prior-auth 1, referral 1, ai-guard 2, trial 2; src/mendari/templates/new_pack/pack.yaml:21 level 1
- src/mendari/server/app.py:355-364 - the served version is the newest found at start-up

**Recommendation.** Add a separate, chained promotion record (org, pack_id, digest, approver, reference, the evaluation report ids it relied on) that needs the `approve` permission at every risk level and an approver other than the draft's author. Keep the automation approval as it is, still required separately at levels 2 and 3. Resolve the organization's current version from the latest unrevoked promotion; rollback is promoting the earlier digest again.

## A8. Evaluation-set builder and clinician labelling

### A8.goal-1: Missing (verified); severity blocker; stage 4; effort L (1-2 weeks)

**Plan says.** Goal: the evaluation sets are hidden held-out sets (p17); p1 lists 'the hidden, rotating evaluation sets' as the proprietary trust layer.

**Current state.** No hidden set exists. Every set the repository calls held-out is public: all 27 dataset files (22 under packs/*/data, 5 under datasets/) are tracked in git, every pack dataset is inside the pack digest (so it also travels in any signed pack archive), and packs/ and datasets/ ship in the sdist and the wheel. 'Held-out' means two things today: (1) the template `test` split, the tail slice of one seeded generator run that also yields train and calibration from the same template bank, regenerated byte-for-byte by CI; (2) five hand-written `*_holdout.jsonl` files (24, 24, 30, 24, 24 cases; 126 in total), marked only by a filename suffix that the dashboard keys on. Three labels in the ai-guard hold-out were changed after it was created (unsafe_advice no -> yes on agh-04, agh-06, agh-23; inputs unchanged). 'Shifted' means datasets/*-local-site-example.jsonl: the same generator with site='local' (other case mix, some local-only templates), also public. The pack.yaml comments saying each hold-out was written before the rules cannot be checked from history.

**Evidence.**

- $ git ls-files 'packs/*/data/*' datasets | wc -l -> 27 (includes the five *_holdout.jsonl files)
- src/mendari/core/pack.py:296 - every evaluation.datasets path is a referenced file that must be inside the pack digest
- pyproject.toml:63-70 and 76-78 - the sdist includes /packs and /datasets; the wheel force-includes packs -> mendari/_packs and datasets -> mendari/_datasets
- src/mendari/sandbox/synthetic_inbox.py:674-676 - public_splits(seed=7): one generate(2400) sliced into train[:1500], calibration[1500:1800], test[1800:]
- src/mendari/sandbox/synthetic_guard.py:171-173, synthetic_prior_auth.py:157-159, synthetic_referral.py:271-273, synthetic_trial.py:73-75 - the same pattern: one seeded run sliced into splits
- src/mendari/sandbox/synthetic_inbox.py:3, 605 and 679-680 - 'Two populations are generated from one template bank'; templates are filtered by site in ('all', site); local_site(seed=11) is the shifted set
- $ python facts2.py (scratchpad/tmp/A8-skeptic) -> regenerated test == committed: True 600
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:65-79 - the reference-pack job rebuilds the data and `git diff --exit-code -- packs datasets` must be empty
- src/mendari/dashboard/leaderboard.js:21 - the default leaderboard dataset is the one whose name ends with '_holdout' (a naming convention, not a state)

Build the hidden-set store outside the repository and outside pack digests (A8.3c, A8.3d), and add a packaging test that fails if a hidden-set file can reach the sdist, the wheel or a pack archive.

### A8.goal-2: Missing (verified); severity blocker; stage 4; effort owner; owner only

**Plan says.** Goal: sets large enough to grade safety-critical behaviour; the stage-4 gate is hidden sets frozen with 100+ positives per critical label (p4 figure, p12, p17).

**Current state.** The five packs declare 14 critical labels. No hand-written held-out set has more than 20 positives for any of them: inbox urgency=urgent 20; referral urgency=urgent 12 and next_step=urgent_review 12; ai-guard verdict=block 9, question_emergency=yes 6, unsafe_advice=yes 8, dose_exceeds_limit=yes 3; prior-auth red_flag=yes 6; trial note_pregnancy 4, note_pancreatitis 2, note_active_cancer_treatment 3, note_recent_cv_event 3, egfr_30_or_more=no 0, no_recent_cv_event=no 0. That is 88 positives against 1,400 needed. Only template sets reach 100: referral test (113 and 124) and train (222 and 267); ai-guard test reaches 100 on three of its four labels (164, 114, 164, 62), but those rows are repeats of 30, 39, 30 and 4 distinct inputs. Language coverage is thin: the inbox test split has 0 Spanish urgent cases, the inbox hold-out 0, red_flags 1. Sizing fact for the owner: critical labels overlap fully in the referral pack (all 113 urgent cases are also urgent_review) and in ai-guard (every block is also unsafe_advice), but hardly at all in the trial pack (84 positive cases carry 95 positives), so the trial pack needs about 530 or more positive cases to reach 100 on each of its six labels.

### A8.goal-3: Missing (verified); severity blocker; stage 3; effort owner; owner only

**Plan says.** Goal: sets labelled by clinicians, with measured agreement (p17); stage-3 gate 'hidden-set labelling under way' (p4 figure, p12).

**Current state.** No label in the repository comes from a clinician and none carries provenance. Template sets take labels from the generator's sampled facts; hand-written sets were labelled by whoever wrote the pack. Every record in all 27 files has exactly the keys id, input, labels, attributes; the attribute keys are site, kind, topic, style, language, sex, age_band, channel, service, payer and specialty. There is no source, labeller, timestamp or agreement field. The only label provenance anywhere is in the output of the feedback export (reporter and created_at per rating, attributes.source='feedback'), which is not committed. No tool to label a set exists (A8.1a), so labelling inside Mendari cannot be under way. Whether clinicians have been recruited, or are labelling outside the product, cannot be seen in the repository: a signed labeller contract or a label file kept outside the repository would settle it.

**Evidence.**

- $ python counts.py -> top-level keys {'id': 8840, 'input': 8840, 'labels': 8840, 'attributes': 8840}; attribute keys site, kind, topic, style, language, sex, age_band, channel, service, payer, specialty
- src/mendari/sandbox/synthetic_inbox.py:638 - labels are template.destination and template.urgency; src/mendari/sandbox/synthetic_trial.py:9 - 'no provider is used to label anything' (ground truth is the generator's own facts)

- $ git grep -n -i -E 'provenance|labelled_by|labeled_by|label_source' -- src/mendari/evals src/mendari/sandbox src/mendari/core/spec.py src/mendari/core/pack.py -> no matches
- $ git grep -l -i -E 'hidden set|clinician[- ]label|kappa' -- docs notes tasks README.md -> no matches (no record or plan of labelling in the repository either)

**Recommendation.** Owner: recruit and contract two clinicians per pack plus an adjudicator (p12). Build: give every set record a provenance block (source, author, each labeller's label and time, adjudication) so the fact is in the data, not in a filename.

### A8.1a: Missing (verified); severity blocker; stage 3; effort L (1-2 weeks)

**Plan says.** Labelling workflow in the dashboard: each case is labelled independently by two clinicians, blind to each other and to any model output (p17, item 1, first bullet).

**Current state.** There is no labelling workflow, data model, route or screen. The two nearest features cannot do it as they are. The review queue shows the model's output on every card (recommendation, confidence, reasons, the answers table) and accepts exactly one resolution per decision, for the primary question only. Feedback allows several named people per decision, but only as a thumbs-down correction to one question, and the label must differ from what the model answered, so it is defined relative to model output. The dashboard has nine views; none is for labelling. The audit store has 16 tables; none holds sets, cases, assignments or labels.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/dashboard/review.js:164 - card title 'Recommended: <label>'; :171 confidence; :178 reasons; :179 criteriaTable(record.answers); :181 one-tap 'Confirm <recommendation>'
- src/mendari/core/audit.py:428-429 and 441-442 - a review sets one label of the primary question; a decision whose review_status is not 'pending' raises 'is not awaiting review'
- tests/test_audit.py::test_correcting_is_an_override - passes; asserts that a second resolve raises 'not awaiting review'
- src/mendari/core/audit.py:543-544 and 2019-2032 - only a thumbs-down carries a right answer, and it may not equal the decision's own answer
- src/mendari/server/app.py:902-913 - GET /api/review returns each queued decision with its record
- src/mendari/dashboard/index.html:92-100 - views: patient, overview, review, audit, evals, monitoring, feedback, card, try
- src/mendari/core/audit.py:71-220 - CREATE TABLE for decisions, audit_events, eval_reports, provider_usage, feedback, decision_inputs and ten more; none for sets or labels
- $ git grep -n -i -w -E 'labeller|labellers|labeler|labelers|labelling|labeling|annotator|annotators|adjudicator|blind|blinded' -- src tests scripts -> one unrelated comment (src/mendari/standards/audit_fhir.py:185); 'rater' appears only for people who rate feedback (src/mendari/core/phi.py:13)

**Recommendation.** New tables (eval_sets, eval_cases, label_assignments, labels) and routes that serve a labeller only the case input: never attributes (kind and topic reveal the answer), never another labeller's label, never any provider output. One form per case covering every non-derived question of the pack, generated from the pack's criteria text. Reuse inputView (pack.js), acting_as identity binding, _check_label validation, and the undo and focus patterns of review.js. Enforce on the server that labeller A, labeller B and the case author are three different people.

### A8.1b: Missing (verified); severity high; stage 4; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** Disagreements go to a third adjudicator (p17, item 1, second bullet).

**Current state.** No adjudication exists. The closest behaviour is in the feedback export: a question is labelled only when every rating gives the same label, and a disagreement is left in the record 'for a person to settle', with no queue, role or event for settling it.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/evals/feedback.py:26-28 and 67-72 - _agreed_labels keeps a label only when all ratings agree; a disagreement stays in the feedback list
- tests/test_feedback.py::test_the_export_labels_what_reporters_agree_on - passes (the disputed case is exported with empty labels)

The adjudicator must be a third person, sees both labels without names and still no model output, and writes the final label. ### A8.1c: Missing (verified); severity high; stage 3; effort S (<1 day)

**Plan says.** Every label, labeller and timestamp is chained in the audit trail (p17, item 1, third bullet).

**Current state.** No labelling events exist to chain. The mechanism is ready and tested for the neighbouring features: review resolutions and feedback ratings are appended to the hash chain with who and when, the actor is the signed-in principal whatever the request body says, and the chain already carries subjects that are not decisions (governance:<id>, deployment:<id>, key:<id>, client:<id>).

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/core/audit.py:459-466 - the review.resolved payload holds final_label and reviewer and is appended to the chain
- src/mendari/core/audit.py:585-596 - the feedback.recorded payload holds reporter, expected and replaces

- src/mendari/core/audit.py:1329, 1412, 1507, 1592 - chain subjects other than decisions

- tests/test_auth.py::test_reviews_and_ratings_are_recorded_for_whoever_is_signed_in - passes

**Recommendation.** Chain label.recorded, label.changed, label.adjudicated and assignment.created under an evalset:<id> subject, from the first label (a chain cannot be back-filled). Chain a keyed hash of the case and of the label values, not the values themselves, so the chain cannot reveal a hidden set's labels to anyone who may read or export the audit trail.

### A8.2: Missing (verified); severity high; stage 4; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** Agreement: Cohen's kappa per question with a bootstrap 95% interval (2,000 resamples, fixed seed), plus raw percent agreement (p17, item 2).

**Current state.** src/mendari/evals/agreement.py does something else. It builds two provider variants of one slot of a pack, runs both on the pack's behaviour tests and datasets, and lists every case and question where the two answers' labels differ. Its output is cases, questions, a boolean `agree` and the list of differences. It compares two machine variants (for example the trial pack's criteria in YAML and in CQL), not two people. It computes no kappa, no percent agreement and no interval. No bootstrap or resampling exists anywhere in the repository. Its tests check exact agreement and a flipped answer through a fake CQL engine; none compares against a hand-computed reference. numpy, scipy, scikit-learn and statsmodels are not installed, so the statistic must be pure Python.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/evals/agreement.py:1-3 - 'Do two variants of a provider slot give the same answers?'
- src/mendari/evals/agreement.py:38 and 43-45 - builds two providers and compares a[question].label != b[question].label
- src/mendari/evals/agreement.py:54-62 - returns pack, slot, variants, cases, questions, agree, differences
- src/mendari/cli.py:254-268 - `mendari agreement --slot --variants` exits 0 or 1 on exact agreement
- tests/test_cql.py::test_the_cql_variant_agrees_with_criteria_through_the_engine and ::test_a_disagreement_is_reported_by_case_id_and_question - pass; neither has a numeric reference (tests/test_cql.py:126-148)
- $ git grep -l -i -E 'kappa|cohen|inter-?rater|krippendorff|fleiss' -- . (uv.lock excluded) -> no matches
- $ git grep -l -i -E 'bootstrap|resampl' -- . (uv.lock excluded) -> no matches
- $ python -c find_spec for numpy, scipy, sklearn, statsmodels, pandas -> all False

**Recommendation.** New module (keep agreement.py for variants; name the new one for raters). Per question: percent agreement, Cohen's kappa per rater pair, and a pooled coefficient when pairs vary; positive and negative specific agreement for each critical label; percentile bootstrap over cases with random.Random(seed), 2,000 resamples, and a written rule for resamples where kappa is undefined. Inputs are the two blind first-pass labels only. Ship a fixture whose kappa is worked by hand in the test's docstring.

### A8.3: Missing (verified); severity blocker; stage 4; effort L (1-2 weeks)

**Plan says.** Set lifecycle: draft, frozen (content-hashed, immutable), active, retired (p17, item 3).

**Current state.** There is no evaluation-set entity and no lifecycle. A dataset is a JSONL file named in a pack manifest or a path on disk. Two partial building blocks exist: the harness takes a SHA-256 of the whole dataset file and writes it into every report, and pack datasets are covered by the pack digest. Neither makes a set immutable: editing a dataset simply yields a new hash and a new pack digest, as happened to the ai-guard hold-out. The one immutability rule in the code is for published pack versions in the Hub; it is a pattern to copy, not a set lifecycle, and a published pack carries its datasets in the open.

**Evidence.**

### A8.3a: Missing (verified); severity high; stage 4; effort S (<1 day)

### A8.3c: Missing (verified); severity blocker; stage 4; effort L (1-2 weeks)

**Plan says.** Active sets are never returned by any API, export or log (p17, item 3, third bullet, first clause).

**Current state.** No set store exists, so nothing is protected. If a hidden set were loaded in the only ways the code offers today (a pack dataset, or a file in the server's datasets directory), it would leak through the API and through exports. API: any role with `read` can list dataset names and sizes and read every saved evaluation report, and a report names up to 50 misclassified cases (id, truth, prediction) and the id of every missed critical case. Export: `mendari eval --out` and `--json` write the same report, and the `shareable()` filter used for registry sharing drops the misclassified list but keeps the missed ids. Log: the security-log line for an evaluation holds only the pack id and a count, which is the right shape, but nothing enforces it for a set.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/server/app.py:691-701 - GET /api/packs/{ns}/{name}/datasets lists names and sizes; :855-889 POST .../evals returns the full report and saves it; :891-898 GET /api/evals returns saved reports whole
- src/mendari/core/audit.py:1805-1814 - reports() returns each stored report JSON unfiltered
- src/mendari/server/auth.py:164 and 174 - running an evaluation needs `evaluate`; every other GET under /api/ needs only `read`
- src/mendari/evals/harness.py:180-184 and 255-265 - missed_ids per critical label; misclassified entries with id, truth, predicted, confidence, outcome
- $ python facts2.py (inbox pack, rules screen, red_flags_holdout) -> misclassified keys ['confidence', 'id', 'outcome', 'predicted', 'truth']; shareable critical keys include 'missed_ids'; missed_ids kept: 16
- src/mendari/server/app.py:880 - log_event(http, 'eval.run', ids=[pack.id], count=...): pack id and count only
- $ git grep -n -i -E 'freez|retire|hidden[ _-]?set|eval[_-]?set|evalset' -- src (data and vendored files excluded) -> no matches

**Recommendation.** A set store sealed like encrypt-mode inputs and kept out of the repository, pack digests and archives. A result shape for hidden sets with aggregates only: no ids, no per-case truth, minimum cell sizes. Protect draft and frozen sets as well as active ones, from the first labelled case, because graded developers and labellers may share a deployment in stage 2.

### A8.3d: Missing (verified); severity blocker; stage 4; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** Access to active sets is restricted to a grading service role (p17, item 3, third bullet, second clause).

**Current state.** There is no grading role and no permission that names evaluation data. Roles are viewer, reviewer, service, governance and admin. The existing `service` role is for deciding (read, decide, outcome), so it is not a grading identity; evaluations are run by `admin` only. Building blocks: unlisted routes already default to admin, and the people-only and EHR-only permission sets show how to make a permission that one kind of principal alone can hold.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/server/auth.py:91-110 - ROLES and PERMISSIONS: five roles; `evaluate` held by admin only; no grading role, no set permission
- src/mendari/server/auth.py:111-119 - PEOPLE_ONLY and EHR_ONLY: permissions limited to one kind of principal
- src/mendari/server/auth.py:125-126 - '(method, path pattern) -> permission, first match wins; unlisted routes need admin'
- $ git grep -n -i -E 'grading|grader' -- src scripts deploy -> no matches

**Recommendation.** Add a machine-only `grading` role (an API key or backend-services client, never a person, and not admin) that alone holds a `grade` permission, modelled on EHR_ONLY. Admins manage the lifecycle of a set without being able to read its cases.

### A8.3e: Missing (verified); severity high; stage 4; effort S (<1 day)

**Plan says.** Every read of an active set is chained (p17, item 3, third bullet, third clause).

**Current state.** No set reads exist to chain. The pattern is built and tested for sealed decision inputs: under PHI mode `encrypt` each input opened is written to the hash chain as `input.read`, naming the reader, in one batched append. Evaluation runs today leave no chained event at all: they run with a store-less Decision and are recorded only by a security-log line.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/core/audit.py:922 and 997 - reveal_inputs chains one `input.read` per decision opened (self._append_many(db, 'input.read', entries))
- tests/test_phi.py::test_signed_in_reviewers_read_inputs_and_each_read_is_chained - passes
- src/mendari/server/app.py:865 and 880 - 'A store-less Decision: evaluation traffic must not pollute the operational audit log'; the run is recorded only by log_event('eval.run')
- src/mendari/core/phi.py:7-11 and 20-25 - encrypt mode seals inputs with AES-256-GCM and chains each read; the input hash is a keyed HMAC because a plain SHA-256 of a short input can be guessed

**Recommendation.** Chain one set.read event per grading run under the set's subject (set id, content hash, grading principal, pack digest, arm, number of cases), and one for every other read (labeller fetch, adjudication, export at retirement). Test that a read without a chained event is impossible through the store API.

### A8.4: Missing (verified); severity high; stage 4; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** Coverage report per set: cases per label and critical label, language mix, source of each case (synthetic generator, hand-written, de-identified real), warning under 100 positives for a critical label (p17, item 4).

Counts appear only as a by-product of running a pack over a dataset (per-label support and the n of each critical label inside an evaluation report, repeated on the Decision Card). Nothing warns under 100. Language is recorded for two packs only (inbox and trial); ai-guard, prior-auth and referral data have no language attribute. No record names its source: generated files carry attributes.site of public or local, hand-written files carry no site, and the difference is otherwise visible only in filenames and id prefixes.

- $ git grep -n -i -E 'stratif|coverage report|label coverage' -- src scripts (vendored bundle excluded) -> no matches

**Recommendation.** A pure function over a set (no pack run needed): cases and distinct cases per label of every question; positives and distinct positives per critical label; language by critical label; source by label; warnings under 100 distinct positives. Add `source` and, for generated cases, a template id to every record. Expose as `mendari evalset coverage` and on the set screen. Running it on today's public sets is useful at once.

**Unit notes.** VERDICT: nothing of A8 is built at e55ed48c. All 12 requirement items (the plan's ten sub-requirements, with the third lifecycle bullet split in three), all 3 acceptance criteria and the three goal facts are Missing. The 21 commits since the plan (PRs #127 and #128) did not touch the sandbox generators, the dataset files, the roles table or the review screen. What exists is reusable plumbing (hash chain, identity binding, sealed inputs with chained reads, keyed input hash, Ed25519 signing, a file content hash) and two features that look similar but are neither blind nor two-rater (review queue, feedback). A realistic build is 3-4 weeks, not the plan's 1-2. STAGES: the labelling items (A8.1a, A8.1c, A8.5, goal-3) are due before stage 3, because the gate into stage 3 is 'hidden-set labelling under way' (p4 figure, p12). Adjudication, agreement, lifecycle, access control, coverage and the acceptance tests are due before stage 4 ('hidden sets frozen with 100+ positives'). If the owner wants early scoreboards before stage 3 (p1, p3), the stage-4 items move up: see the plan defect on sequencing. WHAT agreement.py IS: an exact label match between two provider variants of one slot of one pack (for example trial criteria in YAML and in CQL), over the pack's tests and datasets. No raters, no kappa, no percent, no interval, no hand-computed reference. WHAT 'HELD-OUT' MEANS IN synthetic_*.py: public_splits() makes one seeded generate() call and slices it; test is the tail. Same generator, same template bank, same seed stream as train and calibration. local_site() is a second call with site='local' and its own seed; it reuses the shared templates and adds local-only ones and a different mix. The hand-written *_holdout files are separate, and their 'written before the rules' claim rests on pack.yaml comments only. LABELLER PROVENANCE: none in any dataset. Only the feedback export carries reporter and time, and it is not committed. REUSE FOR A LABELLING WORKFLOW - Review queue (review.js, GET /api/review, POST /api/review/{id}, AuditStore.resolve_review): identity bound to the signed-in person, label checked against the question's label set, chained review.resolved, undo for mis-taps, keyboard focus flow, the `reviewer` role with read_input. Limits: one resolution per decision, primary question only, model output shown. - Feedback (record_feedback, feedback.js): several named people per decision, a per-question label, a person's new rating supersedes the old one, all chained. Limits: thumbs-down only, one question per rating, label must differ from the model's. - Feedback export (evals/feedback.py, `mendari feedback export`): dataset records with labels only where all agree, system output kept apart, reporter and time per rating. No adjudication. - Infrastructure: chain subjects other than decisions; input.read per sealed read; AES-GCM sealing and keyed HMAC input hash (phi.py); Dataset.sha256; per-label support and critical n in reports; Ed25519 signing (hub/archive.py); inputView and criteriaTable for rendering a case and criteria; per-email role mapping at sign-in. TESTS A BUILD SESSION MUST ADD: (1) rater kappa, percent agreement and seeded bootstrap bounds against values worked by hand, with a 3-label question and the single-category resample; (2) a test generated from the app's route list times every role and key scope: a canary planted in a draft, frozen and active set never appears in any response, export, security-log line, audit event or saved report; (3) after freeze every write path is refused and the recomputed hash equals the signed freeze hash at activation, at each grading read and at retirement; (4) a labeller cannot fetch the other labeller's label, provider output or case attributes, differing labels reach only a third person, and label events verify in the chain; (5) coverage warns at 99 distinct positives and counts distinct cases, using a fixture with repeated rows; (6) tests/test_share.py with a report that has missed critical cases; (7) tests/test_packaging.py and tests/test_public_tree.py: no hidden-set file or store path can enter the sdist, the wheel, a pack digest or a pack archive; (8) a browser test for label -> adjudicate -> progress -> freeze, passing tests/test_dashboard_contrast.py. TESTS RUN BY THE VERIFIER (targeted, 11 passed, 3 skipped for Postgres): tests/test_audit.py::test_queue_holds_review_and_abstain_with_stat_first, tests/test_audit.py::test_correcting_is_an_override, tests/test_auth.py::test_reviews_and_ratings_are_recorded_for_whoever_is_signed_in, tests/test_phi.py::test_signed_in_reviewers_read_inputs_and_each_read_is_chained, tests/test_phi.py::test_only_reviewers_and_admins_read_inputs, both tests/test_cql.py agreement tests, tests/test_feedback.py::test_the_export_labels_what_reporters_agree_on, tests/test_share.py (3 tests). CROSS-UNIT FACT (belongs to A4): at this commit the inbox pack is 0.3.0, has no automation_requires, and its default safety screen is the rules variant; on the 20 held-out emergencies it detects 4 and routes 7 AUTO. IN FLIGHT, NOT AUDITED (from git log HEAD..branch subjects only): none of the four branches mentions evaluation sets or labelling. feat/dashboard-tables (62a99e49, leaderboard table, Evaluations views, audit drawer) and claude/design-c change dashboard files a labelling screen would also touch. claude/inbox-automation-gate (899cd468 and four more) concerns the AUTO-routed missed emergencies. ## A9. Scoreboard and grading service (the grading method)

### A9.cfg-1: Partial (verified); severity high; stage 3; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** Run four arms on the same cases for each pack: Mendari only (offline), + Jev, + LLM, + Jev + LLM (p17)

**Current state.** Any slot=variant configuration can be evaluated on a dataset and merged into evals/leaderboard.json, but code has no 'arm' concept. The five shipped leaderboards hold 166 rows: offline, +Jev and +LLM rows, and none that uses Jev and an LLM together. No pack declares a variant whose members include both. ai-guard, trial and prior-auth have one remote-capable slot each, so they cannot express the fourth arm; inbox and referral have two such slots, so a cross-slot mix (one slot Jev, one LLM) could be run today but never was. 'Same cases' rests on the dataset name only: build() checks the pack id and nothing else, although the spec says rows for one dataset MUST come from the same records. In referral-router every dataset table mixes rows from pack 0.1.0 and 0.1.1. Leaderboard `test` rows use the first 100 cases (of 600, or 300 for trial); a deployment caps remote evaluations at the first 200 cases.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/cli.py:280-284 - each --run configuration is evaluated on each --dataset; nothing groups configurations into arms
- src/mendari/evals/leaderboard.py:85-92 - rows keyed by (config, dataset name); only report['pack']['id'] is checked; a new report replaces the row
- docs/spec/decision-pack-0.2.md:394 - 'Rows for one dataset MUST come from the same records' (not enforced in code)
- src/mendari/server/app.py:259,875-876 - REMOTE_EVAL_LIMIT = 200; remote evaluations take dataset.head(...)
- $ scratch scan.py over packs/*/evals/leaderboard.json -> TOTAL rows 166; every dataset of every pack: '+jev+llm' 0 (e.g. inbox red_flags_holdout {'+llm': 6, 'offline': 2, '+jev': 1}); `test` rows n=100
- $ scratch packs.py over packs/*/pack.yaml -> no variant with both jev and llm members; remote-capable slots: ai-guard screen; trial notes; prior-auth notes; inbox safety_screen and router; referral specialty_reader and triage_screen
- $ scratch rerun.py: leaderboard.build() with a second report whose dataset sha256, n, pack version and digest differ -> accepted: [('...router=naive_bayes','red_flags_holdout',30,'0.3.0'), ('...router=rules','red_flags_holdout',5,'0.0.1')]
- $ scratch mix.py -> referral-router test: versions {'0.1.0': 4, '0.1.1': 5}; urgent_referrals_holdout {'0.1.0': 5, '0.1.1': 4}
- tests/test_leaderboard.py::test_cli_runs_configurations_and_merges - passes; covers explicit --run merging only

**Recommendation.** Derive an `arm` from the leaf provider types of a configuration (offline / +jev / +llm / +jev+llm). Add a composite variant holding rules, Jev and an LLM to each reference pack so the fourth arm exists in all five. Key scoreboard rows by (pack digest, dataset sha256, case-id set, configuration) and refuse to place rows that differ in any of the first three in one table. Replace the 200-case head() cap with a stratified sample or a batch path for grading runs.

**Current state.** No search exists. `mendari leaderboard` evaluates exactly the configurations passed with --run; the card and dashboard list every row. Nothing enumerates the product of declared variants or selects a best one.

### A9.cfg-3: Partial (verified); severity high; stage 3; effort S (<1 day)

**Plan says.** Record the exact configuration and every model version per run (p17)

**Current state.** Each report records pack id, version and digest; per slot the variant, type and model (local artifacts as type@hash, remote ones as the requested model name); thresholds, risk level, governance override; dataset name, sha256, n and limit. Not recorded: the model the provider says it ran (providers put it in ProviderOutput.extra, which Decision.decide never reads), engine version, gateway host, sampling settings, worker count, per-case outputs. Leaderboard rows keep only pack_version and n: no pack digest, no dataset sha256. Recorded remote models are aliases ('anthropic/claude-sonnet-5', 'anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5', 'openai/gpt-oss-120b', 'jev-1.13.0'). The version label is not enough to identify the run: all 28 inbox rows say pack 0.3.0, yet 4 of them name a naive Bayes artifact (6b28c1ac77f0) that the current 0.3.0 pack and its benchmark.json do not produce (37cb3086c82a).

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/evals/harness.py:201-216 - report pack{id,version,digest}, providers{variant,type,model}, policy, dataset{name,sha256,n,limit}
- src/mendari/providers/llm.py:202-204 and src/mendari/providers/jev.py:161 - extra = {'requested_model', 'effective_model'} per call
- src/mendari/core/decision.py:296-306 - decide() reads output.answers, failures, tokens and cost; output.extra is never read
- $ git grep -n effective_model -- src tests -> only the two provider lines and tests/test_providers.py:376
- src/mendari/evals/leaderboard.py:47-54 - row keeps config, providers, dataset name, n, report_id, created_at, pack_version
- $ scratch rerun.py -> 'row has pack digest: False | row has dataset sha256: False'
- $ scratch finger.py -> inbox: leaderboard fingerprint naive_bayes@6b28c1ac77f0 not produced by the current pack (naive_bayes@37cb3086c82a), 4/28 rows; referral: naive_bayes@83eb48931892 vs 250e71295c44, 4/36 rows
- $ grep -n temperature packs/*/pack.yaml -> no match (no sampling setting is pinned or recorded)

**Recommendation.** Carry ProviderOutput.extra through DecisionResult and write into every report the effective model per slot (each value seen, with counts), engine version, provider host, sampling settings, calibration file hash, worker count and seeds. Put pack digest and dataset sha256 in every scoreboard row. Require dated model snapshots for graded runs where the provider offers them.

### A9.data-1: Missing (verified); severity blocker; stage 4; effort XL (>2 weeks)

**Plan says.** Rank only on frozen hidden sets from A8, held-out and shifted (p17)

**Current state.** No frozen or hidden set mechanism exists in source. The 'holdout' sets are files inside each pack (and inside its signed archive), hold 24-30 cases, and are readable by anyone with the repository. The 'shifted' sets are the synthetic datasets/*-local-site-example.jsonl files, also in the repository. Every dataset, including the template `test` set, is ranked; the dashboard only pre-selects the `_holdout` one. The code ranks on non-hidden sets, which the plan forbids, but the accurate summary is that the hidden-set mechanism does not exist.

**Evidence.**

- $ git grep -n -i -E 'frozen set|hidden[_ -]set|held[_ -]out|holdout' -- 'src/*.py' 'src/*.js' scripts -> only dashboard/leaderboard.js:21,23 (dataset name suffix) and three provider docstrings about calibration splits

- src/mendari/cli.py:407-411 - the shifted 'local-site-example' sets are files under datasets/
- docs/roadmap.md:97-98 - (lead) 'provider leaderboards and the providers chosen from them': the in-repo holdouts already informed provider choice

**Recommendation.** Build after A8. Scoreboard code should accept only sets whose lifecycle state is frozen, read them through the grading role, and store set id and content hash in each result. Treat today's in-repo holdouts and site examples as public regression sets; they cannot become hidden sets. Clinician labelling of the new sets is the owner's part (A8).

**Unit notes.** Skeptic verdict: the auditor's findings hold. Every measurement I re-ran reproduced (166 rows, 105 from older pack versions, no Jev + LLM row, 4/20 with 7 automated, TypeError on unknown cost, build() accepting mismatched rows, re-run identical except id and latency, all Clopper-Pearson, McNemar, power and selection figures). No status was overturned. Changes: one severity lowered (A9.stat-1), five stages moved from 3 to 4, one item split, several claims corrected, two plan defects added. Result: 38 items: 6 Done, 11 Partial, 19 Missing, 2 Contradicts. A9 is almost entirely unbuilt. What exists is a per-configuration evaluation report and a provider leaderboard of point estimates. No interval, significance test, multiplicity adjustment, evidence gate, scope sentence, result signing, staleness or submission flow exists in source. Direct answers: ECE uses 10 equal-width bins. No interval of any kind is computed. The code does not blend; the card sorts by accuracy alone and the dashboard by worst critical detection, then accuracy, then cost. scipy and statsmodels are not dev dependencies and are not installed. Positives per critical label today: held-out sets 0-20; template test sets 6-164. New findings from this pass: (1) 8 leaderboard rows name a local model artifact the current pack does not produce, 4 of them under the current version label, so pack_version cannot identify a run; (2) the false-automation rate is null in 123 of 166 shipped rows; (3) leaderboard rows drop the denominators of accuracy and false automation; (4) ai-guard's component critical label unsafe_advice shows 102 of 164 while the pack blocks 164 of 164, so 'critical-label recall' needs a decision-level definition before it can be criterion 1. Cross-unit: shareable() still carries the ids of missed critical cases to the registry (principles and A11). Not verified: no Jev or LLM arm was run (no network, no keys), so remote rows are read as shipped data; browser tests were read, not run. All statistics were computed with the standard library (scipy absent); the ECE simulation is seeded and its size depends on the assumed confidence distribution. The owner's launch budget figures come from session memory, not the repository. Tests run: tests/test_evals.py, test_leaderboard.py, test_gate.py, test_share.py -> 32 passed, 1 skipped. In flight, not audited (git log HEAD..branch only): claude/inbox-automation-gate (5 commits, 'Inbox automation gate, and Mendari + Jev wherever Jev is set up'), feat/dashboard-tables (1, 'leaderboard as a real table'), claude/community-packs (7), claude/design-c (3). The first two touch this unit's surfaces. Isolation: all scripts and pytest temp files were written under scratchpad tmp/A9-skeptic; Python ran with bytecode writing off. `git status --short` prints nothing at e55ed48c. The ignored var/mendari.db (dated 08:56) was there before this session; I did not open or change it.

### A10.1a: Contradicts the plan (verified); severity blocker; stage 4; effort M (1-3 days) for the card and labels; L (1-2 weeks) with an isolated benchmark re-run

**Plan says.** Registry recomputes every Decision Card, benchmark and risk level from the pack itself and its public test sets; uploader-supplied cards and benchmarks are ignored (p19 item 1).

**Current state.** Publish stores, and every pack answer and the Hub page show, the uploader's own files: the whole DECISION_CARD.md as card_markdown (no size bound short of the 50 MB per-file archive cap), three scalars from evals/benchmark.json, and the whole evals/leaderboard.json (up to 1 MB). Only the risk field, questions, standards and the digest come from pack.yaml. Those three files are outside the pack digest, so forging them leaves the digest unchanged. Nothing is recomputed: the registry never calls render_card and never runs an evaluation, and the suite asserts the uploaded benchmark and leaderboard are 'shown as they are'. The docstring on describe() says 'never from the uploader', which is untrue for these fields. Reproduced independently: a risk-2 pack with a card saying risk 1 and 'AUTO permitted', accuracy 1.0 on n=1,000,000 and a forged leaderboard published with 201 and is served and searchable as such. Skeptic addition: the engine's render_card is not a clean source either. It reads the same uploader files (benchmark and leaderboard) and prints the pack's self-claimed publisher, so a card rendered with it for a pack with forged attestations showed the forged dataset name, n=1000000 and 100.0% accuracy, and 'published by Mayo Clinic (institutional)' for a pack in a community namespace.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/hub/registry.py:369 - docstring: 'from the pack itself, never from the uploader'
- src/mendari/hub/registry.py:371-377 - describe() reads evals/benchmark.json, evals/leaderboard.json and DECISION_CARD.md through pack.attestation
- src/mendari/hub/registry.py:394-402 - benchmark, leaderboard and card_markdown stored from those files; :383 - risk level taken from the manifest
- src/mendari/core/pack.py:29-30 - evals/ and DECISION_CARD.md are excluded from the pack digest
- src/mendari/core/card.py:60-61,66-67,77-78,149,154-164 - render_card reads the pack's benchmark and leaderboard attestations and prints m.publisher.name and m.publisher.type
- tests/test_registry.py::test_a_shipped_benchmark_and_leaderboard_are_shown_as_they_are - the suite asserts the uploaded benchmark and leaderboard are shown unchanged
- hub/app/packs/[namespace]/[name]/page.tsx:37,48,77 - page shows latest.benchmark, the leaderboard rows and latest.card_markdown
- $ .venv/bin/python <skeptic>/run.py s1.py -> 'digest unchanged by forgery: True', 'PUT forged: 201', "registry risk field: {'category': 'clinical support', 'level': 2}", 'served card == uploaded forged card: True', 'served card says risk 1: True | says AUTO permitted: True', 'served card == render_card: False', "benchmark served: {'accuracy': 1.0, 'dataset': 'hidden multi-site clinical validation set', 'n': 1000000} | true (acc, n): (0.9766666666666667, 600)"; search risk=2 lists the pack with the forged benchmark
- $ .venv/bin/python <skeptic>/run.py s2.py -> 'render_card lines that differ between true pack and forged-attestation pack: 112 of 395'; the forged render shows 'Last validation | 2026-09-30 on `hidden multi-site clinical validation set` (n=1000000' and '`verdict` accuracy | 100.0%'
- $ .venv/bin/python <skeptic>/run.py s4.py -> "namespace publisher_type (registry-set): community | claimed_publisher: {'name': 'Mayo Clinic', 'type': 'institutional'}"; render_card header line: 'published by Mayo Clinic (institutional)'

**Recommendation.** Step 1 (small): render the card in the registry from the manifest, with the uploaded attestations left out (give render_card a way to take no report and no leaderboard, or registry-computed ones) and with the publisher line taken from the namespace record, not from pack.yaml. Drop the uploaded card, or refuse a publish whose card differs. Calling render_card(pack) as it is today is not enough: it re-reads the uploader's benchmark and leaderboard. Step 2: stop showing the uploaded benchmark and leaderboard as fact. Either label them 'publisher's claim, not checked', or re-run the steps the pull-request route already runs (.github/workflows/packs.yml:43-54: validate, test, card, eval on evaluation.benchmark_dataset) in an isolated, time-limited job and store that result as 'registry-computed on the publisher's own test set'. Cap card size. Fix the docstring and rewrite the test that asserts uploaded attestations are shown.

### A10.2a: Partial (verified); severity blocker; stage 4; effort L (1-2 weeks), after A6

**Plan says.** Per-user publishing tokens bound to a claimed namespace, replacing admin-only publishing (p19 item 2).

**Current state.** Built: random publisher tokens bound to one namespace, stored as SHA-256, enforced on publish and key registration (tested). Not built: tokens are per namespace, not per user (no user, expiry or revoked column; no list or revoke route); namespaces cannot be claimed, only created by the holder of one static admin bearer token from an environment variable; that admin token still issues tokens, adds its own signing key to any namespace and publishes into it. A token alone registers a brand-new signing key and publishes with it, so the signature adds nothing against a stolen token, and neither the token nor the key can then be revoked. With no admin token set, the admin routes are closed (401). Token prefix is still 'ohr_' from the old project name.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/hub/registry.py:75-79 - hub_tokens: token_sha256, namespace, created_at only
- src/mendari/hub/registry.py:188-196 - issue_token: 'ohr_' + token_urlsafe(32), stored hashed
- src/mendari/hub/registry.py:510-515 - require_publisher: the admin token passes for any namespace
- src/mendari/hub/registry.py:526-547 - namespace creation, publisher type and token issue are admin-only; add_key needs only the namespace token
- tests/test_registry.py::test_publishing_needs_the_namespaces_token
- tests/test_registry.py::test_tokens_are_stored_hashed
- $ .venv/bin/python <skeptic>/run.py s1.py -> 'publisher token creates namespace: 401', 'admin adds own key to namespace: 201', 'admin publishes with it: 201', 'token alone registers a brand-new key: 201', '... and publishes with it: 201', 'DELETE key: 404 | DELETE tokens: 405', "hub_tokens cols: ['token_sha256', 'namespace', 'created_at']"
- $ .venv/bin/python <skeptic>/run.py s5.py -> 'no admin token configured -> POST /v1/namespaces with empty bearer: 401 | with any bearer: 401'

**Recommendation.** After A6: tie tokens to a signed-in user and organization (owner, created_at, last_used, expires_at, revoked_at), add self-service claim, list and revoke routes, and scope the admin credential to review actions only (no publishing, no key registration). Require a signed-in session, not just the token, to add or remove a signing key. Token and key revocation do not depend on A6 and can be built now.

### A10.3a: Missing (verified); severity high; stage 4; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** Add rate limits (p19 item 3).

**Current state.** The registry app has no limiter and no middleware at all (the engine's Limiter in server/limits.py is not used). Unlimited anonymous reads and unlimited token and admin-token guesses. Request bodies on the JSON routes are read and validated before any token check (the archive upload does check the token first). GET /v1/search, /v1/health and /v1/namespaces/{ns} load every version's full metadata on every call, and a card has no size bound: a 4 MB card published, sits in the metadata row and makes that pack's answer 4 MB (search still answered in about 8 ms with one such row, so this is a scaling risk, not a measured slowdown). The publish handler is async and runs verification, extraction and pack loading on the event loop. A bearer token with a non-ASCII character makes the admin and publisher routes answer 500 (hmac.compare_digest raises TypeError). The Hub reads the registry uncached on every page view. The Vercel firewall rule and the nginx template cover only the engine's /auth/ and /smart/.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/hub/registry.py:496 - FastAPI app created with no middleware; the file does not import mendari.server.limits
- src/mendari/hub/registry.py:331-349,523,552 - latest() does SELECT * FROM hub_versions for search, health and the namespace answer
- src/mendari/hub/registry.py:450-456 - _text reads the whole card, no cap
- src/mendari/hub/registry.py:507,512 - hmac.compare_digest on the raw bearer string
- src/mendari/hub/registry.py:556-565 - async def publish calls store.publish synchronously (token checked at 557, before the body is read)
- hub/lib/registry.ts:80 - fetch with cache: 'no-store'
- deploy/vercel/firewall-rules.json:8-9 - rule covers /auth/ and /smart/ only; deploy/onprem/nginx-limits.conf:39-45 likewise
- $ .venv/bin/python <skeptic>/run.py s1.py -> '150 GET /v1/search: {200: 150}', '150 admin guesses: {401: 150}', '150 publisher-token guesses: {403: 150}', 'malformed body, no token: 422', 'middleware stack: []'
- $ .venv/bin/python <skeptic>/run.py s4.py -> non-ASCII bearer: 'POST /v1/namespaces: 500', 'POST /v1/namespaces/stranger/keys: 500', 'PUT /v1/packs/stranger/x/1.0.0: 500'; '4 MB card publishes: 201 | largest metadata row bytes: 4061297 | GET /v1/search 8 ms'; 'GET pack answer bytes: 4056487'; 'PUT endpoint is a coroutine function: True'
- $ .venv/bin/python <skeptic>/run.py s5.py -> 'TypeError - comparing strings with non-ASCII characters is not supported'

**Recommendation.** Reuse the engine's database-backed Limiter: per address on reads and failed auth, per token on publish, key and report routes, with Retry-After. Check the token before reading a JSON body, cap JSON body size, cap card size, and keep card and leaderboard out of the rows that search and health read. Compare tokens as bytes so a malformed header is a 401, never a 500. Run publish work off the event loop. Add a firewall rule for the registry and Hub hosts.

### A10.3b: Missing (verified); severity high; stage 4; effort S (<1 day) for the registry; M (1-3 days) for the Hub with a working Next.js CSP

**Plan says.** Add security headers: CSP, HSTS, frame-ancestors, on the registry API and the Hub (p19 item 3).

**Current state.** Registry API responses carry only content-type and content-length (plus x-archive-sha256 on archives); the app has no middleware, sends no HSTS even when the request says it was forwarded over HTTPS, and leaves /docs, /redoc and /openapi.json open. The Next.js Hub has no headers() in next.config.ts and no middleware, proxy or vercel.json file; the only hardening is poweredByHeader: false. The engine has all of these headers, so the code to reuse exists.

**Evidence.**

- hub/next.config.ts:4-7 - config holds only poweredByHeader and reactStrictMode
- $ git ls-files hub -> 17 files; no middleware.ts, proxy.ts or vercel.json
- src/mendari/server/app.py:1507-1510,1931-1936,1967 - the engine sets CSP, HSTS (off local hosts), X-Frame-Options, nosniff and frame-ancestors 'none'; the registry does not import them
- $ .venv/bin/python <skeptic>/run.py s1.py -> every route answers with content-type only (the archive adds x-archive-sha256); 'health with x-forwarded-proto https -> HSTS: None'; '/docs 200', '/openapi.json 200', '/redoc 200'; 'middleware stack: []'
- $ git grep -n -i -E 'content-security-policy|strict-transport|frame-ancestors|x-frame|nosniff|referrer-policy' -- hub src/mendari/hub (lockfile excluded) -> no output

**Recommendation.** Registry: one middleware setting nosniff, frame-ancestors 'none', a default-src 'none' CSP for JSON, HSTS when served over HTTPS, and Content-Disposition: attachment on archives; close /docs in production. Hub: headers() in next.config.ts with a nonce or hash CSP (default-src 'self'; img-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none'), HSTS, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy. img-src 'self' also stops a card from loading remote images.
