### A10.4a: Missing (inferred); severity medium; stage 4; effort S (<1 day)

**Plan says.** Hub website renders Decision Card tables correctly (p19 item 4).

**Current state.** Fails today. A forged card, benchmark and leaderboard are stored and served word for word; the only correct value on the page is the risk badge, which reads pack.yaml. A card rendered by today's render_card would still fail this acceptance, because that function reads the uploader's benchmark and leaderboard (see A10.1a).

**Recommendation.** Close with A10.1a and A10.1b; make the acceptance test cover the card (risk row, validation section, publisher line), the benchmark, the leaderboard and the search answer, not the card's risk row alone.

### A10.x-signature: Partial (verified); severity high; stage 4; effort L (1-2 weeks)

**Plan says.** Audit brief: signature verification on pull: who signs, which key is trusted, key distribution and rotation, behaviour on a bad or missing signature.

**Current state.** Verification itself is sound and tested: the publisher signs the archive manifest with their own Ed25519 key; pull checks the registry-recorded archive hash, every file hash, the signature, the id and version, and the pack digest before anything reaches the cache; a missing signature, wrong signature bytes, an unknown key, algorithm 'none' and any file changed after signing (card included) are all refused. The trust model is weak for a public registry: the key is fetched from the same registry that serves the archive and pinned on first use, so a wrong or compromised registry is trusted on first contact; there is no Mendari or registry signature and no key shipped with the client; --accept-new-key pins every key the registry lists; keys and pins can never be revoked (no route, no CLI command); a plain-http, non-local registry URL is accepted; Decision.from_hub pulls on its own from the default registry when a pack is not local. A pulled pack replaces a bundled pack of the same id, at a higher version and also at the same version, because the pull cache is searched before the bundled packs and the first found wins a tie.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/hub/archive.py:130-148 - build signs the manifest with the publisher's key
- src/mendari/hub/archive.py:176-196 - no manifest or signature, untrusted key, bad signature all raise HubError
- src/mendari/hub/client.py:210-216 - keys, archive hash, verify, id and version checked before extract
- src/mendari/hub/client.py:232-249 - keys come from client.namespace() on the same registry; pinned when nothing is pinned or with accept_new_key (all listed keys)
- src/mendari/hub/client.py:98-110 - no scheme check on the registry URL
- src/mendari/core/registry.py:27-37,80 - pull cache is searched before bundled packs; max() over versions returns the first found at a tie
- src/mendari/server/app.py:354-364 - the server serves discover(...) and replaces a pack only for a strictly greater version
- src/mendari/core/decision.py:213-229 - Decision.from_hub pulls from the default registry when the pack is not local
- tests/test_hub_client.py:170-171 - first pull from HostileRegistry with its own key succeeds and pins
- tests/test_hub_client.py::test_a_rotated_key_needs_consent
- tests/test_archive.py::test_a_changed_manifest_breaks_the_signature
- $ .venv/bin/python <skeptic>/run.py s3.py -> 'signature file missing: refused', 'signature bytes wrong: refused', 'signed by a stranger's key: refused', 'policy.yaml changed after signing: refused', 'algorithm none: refused', 'card changed after signing: refused - DECISION_CARD.md does not match the manifest'; 'pull over http://registry.example.org succeeded', pins 1 key; a version signed by a newly added key is refused until accept_new_key, then pins 2
- $ .venv/bin/python <skeptic>/run.py s3.py -> 'resolve before pull is the bundled one: True | after pull resolves to cache copy (same version): True'; "resolve_pack('mendari/referral-router') now: 9.9.9 | from cache: True"
- $ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_registry.py tests/test_hub_client.py tests/test_archive.py -p no:cacheprovider --basetemp <skeptic>/pytest-tmp -rs -> '76 passed, 20 skipped in 11.12s' (the 20 skips are the Postgres parameter of tests/test_registry.py)

**Recommendation.** Add a registry signing key whose public half ships in the client: the registry counter-signs each accepted version (id, version, digest, archive hash, publisher key id, review status, time) and the client checks it, so a key no longer has to be trusted because the same server listed it. Add key revocation with a chained event and a client check, a command to list and remove pins, refuse non-HTTPS registries except localhost, and reserve bundled ids (the mendari namespace) so a pulled pack can never replace a bundled one at any version.

### A10.x-yank: Missing (verified); severity blocker; stage 4; effort M (1-3 days) for the registry; M (1-3 days) more for the client check

**Plan says.** Audit brief: yank semantics (the plan's item 3 assumes yank and delete events exist).

**Current state.** There is no yank, unpublish, delete, deprecate or takedown operation in the registry or the client. Versions are immutable and permanent; a pack found to be unsafe, or one holding data that must be removed, can be withdrawn only by editing the database by hand. The client has no notion of a withdrawn version and would keep using its cached copy.

**Evidence.**

- $ git grep -n -i -E 'yank|withdraw|unpublish|deprecat|takedown|tombstone|revoke|recall' -- src/mendari/hub hub/app hub/lib src/mendari/cli.py -> no output
- $ .venv/bin/python <skeptic>/run.py s1.py -> route list has GET, HEAD, POST, PUT and PATCH routes only; 'DELETE version: 405 | POST yank: 404 | DELETE key: 404 | DELETE tokens: 405 | DELETE namespace: 405'
- src/mendari/hub/client.py:204-209 - a cached verified copy is used as is, with no status check

**Recommendation.** Define and build: yank (publisher or admin; hidden from latest and search, still downloadable by exact version with a reason shown, version number never reusable), admin delete for legal or patient-data takedown (archive removed, tombstone kept), both chained events. Client: pull and server start-up check the yank status of cached versions and warn or refuse; mendari pull of a yanked version needs an explicit flag.

### A10.x-auto: Missing (verified); severity blocker; stage 4; effort M (1-3 days), partly in flight

**Plan says.** Audit brief: is a pulled pack recommend-only or can it AUTO? (Lead: tasks/todo.md Part B, community packs are recommend-only.)

**Current state.** A pulled pack can automate. The pull cache is on the pack search path, the engine serves whatever it discovers, and policy caps AUTO only by the risk level the pack's own manifest declares; nothing records or checks where a pack came from or its namespace's publisher type. Reproduced independently: a copy of the inbox pack published by a 'community' namespace, declaring risk 0, was pulled and returned AUTO on 284 of 300 of its test cases. Origin-aware loading and a recommend-only cap are in flight on claude/community-packs (commit 6a2e3b71), not audited and not in this commit.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/core/registry.py:29-32 - packs_cache() appended to search_paths()
- src/mendari/server/app.py:354 - the server serves discover(packs_paths)
- src/mendari/core/policy.py:154-156 - AUTO allowed when manifest.risk.level <= MAX_AUTONOMOUS_RISK; no origin input
- src/mendari/cli.py:808-814 - mendari pull prints 'verified and cached', no publisher-type or origin warning
- $ .venv/bin/python <skeptic>/run.py s3.py -> "published: 201 | publisher_type: community | risk: {'category': 'administrative', 'level': 0}", "outcomes on 300 of its synthetic test cases: {'AUTO': 284, 'HUMAN_REVIEW': 15, 'ABSTAIN': 1}"; the only file the pull adds is '.mendari-verified'
- $ git log --oneline HEAD..claude/community-packs -> 7 commits, among them 6a2e3b71 'origin-aware loading, recommend-only policy and named-only spend (B1, B2)' (in flight, not audited)
- tasks/todo.md:53-62 - lead: B1 and B2 unchecked at this commit

**Recommendation.** Record origin at pull (registry URL, namespace, publisher type, key id) next to the existing .mendari-verified marker, and cap any pack whose origin is a registry at HUMAN_REVIEW in core/policy.py unless the deploying organization records a governance approval for that exact digest. ## A11. Site evaluation network

### A11.1a: Missing (verified); severity blocker; stage 6; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** Site registry: each site has a signing key (p.20, item 1)

**Current state.** No site entity exists. A site is a free-text string typed by the sender (--share SITE) and stored in hub_reports.site; it is linked to no namespace and no key. The only keys the registry holds are publisher-namespace Ed25519 keys, read only when a pack archive is published. Any holder of any namespace token, or the admin token, can post under any site name: a token of an unrelated namespace posted as 'Mayo Clinic' and got HTTP 201. Reusable precursor, not a site registry: namespaces with admin-set publisher types and registered keys, and each report row records the submitting namespace (submitted_by), which GET /reports returns but the Hub page does not show.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/hub/registry.py:62-103 - SCHEMA has hub_namespaces, hub_keys, hub_tokens, hub_versions, hub_archives, hub_reports; no site table, no site key table
- src/mendari/hub/registry.py:98 - hub_reports.site is TEXT NOT NULL; :469 - ReportRequest.site is checked for length and a character pattern only
- src/mendari/hub/registry.py:609-610 - route docstring: any publisher token may submit; the site name is the site's choice
- src/mendari/hub/registry.py:172-186 and 205-212 - keys are registered per publisher namespace and read only by publish() to verify archives
- src/mendari/cli.py:1013-1015 - --share takes a free-text SITE
- $ python scratchpad/tmp/A11-skeptic/verify.py -> '2c other namespace token + site 'Mayo Clinic' + forged signature field -> HTTP 201 'Mayo Clinic''; public row ('Mayo Clinic', submitted_by 'stranger', n 30, accuracy 0.95)
- $ git grep -n -i -E 'site_key|hub_sites|site registry|sign_report|verify_report' -- src hub/app hub/lib scripts tests -> no matches

**Recommendation.** Add hub_sites (site id, display name, verified flag, owning organization from A6) and hub_site_keys (Ed25519 public key, created and revoked timestamps), admin-verified like publisher types. --share must name a registered site id, not free text, and the token used must belong to that site. Reuse hub/archive.py key helpers (generate_key, key_id, load_public_key) and the keys generate / keys register commands. Checking that a key really belongs to the named health system is an owner step the plan omits.

### A11.1b: Missing (verified); severity blocker; stage 6; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** Shared results are signed and verified on receipt (p.20, item 1)

**Current state.** Nothing is signed. The client posts plain JSON {site, report} with a bearer token. The receiver authenticates the token only, has no signature field, silently ignores unknown top-level fields (a made-up 'signature' and 'key_id' were accepted) and accepts the identical body any number of times.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/hub/client.py:163-171 - share_report posts json={'site': site, 'report': shareable(report)}; no signing step
- src/mendari/hub/registry.py:468-470 - ReportRequest has only site and report; no signature, key id, nonce or timestamp; unknown fields are not forbidden
- src/mendari/hub/registry.py:611-618 - the add_report route checks only that some registry token is present, then a 2 MB size cap
- $ python scratchpad/tmp/A11-skeptic/verify.py (real `mendari eval ... --share 'Skeptic Site'` over loopback, body captured by an ASGI wrapper) -> request headers [accept, accept-encoding, authorization, connection, content-length, content-type, host, user-agent]; body keys ['report', 'site']
- $ python scratchpad/tmp/A11-skeptic/verify.py -> '2c ... forged signature field -> HTTP 201'; '2d identical body twice -> HTTP 201, 201'; '2e no token -> HTTP 401'

**Recommendation.** Sign the canonical JSON bytes of the payload with the site key (detached Ed25519 signature plus key id, as archive.build does for manifests at src/mendari/hub/archive.py:130-147). Put a registry-issued nonce and the published pack digest inside the signed bytes. The receiver verifies against the site's registered keys, rejects unknown or revoked keys, a body that does not match the signature and a reused nonce, and stores the signature with the row.

### A11.2a: Partial (verified); severity high; stage 6; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** `mendari eval --share SITE` sends a versioned, metrics-only payload: counts, confusion matrices, calibration bins, configuration and model versions, pack digest, dataset size and a dataset hash (p.20, item 2)

**Current state.** The command exists, is wired to the CLI and works end to end (one passing test; I ran the real CLI against a scratch registry and captured the body). Field by field against the plan: counts - sent (outcome_counts, per-label support, critical n/detected/auto_missed, threshold-sweep error counts); confusion matrices - sent per question; calibration bins - sent, but only bins with at least 10 cases while ECE is still the all-bin value; configuration and model versions - providers{slot:{variant,type,model}} with fingerprints such as 'rules@661449489daf' plus policy risk level and thresholds, but no engine version and no flag saying whether a provider was remote; pack digest - sent, not checked by the receiver; dataset size - sent as dataset.n, with a --limit run not marked as partial; dataset hash - not sent (see A11.2a-hash). Versioned - only the report's own 'mendari.eval/1' string, which the receiver never checks ('bogus/9' and a report holding nothing but the pack id and version both got HTTP 201). Also sent and not in the plan's list: rates, latency percentiles, cost and token totals, error-code counts, subgroup cells. Not metrics-only: record ids travel in decisions.critical[].missed_ids (A11.2b-ids).

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/cli.py:162-165 - `if args.share:` builds a registry client and calls registry.share_report(report, args.share); :1013-1016 - the --share SITE and --registry arguments
- src/mendari/evals/share.py:17-28 - _KEPT, the top-level allow-list; :42 - dataset reduced to {'n': ...}; :38-39 - small bins dropped, ece kept
- tests/test_hub_client.py::test_eval_share_sends_the_metrics - passes (my targeted run of tests/test_share.py plus the two report tests: 5 passed, 1 skipped; the skip is the Postgres variant of the registry test)
- $ python scratchpad/tmp/A11-skeptic/verify.py -> 'exit 0 | stderr: shared with the registry as Skeptic Site (metrics only)'; report keys [cost, dataset, decisions, errors, format, latency_ms, pack, policy, primary, providers, questions, subgroups, threshold_sweep]; 'local keys not sent: [created_at, id, misclassified]'; 'dataset sent: {'n': 30}'
- $ python scratchpad/tmp/A11-skeptic/verify.py -> string leaves on the wire: format 'mendari.eval/1', pack.id, pack.version, pack.digest, primary, providers.*.{variant,type,model}, critical[].question/label, critical[].missed_ids[] = 'ENC-900100'
- $ python scratchpad/tmp/A11-skeptic/verify.py -> '2g format 'bogus/9' -> HTTP 201'; '2h report with nothing but pack id/version -> HTTP 201'; '2f wrong digest, accuracy 1.0, n=1e9 -> HTTP 201'

**Recommendation.** Define a dedicated payload (for example format 'mendari.site-eval/1') built from counts only: per-question confusion counts, per-critical-label TP/FN/auto-missed counts, outcome counts, calibration bin counts and confidence sums, provider configuration with a remote flag per slot, engine version, pack digest, dataset n, whether the run was limited, and a keyed dataset commitment (see the plan defect on the hash). Drop latency, cost and threshold_sweep or declare them. The receiver checks the format string and that the digest is the published version's.

### A11.2a-hash: Contradicts the plan (verified); severity low; stage 6; effort S (<1 day)

**Plan says.** The payload carries a dataset hash (p.20, item 2)

**Current state.** The code does the opposite on purpose. The local report holds the SHA-256 of the site's file; shareable() removes it together with the dataset name, and a test asserts that neither leaves ('no name, no digest'). A build session that follows the plan literally would have to delete that assertion, which the plan's own shared header forbids ('Never weaken an existing safety rule, cap or check to make a test pass', p.6). The code's position is the safer one; the plan needs correcting before A11 is built (see plan_defects).

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/evals/harness.py:89 - sha256=hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest() over the raw dataset file; :211-216 - the local report's dataset block holds name, sha256, n, limit
- src/mendari/evals/share.py:42 - shared['dataset'] = {'n': ...}
- tests/test_share.py:20 - assert shared['dataset'] == {'n': BENCHMARK['dataset']['n']} # no name, no digest
- $ python scratchpad/tmp/A11-skeptic/verify.py -> 'dataset sent: {'n': 30}'

**Recommendation.** Do not send the raw file hash. Decide, in the plan, on a keyed commitment (HMAC-SHA-256 of the file under a secret the site keeps) so the registry can spot an identical re-submission and the site can later prove which file it used, and keep the existing assertion that the plain digest and the dataset name stay home.

### A11.2b: Contradicts the plan (verified); severity blocker; stage 6; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** No case content, no identifiers, no free text; enforced by a schema that rejects any extra field (p.20, item 2)

**Current state.** There is no closed schema on either side. The sender filter is a top-level key allow-list that copies nested objects whole; the receiver's request model is report: dict[str, Any] and it re-applies the same filter. On the real CLI path two site-derived strings leave: record ids in decisions.critical[].missed_ids, and subgroup keys, which are raw attribute values from the site's file. Through the Python API or a hand-built request, anything inside a kept object leaves and is stored: of 8 places where I put a line of case text, 7 survived the sender filter and 7 were stored by the registry with HTTP 201 (extra key in pack, extra key in a question, providers.*.model, an errors key, a subgroup key, missed_ids, governance_override.reference); only the unknown top-level key was dropped. policy.governance_override (approved_by, reference) is passed through by both sides when present; the CLI eval path sends None there because it builds the Decision without governance.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/evals/harness.py:180-184 - missed_ids = [r['id'] ...]; src/mendari/evals/share.py:23 and :32 - 'decisions' is copied whole
- src/mendari/evals/share.py:31-49 - shareable(): allow-list at the top level only; questions copied with dict(question); no type or key validation
- src/mendari/hub/registry.py:468-470 - ReportRequest.report: dict[str, Any]; :302 - the receiver calls the same shareable()
- src/mendari/evals/harness.py:276 - subgroup key is str(record['attributes'][attribute]); src/mendari/core/spec.py:403 - a pack declares subgroup attribute names only, no allowed values
- src/mendari/core/policy.py:28-29 and src/mendari/evals/harness.py:209 - approved_by and reference sit inside policy.governance_override; src/mendari/cli.py:25-28 - the CLI builds the Decision without governance
- $ git grep -n -E 'extra\s*=|additionalProperties|ConfigDict|model_config' -- src/mendari/hub src/mendari/evals -> no matches
- $ python scratchpad/tmp/A11-skeptic/verify.py -> 'sender filter keeps the text in 7 of 8 places'; '2b tainted -> HTTP 201; rows 1->2; copies stored: 7; approved_by stored: True'
- $ python scratchpad/tmp/A11-skeptic/verify.py -> real CLI run: subgroup values sent {language: [en], channel: [unknown], age_band: [unknown], topic: [control]} (values read from the site's file)

**Recommendation.** Replace shareable() with closed models used by both client and registry: pydantic models with extra='forbid', strict ints and floats and bounded lists, or a JSON Schema with additionalProperties false (jsonschema is already a runtime dependency, pyproject.toml). Every string is an enum or a pattern: question names and labels validated against the published pack's manifest, subgroup attribute names and values against a pack-declared vocabulary (unknown values folded into 'other'), digests as hex, model ids by pattern. No free-form dict anywhere. Remove missed_ids, the governance approver and reference, and error-code keys that are not in the engine's fixed list.

### A11.2b-ids: Contradicts the plan (verified); severity blocker; stage 3; effort S (<1 day)

**Plan says.** No identifiers leave the site (p.20, item 2); the shipped docs, README, module docstring and Hub page already promise it

**Current state.** A defect in shipped behaviour, separate from building A11. `mendari eval --share` sends the dataset's record ids whenever a critical-label case is missed, and the registry stores them in hub_reports.report. In my real CLI run on a 30-case file with ids ENC-9001xx, 16 ids were on the wire and 16 were stored. When a record has no id the harness assigns '<file name stem>-<line number>', so the dataset's file name leaves too. The ids are not returned by the public GET /reports (it returns summary numbers only), so the exposure is to whoever runs the registry and its database, not to every reader. The existing test passes only because it uses the referral-router benchmark, whose missed_ids lists are empty. Nothing else in src/ or hub/ reads missed_ids, so dropping it from the shared payload breaks nothing. At a real site the JSONL id is likely an MRN, encounter or message id. README line 547 says there is no public registry yet, which limits who receives ids today to registries a site or partner runs.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/evals/harness.py:180-184 - missed_ids built from record ids; :81 - record.setdefault('id', f'{path.stem}-{number}')
- src/mendari/evals/share.py:1-9 - docstring: shared reports keep metrics, 'never cases', and names case ids as what is removed; :17-28 - 'decisions' kept whole
- docs/deploying-with-phi.md:456 - 'Metrics only; no cases, ids or small groups'; README.md:574-575 - '--share sends a site's metrics, never its cases'; hub/app/packs/[namespace]/[name]/page.tsx:53 - caption 'metrics only; no cases leave a site' (leads; the code contradicts them)
- tests/test_share.py:15-21 - checks only ids from BENCHMARK['misclassified']; $ python (reads packs/*/evals/benchmark.json) -> referral-router critical missed_ids 0 and 0; ai-guard unsafe_advice 62; clinical-trial-prescreener 1 and 1
- $ python scratchpad/tmp/A11-skeptic/verify.py (real CLI, inbox pack, default offline providers, its red_flags_holdout cases re-id'd ENC-9001xx) -> critical ('urgency', 'urgent', n 20, detected 4, auto_missed 7, missed_ids 16); 'record ids on the wire: 16 of 30'; 'record ids stored in hub_reports.report: 16'; 'public GET /reports exposes ids: False'
- $ git grep -l missed_ids (excluding packs/*/evals) -> src/mendari/evals/harness.py only

**Recommendation.** In shareable(), rebuild each critical entry from its counts (question, label, n, detected, auto_missed) and drop missed_ids. Add a test that evaluates a dataset with missed critical cases (the inbox pack's red_flags_holdout misses 16 of 20 with default providers) and asserts that no record id and no dataset file stem appears in json.dumps(payload), and a registry test that a posted missed_ids list is not stored. Correct the docs until the fix lands. Small enough to do before any partner is given a registry token; it must not wait for the rest of A11, because A2 (deliver what the docs promise) gates stage 3.

### A11.3: Partial (verified); severity blocker; stage 6; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** Suppress any cell under 10 (the existing default) before sending (p.20, item 3)

**Current state.** The existing default is MIN_GROUP = 10 in evals/share.py. It is applied to two things only, on both sender and receiver: subgroup cells (by the cell's n) and calibration bins. It is not applied to confusion-matrix cells, per-label support, outcome_counts, critical n/detected/auto_missed, threshold-sweep error counts, automation.n or review.n, nor to rates inside a kept subgroup whose own denominator is small (false_automation_rate is over the cell's AUTO cases only). There is no complementary suppression: dataset n is sent and every record falls in exactly one cell per attribute, so the total of the suppressed cells is always derivable and a single suppressed cell is recovered exactly; ECE is sent as computed over all bins, so the dropped bins' total n and their error mass are recovered exactly. Suppressed cells are dropped without a marker. There is no minimum dataset size: a 1-case evaluation is shareable and gives that case's true label, prediction and outcome.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/evals/share.py:16 - MIN_GROUP = 10; :38 - calibration bins filtered; :39 - ece kept unchanged; :44-47 - subgroup cells filtered; nothing else is filtered
- tests/test_share.py:24-38 - tests subgroup and bin dropping and asserts ECE is unchanged
- src/mendari/evals/harness.py:276-277 - each record goes to exactly one value per attribute (default 'unknown'); :294-296 - false_automation_rate divides by the cell's AUTO count, which is not sent
- src/mendari/standards/omop.py:413-419 - a second min_cell=10 default (nulls cells in the OMOP population report); src/mendari/evals/compare.py:8 - a different MIN_GROUP = 15
- $ python scratchpad/tmp/A11-skeptic/verify.py (inbox pack on datasets/local-site-example.jsonl, n 400) -> 'confusion cells 1..9 sent: 6', e.g. (destination, front_desk, billing, 1); outcome_counts ABSTAIN 9 sent; threshold_sweep errors [19, 10, 0, ...]
- $ python scratchpad/tmp/A11-skeptic/verify.py -> 'subgroup topic: 20 cells dropped locally; recoverable total from payload = dataset n - sent = 101'; age_band, language and channel on this file have no cell under 10 (so the exact single-cell recovery is shown by the code, not by this file)
- $ python scratchpad/tmp/A11-skeptic/verify.py -> 'calibration urgency: local bins n=[2, 10, 372, 16] sent n=[10, 372, 16]; recovered dropped n=2, recovered mass=0.9003 actual=0.9003'; 'calibration destination: local bins n=[5, 7, 13, 11, 5, 4, 355] sent n=[13, 11, 355]; recovered dropped n=21, recovered mass=2.5862 actual=2.5862'
- $ python scratchpad/tmp/A11-skeptic/verify.py -> 'n=1 share: {'n': 1} [(destination, medical_assistant, medical_assistant, 1), (urgency, routine, routine, 1)]'

**Recommendation.** Write one suppression function over the typed payload that walks every count, with a written rule per field (see the plan defect: blanket suppression of error cells under 10 hides the missed-emergency counts the network exists to measure, and breaks pooling). Add complementary suppression for margins, recompute ECE over the bins that are sent or merge small bins into neighbours, mark suppressed cells explicitly, refuse to share below a minimum dataset size, and share one helper with omop.population. Test by walking every integer in the payload and by showing that a table with exactly one small cell cannot be rebuilt from dataset n, question n or ECE.

### A11.x-poison: Missing (verified); severity high; stage 4; effort S (<1 day)

**Plan says.** Not a numbered requirement; follows from 'verified on receipt' (p.20, item 1) and concerns the receiving endpoint that already ships

**Current state.** The report endpoint does not validate the report's shape and inserts the row before it computes the summary. A report whose 'primary' is a list, whose 'decisions' is a list, or whose calibration is a number returns HTTP 500 to the sender, yet the row is committed; from then on GET /v1/packs/{ns}/{name}/reports returns 500 for that pack (the pack detail route still answers 200). Shapes that fail earlier, inside shareable() (questions as a list, pack as a string, a subgroup as a list), return 500 and store nothing. The Hub pack page awaits the reports call together with the pack call and its fetch helper throws on any non-OK answer, so the page would fall to the error boundary (read from code, not run). Any namespace's token can do this to any pack, and the registry has no route to delete a report. Tokens are issued only by the admin today, which limits who can do it until per-user tokens arrive (A10 item 2).

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/hub/registry.py:302-319 - shareable(), the INSERT inside the session, then summary(shared) in the return statement; :329 - reports() calls summary() on every stored row

### A12.1a: Missing (verified); severity blocker; stage 6; effort L (1-2 weeks)

**Plan says.** Verify each EHR-signed CDS Hooks JWT against that EHR's registered JWKS: iss, aud, exp, jti replay check (p21 item 1)

**Current state.** No CDS Hooks JWT verification exists. Sign-in on: a Bearer credential that is not an ohk_ key or a mat_ token is refused 401 invalid_token on discovery and on the hook, before anything is parsed; a token the size of a real RS384 JWT (768 characters) is refused earlier still, as 'malformed', because a bearer credential may be at most 512 characters. So a real EHR cannot call at all. Open mode: the Authorization header is never read, so a forged unsigned JWT gets 200 and a card. There is no per-EHR iss/JWKS registry for CDS (MENDARI_SMART_EHRS holds base=org:level for SMART launches only). Reusable pieces: the atomic one-time claim used for jti at /auth/token. The private_key_jwt verifier is not reusable as written: it requires iss to be a 24-hex Mendari client id equal to sub, and refuses any header beyond alg/kid/typ.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/server/auth.py:577-599 - _bearer: the credential must match _BEARER, then only the ohk_ and mat_ prefixes are known; anything else raises refused_credential('unknown_prefix')
- src/mendari/server/auth.py:334 - _BEARER allows at most 512 characters
- src/mendari/server/auth.py:462-463 - settings None -> return OPEN, before any header is read
- src/mendari/server/app.py:1125-1146 - cds_invoke: no credential or JWT handling in the route
- $ probe.py (auditor's script, re-run by the verifier; TestClient, open mode) POST /cds-services/mendari.referral-router with a forged unsigned JWT -> HTTP 200, one card
- $ probe.py (sign-in on) GET /cds-services and POST hook with the same 250-character JWT -> HTTP 401, WWW-Authenticate 'Bearer realm=mendari, error=invalid_token'; security log reason unknown_prefix
- $ probe4.py (verifier; sign-in on) POST hook with an RS384-sized JWT (768 characters, jku header) -> HTTP 401; security log reason malformed
- src/mendari/server/backend_services.py:307-365 - verify_assertion (signature, aud, exp, lifetime, jti); :326-330 iss must be a 24-hex client id and sub must equal it; :77 and :321 any header beyond alg/kid/typ is refused
- src/mendari/core/audit.py:1272-1290 - smart_claim: one statement, one winner; used for jti at backend_services.py:406
- $ git grep -n -i -w jti -- src -> core/audit.py, server/backend_services.py, server/api_docs.py, standards/bulk.py (Mendari's own outbound assertion); none in cds_hooks.py or auth.py

**Recommendation.** Add a CDS client registry (per EHR: iss, JWKS by value or one pinned jwks_uri on the allow-list, organization, allowed fhirServer bases) and a third Bearer branch for JWS-shaped credentials on /cds-services only, with its own size limit (the 512-character cap must not apply): verify the signature against the registered keys (never follow a jku that is not the registered URL), iss registered, aud equal to the public URL of the endpoint called, exp and iat with skew and a maximum lifetime, jti claimed once per iss through store.smart_claim. One uniform 401; fixed-reason security-log lines. Buildable and testable now against a locally generated key pair; only the real vendor's iss and JWKS are owner-dependent.

### A12.1b: Missing (verified); severity blocker; stage 6; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** Map the verified JWT to a narrow EHR user in the registered organization (p21 item 1)

**Current state.** The narrow `ehr` principal exists only for SMART launches (launch cookie on /api/smart/*, permissions launch and launch_decide, organization from MENDARI_SMART_EHRS). A CDS Hooks call has no EHR principal. With sign-in on, the only credentials that work are a Mendari API key or mat_ token: an unscoped service key calls discovery and the hook but also reads the organization's whole audit list; a decide-scoped key calls the hook and nothing else. In open mode the caller is the OPEN admin principal with no organization. This is one deliverable with A12.1a.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/server/auth.py:113-119 - EHR_LEVELS / EHR_ONLY: launch and launch_decide only, held by kind 'ehr'
- src/mendari/server/auth.py:475-526 - the ehr principal is built only from the launch cookie's session
- src/mendari/server/auth.py:147 and :163 - POST /cds-services/{id} needs 'decide', GET /cds-services needs 'read': ordinary role permissions, no EHR-only permission
- src/mendari/server/auth.py:287-289 - OPEN principal: roles {'admin'}, no organization
- $ probe3.py (verifier; sign-in on, unscoped service key) GET /cds-services -> 200; POST hook -> 200; GET /api/audit -> 200 with the organization's decisions
- tests/test_smart_launch.py - ehr principals are tested for launches only (ran green in the targeted run)

**Recommendation.** Introduce a principal kind for a CDS client (for example kind 'cds', id cds:<hash of iss and tenant>, actor '<iss>') with exactly two permissions (cds_discover, cds_invoke), the organization from the registration, a per-principal rate limit, and requested_by in the chain. It must not reach /api or /fhir. Mirror the EHR_ONLY tests in tests/test_auth.py.

### A12.1d: Missing (verified); severity medium; stage 6; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** Add CORS for registered EHR origins (p21 item 1)

**Current state.** No CORS anywhere. A request with a foreign Origin and no Authorization header, and every preflight, is refused 403 'cross-site request refused' with no Access-Control-* headers (open mode and sign-in on). The CapabilityStatement declares cors: false and a test asserts it. The origin guard's own safety argument depends on Mendari never granting a preflight.

**Evidence.**

- $ git grep -l -i -E 'CORSMiddleware|access-control-allow|allow_origins' -- src deploy hub web (vendored JS excluded) -> no match
- src/mendari/server/origin.py:22-24 - 'another site cannot attach one without a CORS preflight, which Mendari never grants'
- src/mendari/standards/capability.py:203 and :207 - security.cors False; tests/test_backend_services.py:237 asserts it
- $ probe.py (re-run) OPTIONS /cds-services and /cds-services/{id} with Origin and Access-Control-Request-Method -> 403, no Access-Control headers (both modes)
- $ probe.py (re-run) open mode POST hook and GET discovery with Origin: https://sandbox.cds-hooks.org -> 403

**Recommendation.** Add a narrowly scoped CORS responder for /cds-services and /cds-services/* only: echo Access-Control-Allow-Origin for origins in the CDS registration, allow Authorization and Content-Type, never Allow-Credentials, and answer OPTIONS before the origin guard for those paths only. Keep every cookie-authenticated route out and keep the FHIR base at cors:false. Server-to-server EHR callers do not need it; it matters for browser-based CDS clients such as the public CDS Hooks sandbox.

### A12.1e: Partial (verified); severity high; stage 6; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** Open mode stays unauthenticated only for local sandboxes (p21 item 1)

**Current state.** Open mode exists and is unauthenticated, but nothing confines it to local hosts: it is simply 'sign-in not configured', on any host. Measured: in open mode, discovery and a hook both answer 200 with no credential when the request's Host is mendari.example.org. The container image binds 0.0.0.0 with no sign-in by default. The only locality controls are defaults outside the server: `mendari serve` binds 127.0.0.1 and docker compose publishes the engine on 127.0.0.1.

### A12.2b: Missing (verified); severity high; stage 6; effort M (1-3 days)

**Current state.** POST /cds-services/{id}/feedback does not exist: 404 in open mode, and with sign-in on a service key gets 403 because unlisted routes need admin. Cards carry no overrideReasons. ### A12.3a: Missing (verified); severity blocker; stage 6; effort L (1-2 weeks)

**Plan says.** Mappings: fetch linked DocumentReference notes (p21 item 3)

**Current state.** Notes are read only from inline base64 attachment.data. A note delivered as attachment.url (a Binary link) is silently read as no notes: no fetch, no issue, no abstention, and US Core validation raises nothing because a url-only attachment conforms. Measured through the real CDS route: a chart whose note says the patient is pregnant flips from not_eligible (no card) to a 'Possible GLYCEMIA-2 candidate' card when the same note arrives as attachment.url.

**Evidence.**

- packs/clinical-trial-prescreener/fhir/mapping.yaml:17-19 and packs/prior-auth-preflight/fhir/mapping.yaml:29-31 - notes: DocumentReference.content.attachment.data, transform base64_text
- src/mendari/standards/fhir.py:306-308 and :414-418 - base64_text decodes inline data only
- src/mendari/standards/us_core_6_1_0.json:564 - US Core accepts attachment.url or attachment.data
- src/mendari/sandbox/fhir_records.py:119 - synthetic notes are always inline data
- $ probe2.py (auditor's script, re-run by the verifier) pack example 'a pregnancy in the notes excludes the patient and is flagged': note inline -> recommendation not_eligible, cards []; the same note as attachment.url -> recommendation candidate, card 'Possible GLYCEMIA-2 candidate: confirm eligibility' (both HUMAN_REVIEW)
- $ git grep -n -E 'attachment\.url|Binary/' -- src packs (schema, vendored JS and data excluded) -> only the US Core rule text above

**Recommendation.** In the CDS and SMART fetch paths, resolve DocumentReference.content.attachment.url through the allow-listed FhirClient with the request's token (Binary read; text/plain, and text/html stripped; size and count caps; same base only). Independently, make 'a DocumentReference whose content could not be read' an explicit reason that forces HUMAN_REVIEW or ABSTAIN for packs that read notes; never treat unread notes as no notes. Handling of the vendor's real note formats (HTML, RTF, PDF) is owner- and vendor-dependent.

### A12.3b: Missing (verified); severity blocker; stage 6; effort L (1-2 weeks)

**Plan says.** Mappings: choose codes by code system (p21 item 3)

**Current state.** Nothing selects a coding by its system. The path language has dotted names, [n] and [*]; every shipped mapping reads coding[0].code, and a field mapping always takes the first value. A resource whose first coding is the site's local code is misread or ignored, in both directions. Measured through the real CDS route: a true candidate with a myocardial infarction 20 days ago stays a 'candidate' card when the Condition lists a local coding before ICD-10 (it is not_eligible when ICD-10 is first); a LOINC HbA1c behind a local code turns a candidate into needs_review; a CPT order with a local code first, and a referral whose SNOMED category is the second coding, are not recognised as the pack's focus at all (no decision, no card). A focus filter could be made order-insensitive today by dropping [0] (is_focus matches any value), but it would still be blind to the system.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/standards/fhir.py:42 and :280-299 - _SEGMENT / select: a name with an optional [n] or [*]; no system predicate
- src/mendari/standards/fhir.py:309 - value = values[0]; :153 - is_focus uses any() over the path's values
- packs/*/fhir/mapping.yaml - every code path is ...coding[0].code (trial 26, 37, 50; prior-auth 8, 17, 38, 45; referral 6, 34, 43, 52)
- $ probe.py (re-run) observation with a local coding first -> code '1558024' (the local code); 'draft order with a local code before CPT is the pack's focus: False'; 'referral whose SNOMED category is the 2nd coding is the pack's focus: False'
- $ probe2.py (re-run) candidate chart with a local coding before LOINC on labs -> needs_review instead of candidate
- packs/clinical-trial-prescreener/logic/criteria.yaml:54-62 - no_recent_cv_event: default 'yes' when no matching Condition code is seen; $ probe5.py (verifier) candidate + MI 20 days ago: ICD-10 coding first -> not_eligible, no card; local coding first -> candidate, card 'Possible GLYCEMIA-2 candidate: confirm eligibility'

**Recommendation.** Add a system-aware selector to FieldMapping and FocusFilter (for example path: code.coding with system: http://loinc.org, or a coding[system=...] segment) with an ordered list of preferred systems, and have focus_where match any coding in the named system. Convert all four mappings, add fixtures with multi-coded resources in both orders, rebuild the packs. A resource with no coding in a known system must be a recorded reason, not an absent fact. Then fit against the chosen vendor's sandbox data (owner-dependent).

### A12.3c: Missing (verified); severity high; stage 6; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** Mappings: read the payer by Coverage reference (p21 item 3)

**Current state.** The payer is the literal Coverage.payor[0].identifier.value, compared with the pack's two synthetic labels ('acme', 'beacon') hard-coded in pack logic. Nothing resolves payor.reference or maps an Organization to a payer label. A Coverage whose payor is a reference yields no payer, so the pack answers not_checked: no card and no CRD system action. Even the repository's own US Core fixture (identifier value 'acme-health') is not recognised; only the exact value 'acme' is. With several active coverages the first in the Bundle wins; Coverage.order is not read.

**Evidence.**

- packs/prior-auth-preflight/fhir/mapping.yaml:20-22 - coverage.payer: Coverage.payor[0].identifier.value; comment 'The synthetic payers are identified by their payor identifier value'
- packs/prior-auth-preflight/logic/structured.yaml:15-19 - payer: coverage.payer in [acme] -> acme, in [beacon] -> beacon, default other
- $ probe4.py (verifier; POST /cds-services/mendari.prior-auth-preflight with tests/fixtures/us-core/prior-auth.json) payor identifier 'acme-health' (fixture as is) -> not_checked, cards [], 0 systemActions; identifier 'acme' -> needs_attention, 1 card, 1 systemAction; payor by reference only -> not_checked, cards [], 0 systemActions
- tests/test_prior_auth_pack.py:142 - tests pass the bare label as payor identifier value
- src/mendari/standards/davinci.py:30-38 - coverage_reference takes the first Coverage and uses only its id
- packs/prior-auth-preflight/pack.yaml:294 - prefetch: Coverage?patient=...&status=active; no Organization read

**Recommendation.** Resolve Coverage.payor[].reference (contained, prefetched or fetched Organization) and map the Organization's identifier, by system, to the pack's payer labels through a site-supplied table held outside the pack; choose the primary coverage by Coverage.order; fall back to not_checked with an explicit reason. The real payer identifiers are vendor and site data (owner-dependent).

### A12.3f: Contradicts the plan (verified); severity high; stage 6; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** A failed fetch degrades to ABSTAIN with a reason instead of failing the hook (p21 item 3)

**Current state.** Any failed prefetch read fails the whole hook with HTTP 422 and no decision is recorded: the fetch has no error handling (cds_hooks.py:146-147: 'with FhirClient(str(server), token=token) as client: return {key: client.read(query) ...}') and FhirError maps to 422. Measured for an EHR 500, an EHR 403 on one resource type and a timeout. The SMART launch path does the same (a test asserts 422 for an EHR 404), except a 401, which ends the launch. Two adjacent paths the plan does not name also defeat 'no failed hook': the structural R4 gate rejects the whole hook with 400 when any one prefetched resource has an unknown element or an empty string, and a search with more than 11 pages is silently truncated, so the pack decides on a partial record.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/standards/cds_hooks.py:93-96 and :131-147 - fetch raises FhirError; invoke does not catch it
- src/mendari/server/app.py:125 - FhirError -> 422; :124 - FhirStructureError -> 400
- $ probe.py (re-run) fetch with Observation -> 500: HTTP 422 'the server answered HTTP 500', decisions recorded 0; DocumentReference -> 403: 422, 0 decisions; DiagnosticReport -> timeout: 422 'could not reach the server (ConnectTimeout)', 0 decisions; all reads ok: 200, 1 decision
- tests/test_fhir_client.py:283-297 (a server off the allow-list -> 422) and :300-307 (no fhirServer and no prefetch -> 422); no test covers an EHR error during the fetch
- src/mendari/server/smart_routes.py:446-451 - decide_for: fhir.read errors propagate; tests/test_smart_sealing.py:258-263 asserts 422 for an EHR 404
- $ probe3.py (verifier) POST hook where one prefetched Observation has an unknown element -> HTTP 400 FhirStructureError; one with an empty string -> HTTP 400; no decision recorded for either
- src/mendari/standards/fhir_client.py:214-221 - next links followed MAX_PAGES (10) times, then the Bundle is returned with no marker; $ probe3.py -> 11 pages requested, 11 entries returned, no truncation marker

**Recommendation.** Catch per-key fetch failures in cds_hooks.invoke (and in smart_routes.decide_for) and record an ABSTAIN decision whose reason names the prefetch key and a fixed failure code (never the EHR's body); answer 200, and show a card only where silence could be misread (order hooks). Keep 4xx for requests Mendari must refuse (wrong hook, bad ids, a server off the allow-list). Never decide on a partial record: treat a truncated search and a resource the structural gate rejects the same way (abstain with a reason naming the resource type, rather than a 400 for the whole hook). Add a test for an EHR error during the fetch and change tests/test_fhir_client.py:300-307 deliberately.

### A12.4: Missing (verified); severity medium; stage 6; effort L (1-2 weeks); owner only

**Plan says.** Vendor fit: refresh tokens or iframe mode as the vendor requires (p21 item 4)

**Current state.** Both are deliberately refused today and deferred until the pilot EHR is known. offline_access in the configured scopes refuses every launch, and a refresh token sent unasked is dropped. Every response forbids framing (X-Frame-Options: DENY, CSP frame-ancestors 'none') and the launch cookies are SameSite=Lax, so an iframe launch cannot hold a session.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/standards/smart.py:161-166 - offline_access raises SmartError(reason='configuration')
- tests/test_smart_sealing.py:301-320 (offline_access refused) and :85-104 (a refresh_token sent unasked is not kept); both ran green
- src/mendari/server/app.py:1934 - 'X-Frame-Options': 'DENY'; :1967 - frame-ancestors 'none'
- src/mendari/server/sessions.py:134-147 - cookies HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax
- docs/decisions/ADR-0006-an-ehr-launch-is-a-principal.md:52-55 - 'No refresh, no iframe for now ... Both wait for the pilot EHR'

**Recommendation.** Blocked on the owner's vendor choice; the build itself is engineering work. Once the vendor is known: for short-lived tokens add refresh (online_access first; a sealed refresh token in the session row, rotation, revocation on logout) under an ADR that supersedes ADR-0006's refusal; for a vendor that embeds in an iframe add a per-registration frame-ancestors allow-list for the launch pages only and a partitioned SameSite=None cookie for the launch session, keeping DENY everywhere else.

### A12.ctx-jwt-today: Missing (verified); severity blocker; stage 6; effort L (1-2 weeks)

**Plan says.** Context asked of this audit: what happens today when a CDS request arrives with a JWT (p3 'Trust for EHR-signed CDS Hooks tokens')

**Current state.** The same gap as A12.1a and A12.1e, described by behaviour; not an additional blocker. Sign-in on: the JWT is rejected without being parsed (401 invalid_token; logged unknown_prefix for a short token and malformed for one of real size, over 512 characters), for discovery and for the hook, so an EHR cannot connect. Open mode: the Authorization header is ignored and the request is served as an unauthenticated admin; a forged token is as good as a real one. A browser-origin call without an Authorization header is refused 403 in both modes.

**Evidence.**

- $ probe.py (re-run) open mode: POST hook with a forged JWT -> 200 with a card; sign-in on: GET discovery and POST hook with the JWT -> 401 'the credential is not valid'
- $ probe4.py (verifier) RS384-sized JWT -> 401, security log reason malformed
- src/mendari/server/auth.py:462-466 and :577-599 - open mode returns OPEN before reading headers; a credential over 512 characters or with an unknown prefix is refused
- src/mendari/server/origin.py:65-84 - open mode checks every request's origin; a foreign Origin -> 403

**Recommendation.** Covered by A12.1a-e. Until then, document that CDS Hooks works only with a Mendari API key (sign-in on) or unauthenticated (open mode) and must not face a real EHR.

### A12.ctx-prefetch: Partial (verified); severity medium; stage 6; effort S (<1 day)

**Plan says.** Context asked of this audit: prefetch templates

**Current state.** The mechanism works and is tested: each hook pack declares prefetch templates, discovery publishes them, and a key the EHR leaves out is fetched from fhirServer with the template, every {{context.x}} token restricted to a FHIR id and URL-quoted. The templates themselves are not pilot-ready. The trial pack's Observation template asks for LOINC 4548-4, 33914-3 and 62238-1 but its own criteria also accept eGFR 98979-8 (CKD-EPI 2021), so that result is never requested when Mendari fetches (always, on the SMART launch path). Templates name MedicationStatement and bare codes without a system. Only {{context.x}} tokens are supported (a specification token such as {{userPractitionerId}} cannot be filled). A search longer than 11 pages is truncated without a marker. No test asserts what discovery publishes as prefetch.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/standards/cds_hooks.py:35-36 and :150-163 - _TOKEN, _ID, fill_template; :93-96 - missing keys fetched; :55 - discovery publishes hooks.prefetch
- tests/test_fhir_client.py:249-266 (fetches exactly the four templated queries with the token) and :310-315 (only a FHIR id fills a template); ran green
- packs/clinical-trial-prescreener/pack.yaml:338 - observations: Observation?patient=...&code=4548-4,33914-3,62238-1; packs/clinical-trial-prescreener/logic/criteria.yaml:38-41 - egfr_30_or_more codes ['33914-3', '62238-1', '98979-8']
- src/mendari/server/smart_routes.py:443-451 - the SMART launch reads the record through the same templates
- src/mendari/standards/fhir_client.py:214-221 - at most 10 next links, then returned as if complete; $ probe3.py -> 11 pages requested, no truncation marker
- tests/test_fhir.py:119-122 - the discovery test asserts id and hook only

**Recommendation.** Add 98979-8 to the trial pack's Observation template (digest change: rebuild the pack) and add a pack check that every code a criteria check accepts is requested by the prefetch template. When fitting to the vendor: replace MedicationStatement, add system|code tokens to code searches, check each template against the vendor's supported search parameters, and make a truncated search a recorded reason.

### A12.ctx-fhirAuthorization: Partial (verified); severity medium; stage 6; effort S (<1 day)

**Current state.** The access_token is used as a Bearer token for reads from fhirServer, only when that server's origin is on the deployment allow-list; a non-Bearer token_type is refused; the token never appears in errors. Not checked: expires_in, scope (whether it covers the templates), subject, and whether fhirServer belongs to the caller (there is no caller-to-EHR binding, so any caller allowed to decide can name any allow-listed server).

**Recommendation.** With the CDS registration of A12.1a, require fhirServer to be one of the calling EHR's registered bases, and abstain with a reason when the token's scope lacks a resource type a template needs.

### A12.ctx-hooks: Partial (verified); severity medium; stage 6; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** Context asked of this audit: hook types supported

**Current state.** A service answers exactly the one hook its pack declares (any string). order-select and order-sign get one decision per draft order the pack is about (at most 50, each counted against the rate limit); every other hook is one decision from prefetch. Shipped: patient-view (trial), order-sign (referral, prior auth), and a non-standard mendari-message-received (inbox). hookInstance is never read or validated (a request without it gets 200); order-select's `selections` is not read, so every draft order would be re-decided on each selection; a wrong hook is a 422.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/standards/cds_hooks.py:31-34 and :79-92 - ORDER_HOOKS, MAX_ORDERS, hook equality check
- src/mendari/core/spec.py:457-458 - hook: str (unconstrained)
- $ probe.py (re-run) hooks offered (4 services); 'service expects hook order-sign, got patient-view' -> 422
- $ probe3.py (verifier) POST hook without hookInstance -> 200; $ git grep -n -E 'hookInstance|selections' -- src -> no CDS match

**Recommendation.** Validate the request envelope (hook, hookInstance as a UUID, the context fields each hook requires) with 400s, decide only the selected orders on order-select, and decide how the inbox pack reaches a real EHR (no vendor fires mendari-message-received): SMART launch, a polling worker, or a vendor messaging API.

**Unit notes.** Skeptic pass over unit A12 at commit e55ed48c (branch audit/vision-2026-10), read-only. `git status --short` printed nothing at the end; nothing was created in the worktree. My scripts (the auditor's probe.py and probe2.py copied and re-run, plus my own probe3.py, probe4.py, probe5.py), their SQLite files and pytest temp dirs are under scratchpad/tmp/A12-skeptic/. No network, docker or installs. Verdict on the auditor's work: the headline stands. Every measurement was reproduced, and no status had to be upgraded: A12 is essentially unbuilt and no A12 code has landed since the plan was written. Of the 27 plan items here (26 from the auditor, one split): 0 Done, 4 Partial (1e, 2c, 2e, 5d), 20 Missing, 1 Contradicts (3f), 2 Unknown (goal, acc-3). Four context items answer the audit's specific questions; one of them (prefetch) I downgraded from Done to Partial. What I changed that matters to the owner: (1) The mapping gaps fail in the unsafe direction too, which the auditor had not shown: through the real CDS route, a patient on current insulin recorded as a MedicationRequest, and a patient with an MI 20 days ago whose Condition lists a local code before ICD-10, each still get a 'Possible GLYCEMIA-2 candidate' card. All stay HUMAN_REVIEW (risk level 2), but the card is wrong. (2) A real EHR JWT is refused even earlier than reported: bearer credentials are capped at 512 characters, so a real signed token is 'malformed'; the existing private_key_jwt verifier cannot be reused as written. (3) 'No failed hook' has two more enemies than a failed fetch: one resource with an unknown element or an empty string anywhere in the chart fails the whole hook with 400, and a search longer than 11 pages is silently truncated. (4) The prior-auth pack does not recognise the payer even in the repository's own US Core fixture; it answers not_checked silently. (5) The trial pack's prefetch template omits an eGFR code its own criteria accept. Blockers for stage 6, in build order: A12.1a/1b (JWT trust and the CDS principal), A12.3a/3b/3d (linked notes, code systems, MedicationRequest), then the acceptance jobs. Everything in A12.1, A12.2, the generic halves of A12.3 and A12.5a-d can be built and tested now against locally generated keys and the docker sandbox. Owner-dependent: the vendor choice and sandbox credentials (A12.goal, A12.4, A12.acc-3, the vendor-specific halves of A12.3 and A12.5e), clinician sign-off on card wording and on the MedicationRequest derivation, and the EHR scorecard itself, which is not in the repository. By the per-item estimates the unit is roughly 10 to 20 engineer-weeks, above the plan's 4-7. Caveats: statements about what the CDS Hooks specification requires (selectionBehavior, JWT claims), which suites current Inferno kits contain, and how specific vendors shape data or scopes are from general knowledge and could not be checked offline; they are marked where used. How often a real vendor's data trips the structural gate or the page limit is unknown until the vendor's sandbox is available. Targeted tests re-run (all green): tests/test_server.py::test_cds_hooks_endpoints, tests/test_fhir_client.py, tests/test_order_sign.py, tests/test_smart.py, tests/test_smart_launch.py, tests/test_scopes.py (170 passed, -k 'not postgres'); plus tests/test_auth.py::test_a_scoped_key_reaches_only_what_its_scopes_name, three tests in tests/test_smart_sealing.py, two CDS tests in tests/test_fhir.py and tests/test_capability.py (21 passed). In flight, not audited (from git log --oneline HEAD..<branch>): claude/community-packs is 8 commits ahead and claude/inbox-automation-gate is 5 commits ahead; a file-level stat shows the first touches standards/cds_hooks.py and server/smart_routes.py and the second touches packs/referral-router/pack.yaml and packs/patient-inbox-router/pack.yaml, so an A12 build session must rebase on both. feat/dashboard-tables (1 ahead) and claude/design-c (3 ahead) show no overlap with this unit's core files. ## A13. Operations for a public service

### A13.1: Missing (verified); severity blocker; stage 5; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** A public status page with uptime checks on the API, sign-in, decide, the registry and the Hub (p.22, item 1; 'status page live' in the gate before stage 5, p.4).

**Current state.** No status page, status-page config or synthetic check exists anywhere in the tree. The only engine probe target is GET /api/health. With sign-in on, its anonymous answer is three static fields returned before any store call, so an uptime check on it stays green through a database outage (reproduced: 200 'ok' while a keyed health call and a decide returned 500). In open mode the same route does read the store. The registry has /v1/health, which reads its store. The Hub (Next.js) has no health route, but every Hub page reads the registry at request time. Sign-in is an OIDC redirect and decide needs a credential and appends a chained decision, so neither can be checked by a plain URL ping; no synthetic-check key, organization or dry-run exists. A check that only looks for a 3xx from /auth/login is not enough either: on a host other than MENDARI_PUBLIC_URL it still answered 302 during the simulated outage. The registry and Hub are not deployed publicly yet (A10), and the status-page provider is an owner choice (Part B p.13).

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/server/app.py:577-580 - the anonymous answer {status, version, sign_in} is built and returned before any store call (docstring line 570: 'no database work either')
- tests/test_public_surface.py::test_anonymous_health_is_three_fields_and_no_database_work - pins that design; passed in my run
- $ python tmp/A13-skeptic/p1/probe.py (sign-in on, SQLite file replaced by garbage) -> 'outage: signed-out /api/health -> 200 {status: ok, version: 0.1.0, sign_in: True}'; 'with a key /api/health -> 500 InternalError'; 'decide with a key -> 500 InternalError'; 'GET /auth/login -> 302' (the hop to MENDARI_PUBLIC_URL)
- src/mendari/hub/registry.py:517-524 - registry GET /v1/health returns status, version, storage and len(store.latest()) (a store read)
- $ git ls-files hub -> app/page.tsx, app/packs/[namespace]/[name]/page.tsx, app/publishers/[namespace]/page.tsx, app/error.tsx, app/not-found.tsx, lib/registry.ts: no health or status route
- $ git grep -n -i -I -E 'status ?page|statuspage|uptime|synthetic check|healthz|readyz' (tree, minus lockfiles and vendored bundles) -> no status-page match; only the Kubernetes probes
- vercel.json:1-13 - only git.deploymentEnabled and functions (maxDuration 300); no crons and no status config
- deploy/kubernetes/mendari.yaml:65-70 and Dockerfile:47-48 - readinessProbe, livenessProbe and HEALTHCHECK all call the same /api/health

**Recommendation.** Add a separate deep readiness route (for example GET /api/health/ready: one cheap database round trip, packs loaded, cached a few seconds, nothing secret) and leave /api/health as it is. Add synthetic checks: readiness; GET /auth/login on the public host followed to the identity provider's authorize URL (not just any 3xx); one decide with a dedicated narrow-scope key in a dedicated 'status' organization so it never touches a partner's statistics or quota; registry /v1/health; and the Hub home page (which also proves the Hub can reach the registry). Publish them through the provider the owner picks. Point the Kubernetes readinessProbe at the deep route.

### A13.2: Partial (verified); severity blocker; stage 5; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** Scheduled monitoring: run the existing monitor on a cron and post alerts to the alert webhook (p.22, item 2; 'scheduled monitoring live' in the gate before stage 5).

**Current state.** The monitor and its CLI exist and post alerts (I ran the real CLI against a seeded scratch database with a real local listener). The two self-hosted templates schedule it daily. The hosted platform has no schedule at all: vercel.json has no crons, no route runs the monitor across packs or posts alerts, and no workflow has a schedule. In both templates the monitor's exit code is discarded with '|| true'; the Kubernetes template never sets MENDARI_ALERT_WEBHOOK and the compose example leaves it empty, so as shipped a scheduled alert is only a line in the job's stdout (I ran the exact CronJob command line: exit 0, alert printed, nothing posted). In Kubernetes the monitor is chained after 'phi purge &&': the template sets MENDARI_RETENTION_DAYS=90 so the purge normally passes, but if a deployer removes that setting or the purge fails for any other reason, the job exits 1 and the monitor never runs (reproduced with retention unset). Without --org the monitor pools every organization's decisions per pack and the alert body carries organization: null.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/cli.py:846-879 - cmd_monitor: runs monitor() for every pack, prints alerts, posts {source, organization, alerts} to the webhook, returns 1 on any alert
- src/mendari/cli.py:1339-1349 - 'monitor' arguments: --db, --pack, --days, --org, --webhook
- $ mendari monitor --db seeded.db --pack mendari/patient-inbox-router --webhook http://127.0.0.1:<port>/hook (scratch, 25 seeded re-routed decisions) -> exit=1; '[high] accuracy: observed accuracy 0.0% over the last 7 days, below the benchmark's 99.3% by more than 3%'; the local listener received {source: mendari, organization: null, alerts: [...]}
- $ the exact CronJob command line from deploy/kubernetes/mendari.yaml:109, DATABASE_URL pointed at the seeded scratch database, MENDARI_RETENTION_DAYS=90, no webhook -> exit=0; stdout holds the '[high] accuracy' line; 0 posts reached the listener
- $ the same command line with MENDARI_RETENTION_DAYS unset -> exit=1; stderr 'error: give --days or set MENDARI_RETENTION_DAYS'; the monitor did not run
- deploy/kubernetes/mendari.yaml:88-112 - CronJob 'mendari-daily' at 15 3 * * *; line 109: mendari phi purge ... && (mendari monitor ... || true); line 28: MENDARI_RETENTION_DAYS: "90"
- $ grep -c MENDARI_ALERT_WEBHOOK deploy/kubernetes/mendari.yaml -> 0 (not in the ConfigMap, lines 19-38, nor in the secret example, lines 5-9)
- deploy/onprem/docker-compose.yml:35-52 - 'jobs' service loops: phi purge; monitor || true; sleep 86400
- deploy/onprem/.env.example:37-38 - '# Optional' MENDARI_ALERT_WEBHOOK= (empty)
- vercel.json:1-13 - no 'crons' key; $ grep -n 'schedule|cron' .github/workflows/*.yml -> no matches
- src/mendari/server/app.py:772-779 - the only monitoring route is GET /api/monitoring?pack_id= for one pack and the caller's organization; it posts nothing
- tests/test_monitoring.py::test_the_cli_exits_1_on_alerts_and_posts_them (httpx.post stubbed) and ::test_the_cli_watches_one_organization - passed in my run
- tests/test_deploy.py:37-52 (::test_the_templates_parse_and_hold_no_secrets) - checks only that the templates parse, their kinds and that they hold no secrets; nothing runs the scheduled command

**Recommendation.** For the hosted site add a scheduled trigger. A5 item 2 (p.10) already asks for a Vercel cron for the retention purge: build one guarded cron route there (GET, CRON_SECRET bearer, constant-time compare) and have it also run the monitor per organization and post alerts, or use a scheduled GitHub Actions job with the database URL in a protected environment. Loop per organization so the alert names it. In the templates: add MENDARI_ALERT_WEBHOOK to the Kubernetes secret example, replace '&&' with ';', and stop discarding the result (a distinct exit code for 'alert delivery failed'). Fix the alert logic first (plan_defects 1) or the cron will page on healthy packs and stay silent in an outage.

### A13.3a: Missing (verified); severity blocker; stage 5; effort S (<1 day)

### A13.3b: Missing (verified); severity blocker; stage 5; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** How to disable automation for one pack or every pack: a single kill switch that forces HUMAN_REVIEW, added if it doesn't exist (p.22, item 3).

**Current state.** No kill switch exists, per pack or global: no setting, table, route, CLI command or policy input. apply_policy takes only the manifest, answers, failures, a governance override and provider variants. Four existing levers come near and none is the switch: (1) revoking a governance approval stops AUTO only for risk level 2-3 packs, per organization; the inbox router is level 0 and automates with no approval to revoke. (2) MENDARI_PACKS stops serving a pack (404, integrations break, nothing reaches the review queue) and needs a restart or redeploy. (3) MENDARI_ORG_DAILY_LIMITS=decisions=0 stops all automation for every pack and organization, but as ABSTAIN with no recommendation, and it also silences the pack's local emergency rule (A13.also-4). (4) For the three packs that set automation_requires (referral router, prior auth, AI guard), MENDARI_PROVIDERS can pin the slot to its rules-only variant, which caps AUTO to HUMAN_REVIEW and keeps rules and priorities; it is per pack, deployment-wide, needs a restart or redeploy, and does not exist for the inbox router at this commit. All AUTO outcomes pass one choke point (policy._cap, reached only from Decision.decide), so a switch there would cover REST, FHIR $decide, CDS Hooks, SMART, PAS and the AI guard.

- src/mendari/server/security_log.py:64-81 - the FIELDS allow-list
- docs/deploying-with-phi.md:512-514 - Vercel keeps stdout 'an hour on Hobby, a day on Pro'; 'add one [drain] when the first outside developer gets a key' (a lead)
- tests/test_security_log.py - the whole file passed in my run
- tasks/todo.md:383 - 'Deferred: ... database tables for security events' (a lead)

**Recommendation.** Owner: add a log drain with at least 30 days' retention before the first partner signs in to the hosted site, and write where the logs live in the runbook. Build: an alert rule on error.unhandled and on quota.reached or ratelimit.hit bursts at the drain, or a small counter the scheduled monitor reads.

### A13.also-7: Missing (verified); severity high; stage 5; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** Backup and restore of the audit chain (an incident runbook must cover restoring the hosted service; p.22 goal and item 3).

**Current state.** There is no backup or restore procedure, script or test; the threat model leaves backups to 'the site', and for the project's own hosted site nothing is written. The chain can be verified ('mendari audit verify', GET /api/audit/verify) and verification prints the head hash and event count, but nothing records that head anywhere outside the database and the command takes no expected head, so a restore that silently lost the newest events still verifies. Reproduced: a copy taken after 10 decisions verified ok after the live database had 15.

**Evidence.**

- $ git grep -n -i -I -E 'backup|restore|pg_dump|point-in-time|checkpoint' -- src docs deploy README.md scripts SECURITY.md tests -> only statements that backups may still hold erased notes or sealed rows; no procedure
- docs/security/threat-model.md:93-95 - 'The deployment is the site's. TLS termination, network placement, backups ...' (a lead)
- src/mendari/core/audit.py:1816-1841 - verify() walks from GENESIS and returns {ok, events, head}; no comparison with a stored checkpoint
- $ python tmp/A13-skeptic/p2/probe.py -> 'live after 10: True 10 d92b55c0 | live after 15: True 15 9e36e736'; 'mendari audit verify --db backup.db' exit=0 {ok: true, events: 10, head: d92b55c0...}
- $ mendari audit verify --help -> options: --db, --notes only
- src/mendari/cli.py:1097-1118 - audit subcommands: verify and export (FHIR NDJSON) only

**Recommendation.** Have the daily job record a checkpoint (event count, head hash, time) outside the database: in the webhook post and the log, and ideally published (see opportunities). Add 'mendari audit verify --expect-head <hash> --min-events <n>' and a restore drill to the runbook: restore the database provider's point-in-time copy to a scratch database, verify against the last checkpoint, state the recovery point and what is lost. Add a test for the stale-restore case.

### A13.also-8: Partial (verified); severity medium; stage 5; effort S (<1 day)

**Plan says.** What breaks if the alert webhook is down (scheduled alerts must reach someone; p.22 item 2).

**Current state.** Nothing user-facing breaks, by design and by test: a quota alert that cannot be delivered logs a warning and the decision proceeds. But the alert is lost: the quota alert fires only on the one call that reaches the limit, so it is never retried that day (the quota.reached log line remains), and that request can wait up to 5 s on the webhook. The monitor CLI reports 'the alert webhook failed (ConnectError)' on stderr with exit 1, the same code as 'alerts found', and both templates swallow it with '|| true'. Only the webhook's URL form is checked at startup, and only when quotas are set; reachability never is. There is no retry, queue, second channel or heartbeat, so a dead webhook is indistinguishable from 'no alerts'.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/server/app.py:1679-1682 - httpx.post(webhook, timeout=5) in the request path; on failure only quota_logger.warning
- src/mendari/core/decision.py:173-174 - the alert fires only when count == limit
- tests/test_limits.py::test_a_quota_alert_that_fails_never_fails_the_decision - passed in my run
- $ python tmp/A13-skeptic/p2/probe.py, A6 webhook down -> exit=1; stdout has the alert; stderr 'error: the alert webhook failed (ConnectError)'
- src/mendari/cli.py:875-879 - a webhook failure raises MendariError; alerts also return 1
- src/mendari/server/app.py:331-333 - check_webhook only 'if org_limits and webhook'; src/mendari/evals/monitoring.py:65-74 checks scheme and credentials only

**Recommendation.** Give delivery failure its own exit code and stop discarding it in the templates; retry with backoff in the CLI; move the quota alert out of the request path (record it, let the scheduled job deliver and re-deliver); send a daily 'monitor ran, N packs, 0 alerts, chain head ...' heartbeat so silence means broken.

### A13.also-9: Partial (verified); severity high; stage 5; effort M (1-3 days)

**Plan says.** Limits must hold when strangers share the hosted platform (p.22 goal; per-organization quotas referenced in A6 item 5, p.15).

**Current state.** Per-organization quotas cover decisions and the remote calls decisions make. Evaluations are deliberately charged to the deployment-wide daily budgets only and to no organization. An evaluation may run up to 200 remote-provider cases, the request may choose the provider variant, and each admin may start 6 an hour, so once organizations are self-service one organization's admin can use up the whole deployment's daily Jev or LLM budget (at the planned ceilings of 2,000 and 200, one evaluation exhausts the LLM budget), after which every other organization's remote-provider decisions fall back to review until midnight. No alert or log event marks the deployment budget being exhausted.

**Evidence.**

- src/mendari/server/app.py:868-873 - 'Provider calls count against the daily budgets, never an organization's quotas'; the request's providers override the deployed ones (line 871)
- src/mendari/core/decision.py:162-165 - for_evaluation() returns CallBudget(self.store, self.limits) without organization limits
- src/mendari/server/app.py:259-260 - REMOTE_EVAL_LIMIT = 200, REMOTE_EVAL_WORKERS = 8
- src/mendari/server/limits.py:100 - 'evaluate': Rate(6, 3600, 6), keyed per principal (limits.py:265); src/mendari/server/auth.py:97-108 - only the admin role holds 'evaluate'
- tests/test_limits.py::test_each_organization_has_its_own_quota_and_evaluations_spend_none[sqlite] - passed in my run: the behaviour is intended and pinned
- src/mendari/core/audit.py:636-637 - budget_exhausted is raised with no alert or security-log event

**Recommendation.** Before self-service: give evaluations their own per-organization daily quota (for example evals and eval_remote_calls metrics), reserve a share of the deployment budget for decisions, and alert when a deployment budget passes 80% and when it is exhausted. Update the pinned test deliberately.

**Unit notes.** Scope and method: audited commit e55ed48c only, read-only, as the skeptic for unit A13. I re-opened every cited file for the Done, blocker and high items and re-ran every measurement with my own scripts; the auditor's findings held up well and the statuses did not change. The changes are one item split, two severity or stage corrections, two factual corrections (A13.2 purge chaining, A13.5 attribution of guard and evaluation spend), one missed lever (A13.3b) and sharper plan defects. Bottom line: nothing in A13 is finished for the hosted platform. Of the plan's five items and three acceptance criteria none is Done; three are Partial because self-hosted pieces exist (the monitor CLI and template crons; the firewall rule file in log mode; key revocation without an operator path). The strongest existing foundations are the database-backed rate limits and quotas, the fail-closed budget paths and the security log. The gate before stage 5 says 'A13 done' and also names the status page, scheduled monitoring, incident runbook and firewall enforcement; those four and the kill switch are rated blocker, the other A13 items high or medium. What I ran (all under scratchpad/tmp/A13-skeptic/, synthetic data, 60 s timeouts, nothing contacted but 127.0.0.1): - p1/probe.py: defaults of the daily limits; default vs decisions=0 quota vs MENDARI_PACKS (no kill switch; the emergency case over quota); public health, keyed health, decide and /auth/login during a simulated database outage. - p2/probe.py: the real 'mendari monitor' CLI on a seeded degradation with a real local listener (webhook up, down, other organization); the exact Kubernetes CronJob command line with and without MENDARI_RETENTION_DAYS; a healthy week, a better-than-benchmark week and an all-failing week through monitor(); 'audit verify' on a stale copy. - Targeted tests, all passed: tests/test_monitoring.py, tests/test_deploy.py, tests/test_security_log.py, tests/test_limits.py and selected tests from test_public_surface, test_any_of, test_audit, test_api_keys and test_auth (pytest run from the scratch directory with --basetemp there, -p no:cacheprovider, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1). Postgres-parametrised variants were skipped (no test database configured). I did not run tests/test_vercel.py. Pinned tests a future A13 build must change deliberately (carried over from the auditor, each confirmed to exist): - tests/test_limits.py::test_the_firewall_rule_starts_in_log_mode_on_signed_out_routes_only asserts rateLimit.action == 'log'. - tests/test_public_surface.py::test_anonymous_health_is_three_fields_and_no_database_work pins the static public health: a status probe must be a new route. - tests/test_deploy.py::test_the_templates_parse_and_hold_no_secrets pins the manifest kinds and compose services; ::test_every_setting_the_templates_use_is_documented requires any new MENDARI_* setting used in deploy/ to appear in docs/deploying-with-phi.md or README.md. - tests/test_limits.py::test_each_organization_has_its_own_quota_and_evaluations_spend_none pins that evaluations spend no organization quota. - tests/test_limits.py::test_over_its_quota_a_decision_falls_back_to_human_review_with_one_alert accepts HUMAN_REVIEW or ABSTAIN; tighten it once local providers run over quota. - tests/test_limits.py::test_costly_routes_have_their_class_reads_none_and_one_call_of_each_passes walks every route: new routes (readiness, usage, hold, cron) need a class or an explicit 'none'. - tests/test_threat_model.py keeps docs/security/threat-model.md true to the code: new controls need rows naming real tests. - Harness note: tests/test_vercel.py imports mendari.server.vercel, which opens var/mendari.db relative to the working directory; run it from a scratch working directory. Not determinable from the repository (Unknown): the hosted site's actual limit values, whether the firewall rule has been applied or its log-only week started, whether a log drain exists, the hosted database's backup settings. I made no calls to Vercel or any hosted service. A small plan-versus-repository difference outside this unit: the plan (p.13) has the owner commit to answering security reports within 5 business days, while SECURITY.md:17 already says 3 working days. In flight, not audited (from git log --oneline HEAD..<branch> only): claude/community-packs has 6a2e3b71 'origin-aware loading, recommend-only policy and named-only spend (B1, B2)', which by its subject adds a recommend-only cap for community packs and may be the natural place to hang the automation hold; claude/inbox-automation-gate has 899cd468 'Inbox automation gate ...'
